## 2026-10-10 P1-A4: how `released` is decided (lib/pages/released.ts)
Decision: one module, pure functions over plain lists plus build-time wrappers. A module or page is released when its file exists and its frontmatter says `released: true` (read from the raw MDX with `import.meta.glob(..., { query: '?raw', eager: true })` and `parseFrontmatter` of `@astrojs/markdown-remark`, so it is synchronous and usable in MDX). A tool is released when `site/src/tools/registry/T{nn}.ts` exists and its raw text does not say `released: false`. An Atlas page is released when `src/pages/atlas/[board].astro` exists. `sources` always; `open-items` only when `isReleaseBuild()` is false. `hrefFor(target)` and `linkIfReleased(target)` join `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` and the route with exactly one slash; targets: `{kind:'module', slug}` or `{kind:'module', number}`, `{kind:'page', slug}`, `{kind:'tool', id, query?}`, `{kind:'atlas', board}`, `{kind:'static', name: 'index'|'modules'|'sources'|'open-items'}`. `nextModule(n)` is module n + 1 only, never a later one.
MDX pattern for released-aware prose links (P1-A8 asked for it):
```
import { linkIfReleased } from '@lib/pages/released';
export const m = (n) => linkIfReleased({ kind: 'module', number: n });
{m(1) ? <a href={m(1)}>the mutation game</a> : <>the mutation game</>}
```
about.mdx uses exactly this for the seven statements, mapped (plan, [D]) 1 to M7, 2 to M1, 3 to M4, 4 to M5, 5 to M3, 6 to M8, 7 to M9.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A5: mode text, game over, refusals and the linked sentences
Decision: `data-out="mode"` reads `free play`, `legal play` or `raising moves`. In legal mode `data-out="gameOver"` reads `Game over after N moves.` (`1 move` in the singular, as P0-A5's template) when no number is positive, and is an empty reserved line otherwise. A move that ends a legal game appends `Game over after N moves.` to its announcement; a play to the end is one sentence (`Played N moves to the end. ...`, populations named for a raising play) and does not append it. A refused action in raising mode: `City 2 cannot be raised: its number is 1.` (plan; SPEC has no template). Linked view above four nodes: `Mutated city 2 and fired node 2. City 2 now 1; node 1 now 1, node 2 now 1, node 3 now minus 1. Move 1.` (plan). Undo in the linked view: `Undid move 4. Populations now ...; numbers now ....` (plan). A play stopped by its cap: `Still running after 20000 moves. Numbers now ...` in the live region and `still running after 20000 moves` in `data-out="limit"`; the words "not of finite type" never appear. Reason: A-4, 4.0 Stated limits.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A5: step, play to the end, the worker
Decision: Step and Play to the end appear in legal and raising modes only. Step makes the move at the lowest allowed position; play to the end calls `play` (legal; and raising from a numbers start, on -a, which makes the same moves because firing is linear) or `raisingPlay` (raising from a population), with no `choose` and the cap `CAPS.playMoves`, appends the word and keeps every position. `whereToRun({ board, kind: 'play', finiteKnown: isNamedFinite(board) })` is asked before each play; custom boards go to the worker through `engineCall`, named finite boards run on the main thread. "play on" and `playFate` are phase 2: on a custom board the control stays "Play to the end" and reports the cap. A link's move list is replayed on the main thread when the tool loads it, as `decodeState` itself does under P1-A2's accepted `LONG_LIST_REPLAY = 'sync'` reading (deviation from E-9 rule 2 for lists above 2000 moves, consistent with MERGE's stage 1.1 decision). Reason: 4.0, 5.6, E-9.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A5: history, the state, view and mode choosers
Decision: History.svelte is composed in the figure (after the boards, before the controls) and ToolFrame's own Undo/Redo/Reset are not used. `state.moves` holds the moves up to the cursor, so `data-moves` and the link follow undo and scrubbing; the redo tail stays in memory only. On the tool's own route (instance id empty; the `settings` property overrides) the controls row also holds the board picker and choosers for the view and the mode (`data-control="picker"`, `"view"`, `"mode"`); a view change keeps the moves (a mode the new view does not allow becomes free play); a mode change keeps the moves when `firstForbiddenMove` allows them all and otherwise restarts from the start (plan). Reason: 4.0 History; 6.6.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A5: Download data
Decision: `derived` is `{ view, mode, labels, positions }`, `positions` one entry per position of the current play up to the cursor: `{ move, populations?, numbers? }` in label order, safe integers as numbers, longer ones as decimal text, fractions as `p/q`; the linked view holds both. The state is the ToolState of the current point. Reason: 6.6 Data export (plan).

## 2026-10-10 P1-A5: properties, shapes and the predicate list
Decision: beyond the common ones: `view`, `mode`, `script: { move: label; caption }[]`, `goal` (`{ kind: 'reach', position, game?, text? }`, `{ kind: 'no-positive', text? }`, `{ kind: 'no-unhappy', text? }`, `{ kind: 'predicate', name: 'mixed-signs', giveUpAfter?, giveUpText?, text? }`), `prediction` (CONTRACTS 5.2 exactly, no field added), `hints: boolean`, `panels: ('form'|'level'|'colours'|'lengths')[]`, `roadStyle`, `rounds: number`, `settings: boolean`, `onChange({ state, populations, numbers })`. `linkTo`, `layers` and `preset` are accepted and ignored. The predicate list is `mixed-signs` (a population with a negative and a positive city; M1 beat 2). A reach goal compares values as text in label order, in the game of `coords` unless `game` says otherwise. `goalMet` shows `Goal reached.` (announced once, appended to the move's sentence); `goalNote` shows the give-up text once `giveUpAfter` moves are made and the goal is not met. Script: Next makes the next scripted move through the same path as a click; `scriptCaption` shows the caption of the next scripted move, `End of the script.` at the end, and `The script has ended: a move was made that it does not contain.` while the moves made differ from the script (undoing back onto it resumes it). A script move the mode forbids, or a view and mode outside the table, throws at build time naming the instance. `rounds`: `Round k` in `data-out="roundCounter"`, k = floor(moves made / rounds), following undo and scrubbing, not part of the state. Reason: SPEC 4 T1 Configuration; 3 M6 row 2 (plan).

## 2026-10-10 P1-A5: prediction check
Decision: `Predict.svelte` takes the `Prediction` of CONTRACTS 5.2 unchanged and checks `value` (number, position) or `correct` (choice); no `check` field was added, so there is no deviation of CONTRACTS 5.2. The engine check required by the plan is in `T01.test.ts > M0 figure configurations` (A3 from (1,1,0), city 2 gives 0). While a prediction is unanswered every node is `data-can-act="false"` and disabled, History and the step controls are disabled, and there are no hint ghosts. Without JavaScript the question is followed by `<details>` holding the answer and the reveal.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A5: hints
Decision: with `hints`, hovering or focusing a node draws below it (aria-hidden, `data-ghost`) the value it would take after acting there, from the engine (mutate or fire; both boards in the linked view), only where the mode allows, never during a prediction.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A5: panels
Decision: `panels` is accepted and filtered by `PANELS_AVAILABLE`, empty in phase 1: form value, level and long and short nodes arrive with their engine functions in phase 2 (formValue, level, symmetrizer), the colour classes in phase 3 (bipartition). No panel and no message in phase 1.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A5: linkTo and the highlight
Decision: on main P1-A2's `publishToolState` and `followToolState` (state.ts) exist, so no `t01/link.ts` was written. T1 publishes its ToolState under its instance id after every change (never positions) and follows the same id: a published state different from its own, on the same board, coords and start, is applied as a new move list from its own start (T2's jump). Highlight: hovering or focusing a node sets `{ kind: 'node', board: <name or c:matrix>, value: label }` and clears it on leaving; a `position` or `root` value equal to a board's current values (label order, same board name) marks that board (`data-highlighted`, a dashed outline).

## 2026-10-10 P1-A5: Board family extensions (deviation record: optional props only)
Decision: `Board.svelte` now lays out by `nodePositions(board, xy)` and `toPixels` (grid units = toPixels at u = 64 divided by 64; the CSS rule u = min(64, floor((W - 16)/k)) scales the box; hit side min(44, u)); a polygon or circle layout is a square box of side min(W, 360) with 44-pixel hit areas, the drawing scaled with the box, so the polygon radius is 150/360 of the side (at W = 320 the radius is 133 rather than the formula's 130; plan, recorded). W is the figure's width, which ToolFrame runs from edge to edge below 400 pixels (boardBoxWidth). New optional props: `xy`, `states`, `spoken`, `ghosts`, `disabled`, `highlighted`, `onFocusNode`; new hooks `data-sign`, `data-ring`. `Node.svelte` draws stacked fractions, shortened long numbers and the ghost; `History.svelte` gains `frozen` and the hooks `data-control="undo|redo|reset|historySlider"` and `data-step`. CONTRACTS 5.1 props unchanged; BoardSeed and P0-A5's tests unchanged and green. The Board family and T1 import the engine as `@two-games/engine` and lib by relative path (as lib/ does), because a Vite build without the site's aliases (P1-A2's toolframe-hydration fixture) reaches T1 through the registry's lazy import.

Decision: `data-instance={instanceId}` on ToolFrame's root (for P1-A4's Challenge); `released?: boolean` on `ToolRegistryEntry`; in `pages/tools/[tool].astro` the static import of T01GameBoard, its `client:idle` line and `'board'` in `HYDRATED`.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A6: hooks
Decision: `data-out`: found, total, stopMessage, verdict (phase 2), layersGrown, layerChart (bars with data-layer, data-count, data-complete), vertex (data-position, data-layer), edge (data-label, data-from, data-to, data-rise), rise, tableRow (data-position, data-layer), chartRow (data-layer, data-count; addition, so that the chart's numbers in the table view are testable), strip. `data-control`: grow, showTotal, growth, grows, positiveOnly, vertexLabels, picker, scrub (strip buttons with data-step, or the slider), jumpRow (addition: the jump button of a table row); undo, redo, reset, copyLink, downloadData from ToolFrame. data-position and data-value use the ASCII hyphen; the drawn text uses U+2212.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A6: undo, redo, reset and the strip (deviation from "History.svelte does this")
Decision: the Undo, Redo and Reset buttons are ToolFrame's (hooked `data-control`), and the strip of past positions is drawn by T2 itself (buttons `data-control="scrub"` with `data-step`, a slider with a counter above 50 positions, as 4.0 says). `History.svelte` is not used because it renders its own unhooked Undo, Redo and Reset, which would duplicate ToolFrame's row. Request to P0-A5/P1-A5: a strip-only mode of History.svelte, after which T2 can use it. The `u` and `r` shortcuts are wired through `shortcutOf` while focus is inside the board.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A6: the seed of a numbers link
Decision: a link (or property) with `coords: numbers` names a numbers position, which only `orbit` mode can grow: T2 then grows that orbit in the firing game and the `grows` control is disabled. Reason: instruction 5.2.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A6: reset
Decision: reset empties the move list, returns `explore` to the configured `grown` layers (clamped to the layers bound) and `follow` to the current position alone (the start, since the moves are emptied). Reason: plan, instruction 5.2.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A6: follow mechanics and ranking
Decision: the garden starts with the position the board stands on when follow begins; a move adds the position it reaches when new, and the edge it travelled (labelled by the node) when that edge is new; undo, redo, scrubs and revisits add no vertex. (Plan said a revisit adds nothing; a revisit by a new road adds that road's edge, since every move is an edge; no vertex either way.) Each vertex is ranked by its depth in the bounded `orbitGraph` of the followed start, computed once; a position outside it goes one rank below the position it came from. Jumps in follow take their word from that bounded graph. With `linkTo`, a change of the followed state counts as a move when `moveMade` says the new list is a prefix of the old one plus one move; anything else adds the position only. `grown` is ignored. Positive roots only is available in explore only (the switch is disabled in follow and in orbit mode).

## 2026-10-10 P1-A6: stop messages
Decision: `stopMessage(graph, maxDepth, layersBound, cap)` in `t02/limits.ts`: the two sentences of 5.5 exactly; none for a completed search; none for a pause in explore below the bound, where `layersGrown` shows "N layers grown". In follow at 2000 visited positions: "stopped after 2000 positions" without the layers clause. The message is announced when a grow press brings it.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A6: edges
Decision: every move is applied once more to every item; each involutive pair is drawn once; a move that changes nothing (a self-loop) is not drawn; two nodes joining the same two positions give two edges, the second offset by 7 pixels. Colour from `edgeColour(label)` (tokens), the label as SVG text beside the line. In the positive view on a named finite-type board a rise of 2 or 3 is drawn as 2 or 3 parallel lines; on every other board the rise is written as `+k` at 58 percent of the edge's length on the opposite side from the label (at 42 percent), on every edge, 1 included.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A6: finite test
Decision: `isNamedFinite` in `t02/garden.ts` wraps state.ts's `isNamedFinite` (named finite types; every custom board counts as not finite, 4.0, E-9 rule 2). P2-A7 switches this one function to `classify`'s verdict. The layers bound is the `layers` property, else 40 off the finite types and none on a named finite board.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A6: counter without a total
Decision: when there is no total the counter shows `no total on this board`. An orbit search that stopped at the layers bound below 2000 positions gives no total, never "more than 2000" (a reading of SPEC 4 T2 Interactions: the SPEC names only the complete case and the 2000 case). The positive view does not change the counter. `totalOf` is the one function phase 3 changes for `orbitSize`.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A6: highlight
Decision: on hover or focus of a vertex the highlight atom gets `{ kind: 'root' | 'position', board: name or the codec's c: text, value: entries in label order }`; cleared on leave or blur; skipped (null) when an entry is not a safe integer. T2 does not mark vertices highlighted by other tools (optional).

## 2026-10-10 P1-A6: vertex keyboard model, elements, names
Decision: vertices are real `<button>` elements over the SVG of edges, in a group named "Garden of N positions", one in the tab order (roving tabindex). Left and Right move within a layer in drawn order, Up and Down to the nearest vertex (by x) of the nearest occupied layer, Home and End to the first and last in items order, Enter or Space jumps, the focused vertex is scrolled into view. Names: `Root population 1, minus 1, 0, layer 2` (orbit mode: `Position ...`; positive view: `total` instead of `layer`). Labelled vertices are at least 44 by 44 pixels, dots 24 by 24, spaced so none overlap; the box scrolls (A-7, A-11).

## 2026-10-10 P1-A6: announcements
Decision: moves on T2's board use `moveAnnouncement` and `announceTemplates.undid` unchanged. Others (plan): `Layer 3 grown: 3 new, 12 found so far.` (followed by the stop message as a sentence when one appears), `Total: 12.`, `Jumped to root population 1, 1, 0 by 2 moves.`, `Reset. The garden holds 3 positions.`, `Board D4. ...`, `Follow mode: ...`, `Explore mode: ...`.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A6: linkTo
Decision: no new mechanism: T2 uses P1-A2's `followToolState(linkTo, onChange)` from state.ts. It mirrors the followed state (board, coords, start, moves) as its own and shows no board of its own. A jump publishes `{ ...followedState, moves: word }` under the T1's id with `publishToolState`, the word being a shortest one from the T1's own start (`wordFromStart`). In orbit mode the seed is the followed start (the orbit of the current position is the same set). Decision: T9 composes ToolFrame (P1-A2), Board, History and Predict (P0-A5, P1-A5) and drives them with T1's own model, `T1Game` of `t01/model.ts`, configured with view `populations`, mode `raising`, coords `populations`; it also reuses T1's announcement helpers (`t01/announce.ts`) and long-number helper (`t01/longNumber.ts`, through Board and the tooltip). Decision: `{ board: 'A3', coords: 'populations', start: [1, 0, 0], moves: [] }` (M1 row 3's first board); caption "Start with one Martian in city 1 of A3 and mutate only where a city rises: the game stops after 2 moves at (1, 1, 1), the highest root, whatever the order of the moves.", the numbers from `kostantPlay` at module load (test against `kostant.A3`). Decision: words `unhappy`, `happy`, `manic` (SPEC 2.16; "excited" not used). Decision: a link may carry any integer population; it is played as given ("raisingPlay starts from any population"). The end panel then names the population only when it equals `highestRoot` or `highestShortRoot`, and gives no recipe caption or return counts when it is unnamed (the recipe of 2.12 is about Kostant ends); the marked cities are still shown. A link with `c=n` is converted through `startFromLink` (`toPopulation` in Big arithmetic) when every entry is integral and written back as `c=p`; a fractional population loads the default state with the codec's `LINK_NOTICE`. A property `coords: 'numbers'` with a fractional population throws at build time naming the instance (authoring error).

## 2026-10-10 P1-A7: the refusal of other views and modes (no codec hook needed)
Decision: the codec already refuses a view and mode outside the table of T1 (rule 11: `v=n`, `m=l` with populations), a board not in the registry's list (rule 8: custom, affine), and a move the raising mode forbids (rule 6). T9 refuses in addition, after `decodeState`, a state whose view is not `populations` or whose mode is not `raising` (`v=l`, `m=f`), and a fractional numbers start, with the same `LINK_NOTICE` and the default state; the same check runs on popstate. No change to the codec was needed.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A7: announcements
Decision: a move: T1's `moveSentence` for the populations view (A-4 template; above four nodes `changedOnly` with `Mutated`/`city`). A refused city: T1's raising sentence `City 1 cannot be raised: its number is 2.`, so the site has one wording. Play to the end: `announceTemplates.playedToEnd(moves, populations, 'populations')` (P1-A2's noun extension; no request needed). When the goal becomes met, the sentence `No city is unhappy. This is the highest root.` (or `the highest short root`; `No city is unhappy.` for an unnamed end) is appended. Board and start changes: `Board D4. One Martian in city 1.`, `One Martian in city 3.`

## 2026-10-10 P1-A7: the end panel and the return counts without coroot
Decision: the end panel shows `endName` ("The game stops at the highest root, (1, 1, 1)."), `moveCount`, `hMinus2` only when `highestShortRoot` is null, `finalNumbers` (`toNumbers` of the end), `marked`, `affineCaption` and `returnCounts`. The return counts are `b = C^T beta^vee` with `beta^vee` the end itself on a simply laced board, `highestShortRoot(transposeBoard(board))` for the highest root and `highestRoot(transposeBoard(board))` for the highest short root (2.5, F11). The recipe matrix built from them equals `affine[T].cartan_node0_first` for all 125 long starts (unit test). P2-A7 may switch to `coroot`. The caption: "Join a new city to cities 1 and 3. It sends a_j roads to each marked city j (1 to city 1, 1 to city 3) and receives b_j roads back (1 from city 1, 1 from city 3). On a simply laced board the two counts are equal. The board with the new city is an affine board." No affine name in phase 1; the words "not of finite type" and "never ends" are not used.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A7: inline MathML
Decision: the `i` of the bridge sentence, `h − 2`, `a_j`, `b_j` and `j` are inline MathML written in the component (`<math><mi>i</mi></math>`, `<math><mi>h</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math>`, `<math><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></math>`), so A-12 holds without KaTeX at runtime. The bridge sentence's text content is SPEC 2.4(a)'s first sentence character for character. A comment marks that it follows P3-A5's outcome of SPEC 7.3's [U] check (fallback: HTML spans with an aria-label). Note: T1's `Bridge.svelte` writes the `i` as `<i>i</i>`, not MathML; same text content.

Decision: `playOutcome(result, cap)` gives `still running after <cap> moves` for `status: 'cap'`, shown in `data-out="limit"` with no end panel; unreachable on a named finite type (a raising play takes at most N moves: unit test on random starts from -6 to 6, the longest found above 28), tested with a cap of 5.

## 2026-10-10 P1-A7: step, play to the end, the main thread
Decision: step is `stepPosition(board, p)` = the word of `raisingPlay(board, p, undefined, 1)`, so the lowest-position rule lives in the engine; play to the end is `T1Game.playToEnd(CAPS.playMoves)` (raisingPlay, lowest position first). Both run on the main thread; T9 imports nothing from `lib/worker` (unit test reads the source).

Decision: the picker is a `<select>` (`data-control="picker"`) with one `<optgroup>` per letter A to G from `pickerGroups(boardChoices)`, plain names (an `<option>` cannot hold KaTeX markup; as P1-A5 and P1-A6 did); D19 is met since the reader's choice `B2` or `C2` is shown as chosen. Choosing a board sets one Martian in the city with the lowest label and empties the moves. The start-city chooser (`data-control="startCity"`) lists the labels and shows "other start" when the start is not one Martian. Both are shown on every instance (M1 needs the picker on a lesson page).

The words unhappy, happy, manic are credited to [Ele16].

# Decisions of P2-A1 (engine phase 2: form, classification, affine boards, fates, root test, guards)

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: versions observed
Decision: built and tested against node v22.22.0, typescript 6.0.3, vitest 5.0.3, fast-check 4.10.2, all as installed by `npm ci --prefer-offline` from the committed lockfile; the hand checks against the oracle ran under python3 3.13. What the specification left open: nothing; recorded as the instruction asks (5.17). Default used: none. Reason: the toolchain postdates training data (COMMON.md 3); `fc.shuffledSubarray`, `fc.constantFrom`, `fc.array`, `fc.tuple` and `fc.assert` with `{ seed, numRuns }` were read in `node_modules/fast-check/lib/fast-check.d.ts` before use. No dependency was added; `packages/engine/package.json` is untouched.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: the branch is based on the integration head
Decision: the worktree branch `worktree-agent-a6cd2f4a2d5bf6941` (the plan's `agent/P2-A1`) was fast-forwarded with `git merge --ff-only` from `5f439e7` to `ef3122a` (gate G1 green) before any file was written; the engine suite was run first (25 files, 984 tests passing). What the specification left open: nothing. Reason: the harness created the worktree behind the integration head; a fast-forward of a branch with no commits of its own is the same state as branching from that head. Nothing was merged from another agent's branch.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: the guard mechanism: wrappers in guards.ts and re-pointed exports (5.13)
Decision: `finite.ts` is not edited. `guards.ts` exports `highestRoot`, `highestShortRoot`, `coxeterNumber`, `longestWord`, `minusW0`, `minusculeNodes` with the same signatures, each calling `requireFinite(board)` and then the function of `finite.ts` (imported under an `...Unguarded` alias); `index.ts` re-exports the six names from `./guards` instead of `./finite`. Engine-internal code (`extendMatrix` in `affine.ts`) does not call the finite functions at all; it runs its own bounded root search after the public function's guard. What the specification left open: where the guard call goes (`finite.ts` carries a comment marking the spot). Default used: the plan's (P2-A1 instruction 5.13). Reason: `finite.ts` is `P1-A1`'s file and outside the ownership list; the wrappers keep its text untouched. Listed under `deviations` in the report in case `MERGE` prefers the one-line guard inside `finite.ts`.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: the cache of verdicts and `classify` returning fresh copies
Decision: `guards.ts` holds `const verdicts = new WeakMap<object, ClassifyRecord[]>()` and `cachedClassify(board)`, which computes `classifyUncached(board)` (in `classify.ts`) once per board object; `requireFinite` and `requireAffine` read the cache; the public `classify` returns a deep copy of the cached records on every call, so a caller cannot change the cache. `requireGcm` and `requireConnected` do not use the cache (`boardKind` and `components` are cheap), and `cartanClass`, `identify`, `identifyAffine` check kind and connectedness directly because `classify` calls them (no recursion). The cache is keyed by the board object, never by name or matrix text. What the specification left open: the shape of the cache (E-11 names a `WeakMap` from board objects). Default used: the plan's (5.13, trap 17). Reason: boards are frozen, so the cache cannot go stale; E-5 (the cache changes no result) is checked by `guards.test.ts` (a board object built per call gives the same verdict).

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: `requireFinite` on a disconnected board
Decision: `requireFinite` throws `NeedsTwoWayRoads` when any component has a one-way road, then `NotFiniteType` unless every component's class is `'finite'`; a board in several finite pieces passes, so `longestWord` keeps working on the black nodes of a Satake diagram (phase 6). `affineExtension` additionally calls `requireConnected` and throws `NeedsConnectedBoard` on several pieces, since the highest root of a disconnected board has no meaning. What the specification left open: 5.6 speaks of "a gcm board that is not of finite type" without saying what a disconnected finite board is. Default used: the plan's (5.13, 5.7). Reason: the instruction's text; tested in `guards.test.ts`.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: the order of checks inside each function
Decision: argument shape (`RangeError`), then kind (`NeedsTwoWayRoads`), then connectedness where required (`NeedsConnectedBoard`), then class (`NotFiniteType`, `NotAffine`). So `level(board, a)` with a vector of the wrong length throws `RangeError` before any guard, `cartanClass` of a one-way board in two pieces reports the roads, and `coroot` checks the vector's length before `requireFinite`. What the specification left open: the order. Default used: the plan's (5.13). Reason: a malformed argument is a programming error and should be reported first; the rest follows 5.6 row by row.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: the limit semantics of `relabellings`
Decision: `relabellings(b1, b2, limit = CAPS.relabellingsDefault)` stops the backtracking search once `limit` assignments have been found and returns what was found, sorted lexicographically; when the total is at most `limit` the result equals the oracle's list exactly, otherwise it holds the first `limit` found in the search order (the oracle's: the nodes of `b2` in breadth-first order from the least position of each component, candidates in increasing position), sorted. `limit` must be a positive integer (`RangeError` otherwise). `identifyAffine` searches with a limit of 1 (the oracle's `first_only`); `identify` with the default, which is safe because a finite board has at most six matchings onto its standard matrix. What the specification left open: E-6 gives the limit without saying what the truncated list holds. Default used: the plan's (5.5). Reason: `identify` needs the lexicographically smallest matching, which is in every truncated list of at least one element only when the search order starts there; it does, since the candidates are tried in increasing position, and the hand test pins the first five of the star with four arms.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: the `isRootPopulation` cap boundary
Decision: mutations are counted; when the total still exceeds 1 after `cap` mutations the answer is `null`; a descent that reaches the single Martian with its `cap`-th mutation returns `true`; a single Martian returns `true` at `cap` 0; `cap` must be a non-negative integer (`RangeError`). On the triangle `e_1 + k delta` takes exactly `2k` steps (checked against the oracle for `k` = 1 to 4), so `cap` `2k` gives `true` and `2k - 1` gives `null`. The descent picks the lowest position whose number is positive, as the oracle does. What the specification left open: whether the cap counts mutations or loop iterations. Default used: the plan's (5.11). Reason: 5.5 ("the test of `e_1 + k delta` on the triangle takes `2k` steps") and E-10 (a cap is reported, never thrown).

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: `playFate`'s cap and the oracle's order of tests
Decision: `playFate(board, a, choose?, cap = CAPS.playMoves)` requires a positive integer `cap` (`RangeError` otherwise; a cap of 0 would make the first test of the loop meaningless) and keeps the oracle's order: end, move, loop test, cap test. So on `A2` from `(1, 1)` a cap of 3 reports `'cap'` with 3 moves at `(-1, -1)` and a cap of 4 reports `'ended'` with 3 moves, and a repeat on the cap-th move is `'looped'`. `firstVisit` is present only with `'looped'`. Positions are keyed by `arith.show` of the entries joined with commas, like the searches. `choose` receives the allowed positions and the current vector (the plan's `Choose<T>`) and a node outside the allowed list is a `RangeError`. What the specification left open: the cap range and the oracle's differing cap rule. Default used: the plan's (5.14, trap 6). Reason: port of `play_fate` lines 1309 to 1325; the difference from `P1-A1`'s `play` is the oracle's choice and is recorded in the file header.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: `RangeError` cases added
Decision: `RangeError` on a vector of the wrong length (`formValue`, `coroot`, `isRootPopulation`, `level`, `playFate`), a non-positive-integer cap (`playFate`), a negative or non-integer cap (`isRootPopulation`), a non-positive-integer limit (`relabellings`), a non-integer node count (`affineCandidates`), `n < 1` in `twistedAEven`, a non-boolean `short` in `affineExtension`, a non-square matrix in `nullVector`, a form matrix that is not square, not of the board's size, not integer or not symmetric (`formIsInvariant`), a coroot of a vector with form value zero or with a non-integral coordinate (`coroot`; the oracle asserts), a `choose` that returns a node not allowed (`playFate`). What the specification left open: invalid arguments the specification does not cover. Default used: `RangeError`, as `P0-A2` and `P1-A1` did. Reason: E-10 reserves the engine's own classes for the theory.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: `formIsInvariant` on a non-symmetric `M`
Decision: `M` must be a square, symmetric matrix of safe integers of the board's size; otherwise `RangeError`. `invariant` is the oracle's `form_is_invariant` (every `S_i^T M S_i = M`, computed over `bigint`); when it is false the witness is the oracle's `form_invariance_witness` in its loop order (node outside, population inside, the unit vectors then `e_a + e_b` with `a < b`), present only when found. What the specification left open: the two oracle functions answer different questions on a non-symmetric `M` (trap 9). Default used: the plan's (5.10). Reason: for a symmetric `M` the two agree; refusing other input keeps the record consistent.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: `nullVector`'s signature
Decision: `nullVector(M: readonly (readonly (number | bigint)[])[]): number[] | null`, a square matrix of integers; the port of `null_vector` (Gauss-Jordan over `Rational`, one free column, the free variable 1, denominators cleared by their lcm, divided by the gcd, negated when every entry is negative, returned only when every entry is positive). It is exported from `index.ts` (plan). What the specification left open: the signature (CONTRACTS.md 2.1 only places it in `affine.ts`). Default used: the plan's (5.8). Reason: `classify` and the tests call it on raw matrices (transposes included).

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: `AffineExtension` labels and `name`; the board constructor in `affine.ts`
Decision: `affineExtension(board, short = false)` returns `{ board, marks, comarks }` with `board` a frozen `Board<bigint>` with `Big`, kind `'gcm'`, labels `0, 1, ..., n` for both the untwisted and the short extension, and `name` equal to `` `${board.name}~` `` only when `short` is false and the input board has a name; `undefined` otherwise (tools name boards through `classify`). The board is built by a private `bigBoardOf` in `affine.ts`, which freezes the object, the matrix, every row and the labels exactly as `board.ts`'s private `makeBoard` does. What the specification left open: the labels of a short extension (E-7 names only the untwisted case) and the name. Default used: the plan's (5.7). Reason: `makeBoard` is private to `board.ts` and `board.ts` may be edited only to extend `boardFromName`; duplicating five lines was preferable to widening that file's exports.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: `boardFromName` keeps the given name and throws `NotABoard` on unknown names
Decision: `boardFromName('B2~')` has `name: 'B2~'` and `boardFromName('C2~')` has `name: 'C2~'` (their matrices differ; both are identified as `C2~` by `identifyAffine` and `classify`); `pentagon`, `square` and the twisted names keep their spelling. Untwisted names match `^([A-G][1-9][0-9]*)~$` with the finite part validated by `cartan` (so `A0~` and `B1~` throw); twisted names match `^[A-E][1-9][0-9]*\^\((2|3)\)$` and are looked up in `affineCandidates(m)` for `m = 2..13` (the oracle's range; `D14^(2)` and `A25^(2)` throw). There is no node cap in the engine (`A20~` has 21 nodes). Every other string throws `NotABoard`. The phase-0 finite branch is the last statement of the function and is unchanged. What the specification left open: the name field of these boards and the range of the twisted lookup. Default used: the plan's (5.12, trap 18). Reason: the oracle raises `ValueError` on unknown names; E-10 maps that to `NotABoard`.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: the absent-not-undefined rule for record fields and the key order
Decision: `ClassifyRecord` and `NonfiniteSubboard` are plain objects with exactly the golden field names; `bourbaki_order`, `marks`, `comarks` are absent (not present with `undefined`) when they do not apply, and the keys are in the oracle's order: `nodes, kind, balanced, class, name`, then `bourbaki_order` or `marks, comarks`. `p2-classification.test.ts` checks `Object.keys` and a deep equality after converting the node lists. What the specification left open: the representation of an optional field. Default used: the plan's (5.2). Reason: a deep-equality test against the golden record must pass.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: placement of the four record types
Decision: `ClassifyRecord` and `NonfiniteSubboard` are declared in `classify.ts`, `AffineExtension` in `affine.ts`, `InvarianceResult` in `form.ts`, each verbatim from CONTRACTS.md 2.2 and re-exported as types from `index.ts`; none existed before (checked with a search of `src/`). What the specification left open: the file. Default used: the plan's placement. Reason: each type lives with the function that returns it, as `P1-A1` did.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: the `NotAffine` message text
Decision: `requireAffine` throws `P0-A2`'s `NotAffine(cls)` unchanged for a connected board, whose message already carries the class ("this function needs an affine board; this board is finite"); for a board in several components it sets the message to "this function needs an affine board; this board has N components, whose classes are finite, affine" (each class in order) and `data.class` to the first class that is `'finite'` or `'indefinite'`, or `'indefinite'` when every piece is affine (a board in several affine pieces is not affine, and the class's `data` type admits only these two values). What the specification left open: the wording (the instruction's "not an affine board: its class is finite" is marked plan wording). Default used: `P0-A2`'s text, which is the constructor's. Reason: `errors.ts` is not mine to change; the requirement of 5.6 is that the class is in the message, and `guards.test.ts` checks it on finite, indefinite and two-component boards.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: `AnyBoard` overloads on the phase-2 functions
Decision: every phase-2 function whose result does not depend on the arithmetic (`symmetrizer`, `gram`, `cartanClass`, `identify`, `identifyAffine`, `classify`, `smallestNonfiniteSubboard`, `spectralRadius`, `affineExtension`, `marks`, `comarks`, `formIsInvariant`, `isRootPopulation`, the four `require*` guards, the six guarded finite wrappers) has a second overload taking `AnyBoard`; `level`, `coroot`, `formValue` and `playFate` take `AnyBoard` with `Vec<number | bigint>` and return the union. The generic overload `<T>(board: Board<T>, ...)` comes first, as in `P1-A1`'s `transposeBoard` and `subBoard`. What the specification left open: the contract writes `board` as "`Board<number>` or `Board<bigint>`". Default used: the plan's pattern. Reason: a generic parameter does not accept the union that `boardFromName` and the site's `resolveBoard` return; without the overloads `tsc` rejects every tool call on an `AnyBoard`.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: `plainBoard`, `intCartan`, `relabellingsOf`, `extendMatrix`, `corootOf`, `formValueOf`, `classifyUncached`, `cachedClassify` are internal
Decision: these module exports are engine-internal helpers (a plain `SafeInt` board on an integer matrix for internal searches; `cartanNumbers` through a generic parameter; the matrix-level matching; the unguarded extension on an integer matrix; the unguarded coroot and bilinear value; the uncached verdict and the cache reader) and are not re-exported from `index.ts`. What the specification left open: nothing. Reason: `affineCandidates` and `boardFromName` need the extension of standard matrices without a guard (trap 15), and no candidate table is built at module load: `classify.ts`, `affine.ts`, `form.ts`, `guards.ts` and `board.ts` import one another in a cycle that is safe only because every top-level statement is a declaration.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: `p1-api.test.ts` extended by the phase-2 names
Decision: the pinned export list of `test/unit/p1-api.test.ts` (a `P1-A1` file) gained a `PHASE_2_NAMES` constant with the 25 names appended to `index.ts`; the equality assertion now compares against the three lists together and checks each phase-2 name is a function. No other line of a phase-0 or phase-1 test was changed, and none failed because of a guard. What the specification left open: nothing; the harness note for this run said to extend the pinned list rather than break it. Default used: the harness note. Reason: the test's intent (an exact list of the public API) is kept.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: `-0` never appears in an extended Cartan matrix
Decision: `extendMatrix` writes `0` rather than `-0` when a pairing is zero (`Ca[0][j+1] = a === 0 ? 0 : -a`). What the specification left open: nothing. Reason: `-0` passes `intEq` and `BigInt(-0)` is `0n`, but `toEqual` tells `-0` from `0`; an integer matrix should hold integers.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: the fast-check seeds and run counts
Decision: every property file records `SEED = 20261010` (the seed of `P0-A2` and `P1-A1`) and its `NUM_RUNS`: p5-form 400, p7-roots-signs second half 200 (the file's own constants), p10-affine 300, p13-relabel 300. Each property file asserts that no input vector was changed and contains a check that the property is not vacuous (the form is positive on a nonzero vector; every root is accepted and every double rejected; most firings change the position; most permutations are not the identity). What the specification left open: the seeds and counts. Default used: the plan's minimum of 200 runs. Reason: CONTRACTS.md 3, "a fixed seed recorded in the file".

## 2026-10-10 P2-A1: test file names and helpers
Decision: golden files `test/golden/p2-types-form.test.ts`, `p2-affine.test.ts`, `p2-twisted-affine.test.ts`, `p2-affine-names.test.ts`, `p2-classification.test.ts`, `p2-pentagon.test.ts`, `p2-kostant-affine.test.ts` (one key or key group each, registered with `covers` in the harness's spellings); property files `p5-form.test.ts`, `p10-affine.test.ts`, `p13-relabel.test.ts` and the second `describe` block of `p7-roots-signs.test.ts`; unit files `guards.test.ts`, `labels-affine.test.ts`, `p2-hand.test.ts`; the helper `test/helpers/p2.ts` (`boardFromCartan` over `P1-A1`'s `bigBoard`, `renumber`, `permutationArb`, `renumberedBoard`, `transposed`, `unitPlusMultiple`, `star`, `cycle` and the five boards of the 5.6 rows). The oracle's `cartan_class_by_minors` is written inside `p2-hand.test.ts` as the cross-check and is not shipped. What the specification left open: the layout beyond the golden and property files. Default used: the plan's (section 4). Reason: README section 4, every build agent owns its own tests.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A6: markers found in the board family (section 3 of the instruction)
Decision: record. Numeral: the `<text data-numeral="{label}">` of `Node.svelte`; a fraction is a `<g data-numeral="{label}">` holding SVG `<text>` elements (optional sign, numerator, denominator) and a `<line>` bar, so fractions are SVG text already, never a `<foreignObject>` or an HTML overlay. Label: `<text data-label="{label}">` (P0-A5's hook; the selector used is `text[data-label]`, because T2's garden puts `data-label` on its edge `<g>` elements, which must not be matched). Tooltip with the exact digits: the `title` attribute of the node button (`hintFor` in T1 and T9); the exact text is also the button's `data-value`. The board's root `<svg>` has a `viewBox` in grid units (`0 0 k rows`, or the polygon box divided by 64) and CSS sizes it. Arrowheads and chevrons are plain `<path>` and `<polygon>` elements (`draw/roads.ts`), no `<marker>`, so no ids to clash in a composite. The Copy link function is `linkFor(instanceId)` of `site/src/lib/history.ts` (what `copyLink` writes).

## 2026-10-10 P2-A6: the footer line (SPEC 8.3 [D])
Decision: the text is `footerText(f) = boardName + ' · ' + link` (U+00B7 with a space either side), set in the monospaced system stack read from `--font-numerals` (fallback the same stack as `base.css`), 12 pixels, tabular figures, filled with the resolved `--text`, left edge 8 pixels in, first baseline 16 pixels below the top of the footer, 16 pixels per line, height `8 + 16 * lines + 8`, all inside `<g data-footer=""><a href="{link}">...</a></g>`. Lines are broken by `footerLines`, before an `&` where possible, else after the last `.`, `/` or `,`, else hard; no character is dropped and there is no cap on the number of lines, because a PNG carries only visible text and SPEC 8.3 requires the state in the figure. Example of this run: `A2 · http://localhost:4391/tools/board?z=1&g=A2&v=p&m=f&c=p&s=1,0&w=1`. What the specification left open: the format. Reason: the instruction (5.3).

## 2026-10-10 P2-A6: footer lines fit the figure (plan detail adapted)
Decision: the line length in the picture is `min(96, floor((width - 16) / 7.5))` characters (7.5 pixels is a generous advance of a 12-pixel monospaced character), at least 24; a figure narrower than 196 pixels is widened to 196 when it has a footer or a note. `footerLines(text, 96)` itself is as planned and its unit test uses 96. What the plan said: lines of 96 characters. Reason: at the default viewport (360 pixels) an A2 board is 128 pixels wide; 96 characters at 12 pixels (about 700 pixels) would run off the right edge and be clipped in the PNG, losing the state the footer must carry. The tallest footer seen in the tests: 5 lines (A2 with a 16-digit start, 196 pixels wide); a long play gives proportionally more.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A6: the link is the Copy link, which carries the page's origin
Decision: the footer calls `linkFor(instanceId)` (history.ts), so the footer and "Copy link" give the same string (SPEC 7.4). That function builds the link from `location.origin` and the page's path, not from `SITE_URL`/`BASE_PATH`; on the deployed site those agree. On a tool in its default state the link has no query (history.ts writes only what differs from the author's defaults), so the footer then names the route of the default state. What the specification left open: nothing beyond 7.4. Reason: one function for both, as the instruction requires.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A6: FooterLine and the labels option with the signatures of CONTRACTS 4
Decision: `export interface FooterLine { boardName: string; link: string; }` (the definition CONTRACTS 4 names but does not give). `exportSVG(svg, footer)` and `exportPNG(svg, footer, scale?)` have exactly the CONTRACTS 4 signatures. The labels option is built without a parameter: with `Node labels` unchecked ToolFrame passes `withoutLabels(composeFigure(svgs))`, a detached copy without `text[data-label]`; the page keeps its labels. Additive exports: `inlineStyles`, `composeFigure`, `withoutLabels`, `footerText`, `footerLines`, `exportFileName`, `pngSize`, the constants `FOOTER_LINE_CHARS`, `LABEL_SELECTOR`, `PNG_MAX_SIDE`. No deviation from CONTRACTS.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A6: the pixel-unit export root
Decision: the file's root is `<svg width=W height=T viewBox="0 0 W T" role="img">` in CSS pixels, `W` and `H` the `getBoundingClientRect()` size of the live drawing (or the `width` and `height` of a composite); the drawing is a nested `<svg x=0 y=0 width=W height=H>` keeping its own `viewBox` (the inlined clone itself); the note of exact digits and the footer are siblings below it, so the `viewBox` of the drawing clips nothing of them. The exported size is the on-screen size and depends on the viewport (SPEC 6.1 "Size on screen"). First child `<title>`: the board name when a footer is given, else `exported figure`. `aria-hidden`, `tabindex`, `focusable` and `class` are removed from every element; `xlink:href` becomes `href`. Reason: the instruction (5.2 step 3), A-10.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A6: inlined styles, theme and background
Decision: `inlineStyles` walks the live tree and the clone in parallel and writes, as a `style` attribute, these computed properties: `fill`, `fill-opacity`, `fill-rule`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `stroke-opacity`, `stroke-dasharray`, `stroke-linecap`, `stroke-linejoin`, `vector-effect` (the board's strokes are non-scaling; without it a 2-pixel stroke in grid units would be enormous), `opacity`, `font-family`, `font-size`, `font-weight`, `font-style`, `font-variant-numeric`, `letter-spacing`, `text-anchor`, `dominant-baseline`, `paint-order`, `visibility`, `color`. To keep the file small a property is written on the drawing's root always and on a descendant only when it differs from what the element would get anyway (the parent's computed value for an inherited property, the initial value for `opacity` and `vector-effect`) or when the element has a presentation attribute of that name. Any attribute whose value still contains `var(` is removed afterwards (`draw/roads.ts` sets `stroke="var(--road)"` and the like as presentation attributes), as are `<style>` elements and comments (Svelte's hydration markers). Running transitions in the drawing (Node.svelte fades fills in 150 ms) are finished before reading, so the export shows the state, not a frame of the fade. The background is a `<rect>` of the root's full pixel size filled with `--page` resolved through a probe element to `rgb(...)`. The export therefore carries the theme in force (system setting or the `data-theme` switch). Reason: the instruction (5.2 steps 2 and 4, 5.7 Theme), SPEC 8.3.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A6: fractions redrawn as SVG text; pairing rule
Decision: a numeral group whose button's `data-value` is `p/q` becomes, in the export, the same `<g>` marked `data-frac="p/q"` holding one `<text>` with two `<tspan>` children (numerator above, with U+2212 when negative; denominator below, at the positions Node.svelte used) and the bar `<line>`, so there is one value text per node. Pairing rule: a drawn numeral `data-numeral="L"` is paired with the single `[data-node="L"]` button inside the drawing's parent element (Board.svelte puts the SVG and its group of buttons in one box), falling back to the tool root (`[data-tool]`) only when the parent holds no node button; when the label is not unique in that scope the node is left as drawn. Reason: the instruction (5.2 step 5).

## 2026-10-10 P2-A6: long numbers in a picture (SPEC 4.0 "Long numbers")
Decision: a node is shortened when its drawn numeral differs from its `data-value` with ASCII `-` read as U+2212 (no arithmetic, no conversion). For each, the node's `<g>` gets a `<title>` with the exact digits (the SVG tooltip), and the note `<g data-exact="">` below the drawing lists `{label} = {exact digits}`, one entry per shortened node, in the footer's typeface and size, wrapped like the footer without a cap. The note is part of "every export" and no option switches it off. Reason: the instruction (5.7). Open question for the owner: the note's format.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A6: which SVGs make the figure; composites
Decision: ToolFrame binds its existing `<figure>` element (no wrapper added) and takes every `<svg>` in it, in document order, that is not inside another `<svg>`, a `button`, `a`, `label` or `summary` and is at least 32 by 32 CSS pixels (the 16-pixel view icons of T1 and mood glyphs of T9's list stay out). One is exported as it is; several go through `composeFigure`. `composeFigure` keeps drawings that overlap on screen at their relative positions (T9 draws its moods as a second SVG over the board) and stacks separate ones (T1's linked view; T2's board and garden) in document order with a 16-pixel gap, root `width` the widest, `height` the sum plus gaps, both in pixels with a matching `viewBox`. What the plan said: stack all with a 16-pixel gap. Reason: stacking an overlay below its board would misplace T9's moods.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A6: HTML drawn over an SVG (T2's garden vertices)
Decision: the vertices of T2's orbit garden are HTML buttons over the SVG of its edges, so a plain serialisation would export edges without vertices. `inlineStyles` therefore draws every button of the drawing's parent element that lies over the drawing and shows a border, a background, a `::before` dot or text as a rounded `<rect>` (its computed border and background colours and radius) with its text (computed font and colour) and its `title` as a `<title>`, mapped into the drawing's coordinates through `getScreenCTM()`. The transparent, textless hit areas of Board.svelte draw nothing. Exact digits of a shortened garden vertex are in that `<title>` only, not in the `data-exact` note (open question). Reason: the export must be a picture of what is on screen (instruction 5.1).

## 2026-10-10 P2-A6: hint ghosts
Decision: elements with `data-ghost` (T1's hint ghosts, drawn only while a node is hovered or focused) are left out of the export, like elements whose computed `display` is `none`. Reason: they are a transient hint of the pointer, not part of the state; the instruction expected them hidden by display.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A6: PNG
Decision: default scale 2; `pngSize` reduces the scale so that the larger side is at most 8192 pixels. The PNG is drawn from the exported SVG text through a same-origin blob URL, an `Image` and a canvas; errors reject with `the figure could not be rendered as an image`. No font is embedded (system stacks, SPEC 6.3). Reason: the instruction (5.5).

## 2026-10-10 P2-A6: ToolFrame controls, hooks, the boardName prop, file names
Decision: after "Download data", two `<button class="control">` `Export SVG` (`data-export="svg"`) and `Export PNG` (`data-export="png"`), a comment where P6-A5 adds "Export LaTeX" and "Cite", a `<fieldset>` with a visually hidden legend `Export options` holding two checked checkboxes with visible labels `Footer line` (`data-export-option="footer"`) and `Node labels` (`data-export-option="labels"`), and `<span data-out="exportNotice">`, empty by default, showing `Error.message` of a failed export (`nothing to export` when the figure has no drawing) and cleared on the next success. All four controls have `disabled={!hydrated}`. The existing `.control` style gives the buttons 44 pixels; the options are 44 pixels high with 24-pixel checkboxes and wrap inside the share row at 320 pixels. Nothing existing was moved, renamed or restyled. New optional prop `boardName?: string`; default: `state.board` when it is a string, else `custom board`. File name `exportFileName(toolId, boardName, ext)` = `{toolId}-{boardName with every character outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] replaced by -}.{ext}` (`board-A2.svg`), not the instance-id rule of "Download data", because the instruction's tests fix it. `export.ts` stays a dynamic `import()` from the click handlers (as P1-A2 does for "Download data"), so its code is fetched on first use. No announcement in the live region (A-4 reserves it for moves; the download is the feedback). Reason: the instruction (5.6).

## 2026-10-10 P2-A6: size
Decision: record. Built chunk of `export.ts` (fetched only on the first click of an export or "Download data"): 10592 bytes, 4353 bytes gzip level 9, including P1-A2's `exportJSON`. The ToolFrame chunk, which carries the new controls and handlers and is on every tool route, is 32957 bytes, 12425 bytes gzip in all (not a delta). `npm run size` was not run (GATE runs it).

The file is P1-A2's and outside this agent's list, so it is not edited here. # P2-A2 decisions (T3, the Form Finder)

## 2026-10-10 P2-A2: environment and starting point
Decision: none; record. Worktree `/home/user/mutation_game/.claude/worktrees/agent-a6babc4b6454b81c4`, branch `worktree-agent-a6babc4b6454b81c4` (the plan's `agent/P2-A2`), fast-forwarded with `git merge --ff-only` to the integration head `03dc851` (stage 2.1 merged) before any file was written; `npm ci --prefer-offline` once; Node v22.22.0. The engine suite was green at the start (38 files, 1444 tests). Browser runs used a scratch copy of `playwright.config.ts` on port 4372 (`reports/playwright.p2a2.config.ts`, ignored by git); `npm run size` ran on port 4373. No dependency added. By the session's instructions `pages/tools/[tool].astro` received the three additive edits for T3 (static import, the `client:idle` line, `'form'` in `HYDRATED`).

## 2026-10-10 P2-A2: the three parts and what default shows
Decision: all three parts (meter, builder, small values) are always rendered and open, one after the other inside the figure; the preset only decides which comes first (`partsInOrder` in `t03/presets.ts`; the others follow in the order meter, builder, small values). `default` and `meter`: the meter part first, i.e. the populations board on A3 from (1, 0, 0) in free play with the meter beside it and History below, then the builder (every weight 1) and small values with three judged rows. `builder`: A2, builder first. `small-values`: A3, small values first. What the specification left open: the arrangement (instruction 5.1, plan). Reason: P2, nothing the lesson needs sits behind a tab; no part is collapsed, so "expanded" means "first".

## 2026-10-10 P2-A2: boards offered
Decision: `boards: 'all'` in the registry, as T1 and T2. The picker (on the tool's own board, not when linked) shows the 32 named types grouped by letter from T1's `PICKER_GROUPS`; a board outside them (an affine name, `pentagon`, `square`, a custom matrix) is shown as a disabled first option with its name. The `board` prop and links accept every board `resolveBoard` resolves, because P1-A2's codec treats `'all'` as "every board" (6.6 rule 8 then never refuses). What the specification left open: how 4.0 "offers the 32 named types" combines with M3 beat 2 (small values on `A2~` and `D4~`). Reason: the picker is what "offers" governs; pages and links must reach the affine boards.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A2: the linking mechanism
Decision: no new mechanism. With `linkTo` the tool calls P1-A2's `followToolState(linkTo, ...)` (state.ts), the store P1-A6's T2 follows; the meter reads `positionsOf` of the last published state (its last position), and the tool draws no board and no History of its own (`meterModel` in `t03/model.ts` returns `ownBoard: false`). Before the followed instance has published (the build, or a T1 not yet hydrated) the meter reads the T3's own configured state, which the page sets equal to the T1's. The table view's city buttons drive the T1 by publishing `{ ...followed, moves: [...moves, label] }` under its id (P1-A6's protocol). A followed state with `coords: numbers` gives the sentence `The linked board starts from numbers; the meter reads populations only.` instead of a value. The builder and small values keep working on the T3's own configured board. Reason: SPEC 7.4; instruction 5.3; decisions/P1-A6.md.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A2: weights: integers, ranges, defaults
Decision: weights are integers; a city weight runs from 1 to 24, a road weight from 0 to 24 (`CITY_MIN`, `ROAD_MIN`, `WEIGHT_MAX` in `t03/weights.ts`). Each weight is a slider (`input type=range`, arrow keys) paired with a number field; a typed value outside the range or not a whole number is refused by `readWeight` and the field returns to its last accepted weight on blur or change. Default: every weight 1 (on a simply laced board this passes; on B2 it fails), unless the page passes `cityWeights` (label order) and `roadWeights` (by label pairs). Weights, rows and the verdict go back to their defaults when the board changes. What the specification left open: the control and its range (instruction 5.4, plan). Reason: SPEC 4 T3 "City weights are positive; road weights are zero or positive"; 24 admits every passing weight of the named types (at most 6, on G2) times 3; a zero city weight would let the one-way road "pass" (verify.py 1530).

## 2026-10-10 P2-A2: the matrix convention
Decision: `matrixOf(board, city, road)` returns the doubled integer matrix 2M, diagonal `2 w_i`, off-diagonal `-w_ij` on joined pairs (0 elsewhere), symmetric by construction, and that is exactly the matrix handed to `formIsInvariant`. With the passing weights `w_i = 2 d_i`, `w_ij = 2 d_i A_ji` it equals `2 gram(board)`, checked entry by entry in `T03.test.ts > builder accepts the symmetrizer weights on A2, B2, B3, F4, G2`. The data export says so in `builder.convention`. Reason: instruction 5.4; verify.py 1527 builds M with `Fr(-wij, 2)`; scaling does not change invariance.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A2: wording
Decision (plan wording): passing verdict `Passes: every mutation preserves this form.`; failing verdict `Fails: some mutation changes this form.`; before a test `Press Test to ask the engine about these weights.`; witness `Witness: mutating city 2 takes the population (1, 0) to (−1, 1), and the form does not take the same value on the two.` (true minus signs; the populations from the engine's witness and `mutate`, never a form value, 7.3); the verdict is also announced (`Fails: ... The witness is city 2, population 1, 0.`). Small values: `root population`, `not a root population`, `too large to test here` (exact, for `null`), `the test needs two-way roads` (one-way board; `isRootPopulation` is not called), `type a whole number in every city` (incomplete row). No invariant form (meter and value cell): `This board has no invariant form.`. Digit notice: `An entry takes at most 6 digits and an optional minus sign: city 2 in row 1 keeps 123456.` (or `stays empty`). Meter label `Form value (p, p)`. Move announcements use the A-4 templates unchanged; the form value is not appended.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A2: the digit rule: sign and paste
Decision: a field holds an optional leading minus sign (ASCII or U+2212) and at most `CAPS.formFinderDigits` digits; the sign is not counted. Every input event offers the whole new text to `offerEntry`: a text with a seventh digit, a letter or a sign elsewhere is refused whole and the field is put back to its last accepted text, so a pasted seven-digit string is refused, not truncated. Reason: SPEC 5.6 "the field refuses more"; instruction 5.5 (plan reading).

## 2026-10-10 P2-A2: default rows of small values
Decision: the first single Martian, all ones, and the alternating population 1, 0, 1, ..., duplicates removed; on A3 that is (1,0,0), (1,1,1), (1,0,1) with values 2, 2, 4 and verdicts root population, root population, not a root population, computed at build time. A page may pass `populations`. "Add a row" adds an empty row. Reason: 4.0 Starts meaningful; instruction 5.5.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A2: data-out names and properties
Decision: data-out names `formValue`, `meterNote`, `testVerdict`, `witness`, `smallValue`, `smallVerdict`, `digitNotice` (plan names), with History's `moveCounter`, `historyStrip`, `historyCounter`, Predict's `predictResult`, `predictReveal` and ToolFrame's `caption`, `notice`, `noscript`, `exportNotice`; all listed in the registry's `outs` and in the comment block of `T03.spec.ts`. Properties beyond the common ones: `cityWeights: number[]` (label order), `roadWeights: { pair: [number, number]; weight: number }[]` (labels), `populations: (number | string)[][]` (label order). `coords: 'numbers'` throws at build time naming the instance; `layers` is accepted and has no effect.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A2: a link with c=n, v or m
Decision: a link whose coords are numbers, or whose view or mode is not populations and free, is unreadable for T3: the tool loads its defaults and shows P1-A2's `LINK_NOTICE`. The state written back is exactly `{ schema, tool: 'form', board, coords: 'populations', start, moves }`. The weights, the rows and the part shown are never in a link (6.6). Reason: instruction 5.2.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A2: long numbers
Decision: the meter and the small-values value cell use T1's `shortValue` and `isLong` (`t01/longNumber.ts`) above 12 digits, with the exact digits in the `title` tooltip, in `data-value`, in the table view and in the data export. No second shortening was written.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A2: the capped root test on the main thread (deviation reported)
Decision: `isRootPopulation` runs on the main thread at its default cap (`CAPS.rootTestSteps`, 20000), once per complete row on every accepted keystroke. Measured in Node (`T03.test.ts > capped root test timing is measured`, A2~ at k = 11000, 20000 steps, median of 7 runs): 23 to 28 ms on this container (node v22.22.0, linux x64, 4 processors); four times that is about 93 to 114 ms, above the 50 ms long-task rule of SPEC 7.6. The cap and the place of the test were not changed (not mine); reported under `deviations` with a request to the owner and P2-A1 whether the cap or the place (the worker, E-9) should change.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A2: size
Decision: none; record. `npm run size` on this branch: `/tools/form/` 64.9 kB gzip in 10 scripts, limit 90 kB. The registry entry imports no engine function (it is loaded on every tool page).

Decision: D7 (a = Cp; the A-3 state phrase of a city comes from the sign of its number, as T1 derives it) and D19 (the picker shows the name chosen) relied on; no other default of section 10. No [U] item was settled; the tool states no theorem.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: environment and starting point
Decision: none; record. Worktree `/home/user/mutation_game/.claude/worktrees/agent-aeb02b8cff9247516`, branch `worktree-agent-aeb02b8cff9247516` (the plan's `agent/P2-A3`), fast-forwarded with `git merge --ff-only claude/session-6a181f60-hzzoud` from `5f439e7` to `03dc851` (stage 2.1 merged) before any file was written; `npm ci --prefer-offline` once; Node v22.22.0. The scratch checks of the instruction (section 3) all held: `classify` of `[[2, -4], [-1, 2]]` gives one affine record named `A2^(2)` with marks `2, 1` and comarks `1, 2`, its spectral radius prints `2.0000`, `whereToRun` sends 2000 expected items to the main thread and 100000 to the worker, and `resolveBoard` accepts the one-way matrix `[[2, 0], [-1, 2]]`. ## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: the editor contract and the name-against-matrix rule
Decision: `site/src/components/board/editor/types.ts` holds `BoardEditorProps`, `EditorChange` and `EditorPreset` exactly as the plan's block of section 5.2. `onChange` emits the preset's own BoardSpec while the board is an unedited preset (a name such as `E6` or `A2^(2)`, or the `{ cartan }` of a test board), and `{ cartan, xy }` from the first edit on, with labels 1..n in the order of the matrix rows (E-7) and whole grid points obeying 6.1. `values` is indexed by position (the rows of the matrix). What the specification left open: CONTRACTS.md has no editor entry. Default used: the plan's. Reason: T16 (P2-A5) composes the editor by this contract; MERGE copies it into CONTRACTS.md 5.1.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: the editor draws its own nodes instead of composing Board.svelte (deviation)
Decision: BoardEditor.svelte reuses the Board family's parts (Roads.svelte, Node.svelte when the host passes `values`, nodePositions, toPixels, the CSS size rule of 6.1, keyboard.ts arrowTarget for A-1) but renders its own node buttons and discs rather than Board.svelte. What the specification left open: the plan says the editor "composes Board.svelte". Reason: Board.svelte (not mine to edit) names every node with the game template of A-3 ("Node 3, value 2, can be fired"), requires a decimal value on every node (signOf throws on an empty value) and cannot mark nodes or report a selection, while the editor needs "Node 3, selected" names, value-free nodes in T4 and a marked sub-board. The hooks of 4.0 are kept on every node button (`data-node`, `data-board="populations"`, `data-value` empty in T4, `data-can-act="true"`), plus `data-selected`, `data-marked` and `data-xy`. Listed under deviations in the report.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: the keyboard model of the editor
Decision: the nodes are one tab stop (roving tabindex); bare arrows, Home and End move the focus as A-1 says (on a custom layout they follow the labels and wrap); Enter or Space selects the focused node as the subject of the road and move controls (the previous subject becomes the other end of the road); Ctrl, Alt or Meta with an arrow moves the focused node by one grid point; Delete or Backspace removes it; `+` adds a node; `u` and `r` undo and redo (keyboard.ts shortcutOf, inside the `data-board-group`). After the drawing: Add node, Remove node N, four Move buttons, three selects for the roads (the other node, the count from the subject to it, the count back, each 0 to 4), and the board picker with a Load board button. What the specification left open: the keys (A-1 reserves the bare arrows for focus). Default used: the plan's suggestion of a modifier plus arrow. Reason: A-8, P10; the GATE keyboard-only test draws the triangle with `keyboard.press` alone.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: drag, the taken-point rule and the grid adoption
Decision: dragging a node (pointer events with capture, more than 6 pixels) moves it by the dragged distance in grid units, snapped to whole points and clamped to 0..11; a point that holds another node is refused (never swapped). An unedited preset whose layout is not whole grid points (the D fork at 0.6, polygons, the circle of a test board) adopts whole points on its first edit (editor/model.ts gridOf: rows rounded and shifted to start at 0, so D4 becomes (0,1), (1,1), (2,2), (2,0); a circle scaled to the least whole radius at which the rounded corners differ). What the specification left open: the plan's "refuse or swap" and how a named layout becomes grid points. Reason: 6.1 Custom boards.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: the minimum of one node and the resetsPlay rule
Decision: removing the last node is refused (the button is disabled with the visible reason "A board keeps at least one node."), and the 13th node is refused with "A board has at most 12 nodes."; both caps are enforced in model.ts as well as in the buttons. `resetsPlay` is true for add-node, remove-node and preset, false for roads and move (`RESETS_PLAY` in model.ts). What the specification left open: the minimum and the rule for add and roads. Default used: the plan's. Reason: SPEC 4 T4, 4.0 Board pickers, 5.6.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: the tool presets and their options outside schema 1
Decision: `default` is the path A3 in the editor; `verdict` is A3 with the verdict panel before the editor in reading order; `hunter` is the one-way road `{ cartan: [[2, 0], [-1, 2]], xy: [[0, 0], [1, 0]] }` with the hunter switched on. The board of each preset is a state field and a link; the panel order and the hunter switch are view options outside schema 1 (6.6), carried by the `preset` and `hunter` properties, never by a link key. The one-way matrix is built in t04/toolPresets.ts from its definition (one road from city 1 to city 2, C = 2I - A^T), not typed, because the registry module, which is loaded on every tool page, may not import the golden file. The captions state the result without numbers that have golden values. What the specification left open: SPEC 4 T4 names no default board. Default used: the plan's reading of M3 beats 1, 2 and 6. Reason: CONTRACTS 6, 4.0 Configuration.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: how the test boards reach the island at build time
Decision: components/board/editor/presets.ts (`testBoardPresets()`, `editorPresets()`, `testBoard(label)`) reads `classification_tests` through `resolveGoldenPath` of lib/golden.ts and is imported only by Astro frontmatter: pages/tools/[tool].astro passes `boardPresets={testBoardPresets()}` on T4's line, so Astro serialises the thirteen matrices into the island's props. The client-safe names (32 finite types, 32 untwisted affine boards by constructor name, 10 twisted names) live in editor/namedPresets.ts with no import. `site/dist` holds no `wythoff_hull_checks` (checked after the build). What the specification left open: how a build-time list reaches an island whose route page passes fixed props. Default used: the plan's "serialised property". Reason: 7.6 (the golden file is 455 kB). The page edit is the import of T04ClassificationLab, the import of testBoardPresets, the line and `lab` in HYDRATED; the extra import and prop are a small extension of "its line", noted for MERGE.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: the B2 = C2 display (D19) and the gloss on C2~
Decision: whenever classify names a component `B2`, the panel shows "B<sub>2</sub> = C<sub>2</sub>" (text "B2 = C2", `data-name="B2"`), whatever the picker said; the picker lists both B2 and C2 (labelled "B2 (= C2)" and "C2 (= B2)") and both B2~ and C2~. A component named `C2~` is shown as returned with the gloss ", the affine board of B2 = C2". Default used: D19. Reason: SPEC 2.8, 4 T4.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: names typeset with sub and sup, not names.json (deviation)
Decision: every name in the verdict is set with plain markup: the letter, a combining tilde for X~, `<sub>` for the rank and `<sup>` for (2) or (3); `data-name` holds the plain name. names.json is not imported. What the specification left open: 7.3 asks tools to look names up in names.json. Reason: names.json holds KaTeX HTML for the 32 finite names only, needs KaTeX's stylesheet on the page and would ship every entry to the client for any board the reader draws (7.6: no typesetting in the client). Request to MERGE: if names.json gains a plain-markup field for affine and twisted names, the panel can switch to it.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: data-out names
Decision: nodeCount, kind (data-kind), verdictClass (one per component), verdictName (data-name), componentNodes, bourbakiOrder, marks, comarks, balanced, weights (one per component), spectralRadius (absent on a board with a one-way road), nonfiniteSubboard (data-nodes, data-class; absent when null), rootCount, layerCounts (data-counts of the complete layers, data-complete-layers), completeCount, stopMessage (absent when the count is complete), counterStatus, counterNotice, hunterResult (data-population, data-word, data-moves, data-start), linkNotice, editorSubject, editorMarked, editorReason; editor root hooks data-editor, data-road-style, data-nodes, data-selected. Default used: the plan's names, extended. Reason: 4.0 Test hooks; P2-A9 writes M3.spec.ts against them.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: the counter's two calls and the keep-counting rule
Decision: the bounded search runs synchronously through t04/counter.ts `rootSearch` (cap 2000; no layer bound on a board classify calls finite, `layers` otherwise), whose hint `counterHint(board, 2000, finiteKnown)` `whereToRun` sends to the main thread (tested); it is not routed through `engineCall` because the build-time render needs the result synchronously and engineCall answers with a promise. "keep counting" calls `engineCall('orbitGraph', [board, seeds, 'mutation', 100000, maxDepth], counterHint(board, 100000, false))`, a new search in the worker; its result replaces the main one for that board object and is dropped if the board changed meanwhile. The button is offered only after a position-cap stop (`truncated` and not finite): after a layer stop a 100000 search with the same layer bound would return the same count. Seeds are the unit vectors in the board's arithmetic. The stop sentences are T2's own function (t02/limits.ts stopMessage), so the words match character for character. No helper was requested from P1-A2; the 100000 positions come back serialised, which costs a moment after the button press and none on the main thread before it. What the specification left open: plan points of 5.6 and 5.8. Reason: E-9 ("A call is never started in one place and continued in the other").

## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: the hunter's sentences
Decision: found: "(−1, 1) after 2 moves from one Martian in city 1: mutate 2, then 1" (entries with a true minus, shortened above 12 digits; exact digits in data-population, the table view and the export). None found: "none among the k root populations of the first L layers" when the layer bound ended the search (SPEC 4 T4), "none among the k root populations found; layers 0 to L are complete" when the cap did (plan), "none among the k root populations" when the search was complete on a finite board (plan). The hunter searches only the positions the counter found (also after keep counting) and states no theorem; it is off by default and switched on by the `hunter` preset or the "Conjecture hunter" checkbox. Reason: 4.0 Stated limits; 2.11 and Appendix E item 4 keep the theorem in the lessons.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: the node name template in the editor
Decision: "Node 3", "Node 3, selected", "Node 3, marked" (and "Node 3, value 2, selected" when the host writes values). What the specification left open: A-3's template is for game boards. Default used: the plan's. Reason: an editor's nodes are not fired.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: undo, redo and reset of edits
Decision: editor/history.ts EditHistory keeps the board specs of the edits since the board was loaded; undo steps back one edit, redo forward, an edit after an undo discards the redo, reset returns to the loaded board (the preset, the link or the author's board) and empties the history; loading a preset or a link starts a new history. Wired through ToolFrame's onUndo, onRedo, onReset, and `u` and `r` on a focused node. Announcements: "Undid an edit. Verdict: ...", "Redid an edit. Verdict: ...", "Back to the board that was loaded. Verdict: ...". Reason: SPEC 9.2 "undo, reset" for a tool with no move list (plan semantics).

Decision: t04/link.ts `linkFits` checks the readable `g` value against 512 characters; if it ever failed the tool shows "This board is too large for a link; use Download data to keep it." in `data-out="linkNotice"`. No editor board reaches it (the densest twelve-node board with two-digit coordinates encodes to fewer than 493 characters; tested). Reason: 6.6.

## 2026-10-10 P2-A3: announcements after edits
Decision: one sentence per edit through ToolFrame's announcer: "Added node 4. Verdict: indefinite.", "Removed a node; the nodes are now 1 to 3. Verdict: finite A3.", "Roads changed. Verdict: ...", "Node moved. Verdict: ...", "Loaded D4~. Verdict: affine D4~."; on the first edit of a board whose labels start at 0 the sentence adds "The nodes are now numbered 1 to n." Reason: A-4 (one polite region per tool), the plan's wording.
