## 2026-10-10 P3-A5: the MathML [U] of SPEC 7.3, settled for Chromium only on this machine
Decision: LinearForm renders MathML (`RENDER = 'mathml'`). `site/tests/e2e/mathml.spec.ts` ran here on Chromium: the launcher of Playwright 1.64.0 reported Chromium 141.0.7390.37 (the headless shell installed under PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH; `browsers.json` of playwright-core lists chromium revision 1248), and the test passed: the server-rendered forms x1, x2, x3 and the client-created form 2x1 + x2 are `<math>` elements in the MathML namespace with an `aria-label` and a box of non-zero size, and every subscript is set smaller than its base and lower than it. WebKit (playwright-core lists 27.2, revision 2370) and Firefox (157.0, revision 1555) are not installed in this cloud container and cannot be installed here, so their two tests failed at `launch()` with Playwright's "please run npx playwright install" message: not run, not skipped. The owner runs, on the Mac: `npx playwright install webkit firefox` then `npm run build` and `npx playwright test site/tests/e2e/mathml.spec.ts`. If either engine fails there, set `RENDER` in `site/src/components/math/LinearForm.svelte` to `'spans'` (the span path is implemented and unit-tested; the spec then reads the `<sub>` of each term) and record the engine and its version here. What the specification left open: [U] in 7.3 ("MathML Core in Chromium since version 109, from memory; check in phase 3"). Default used: the instruction's (5.9). Reason: Appendix E item 17, the builder settles a tool's [U] when the tool is first used; the item stays partly open (two engines) until the owner's run.

## 2026-10-10 P3-A5: how mathml.spec.ts launches the three engines (deviation from the roster)
Decision: the spec launches each browser itself with `chromium`, `webkit` and `firefox` as exported by `@playwright/test` (re-exported from playwright-core), one test per engine, each against the configured `baseURL`; the repository's single Chromium project runs the file. The roster says "Playwright projects added for this spec only", but `playwright.config.ts` belongs to P0-A6, then MERGE and GATE. Requested from MERGE: install Firefox and WebKit in `ci.yml` (`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit firefox`), and, if MERGE prefers projects, three projects `mathml-chromium`, `mathml-webkit`, `mathml-firefox` with `testMatch: /mathml\.spec\.ts/` and `testIgnore` of that file in the main project (the spec would then use the project's browser instead of launching its own). Reason: COMMON 4.2.

## 2026-10-10 P3-A5: LinearForm rendering and spoken rules
Decision: terms in increasing label order; zero terms omitted; a coefficient 1 is not written, -1 is written as a minus sign; other coefficients as `<mn>`; between terms `<mo>+</mo>` or `<mo>−</mo>` (U+2212), a leading negative term with `<mo>−</mo>`; each variable `<msub><mi>x</mi><mn>label</mn></msub>`; the zero form `<mn>0</mn>`; no invisible times. The `aria-label` speaks coefficients through `speak` of a11y.ts, variables as "x 1", operators "plus" and "minus": "2 x 1 plus x 2", "minus x 1 minus 2 x 3", "0". Props: `coeffs` (by position, number or bigint), `labels` (board.labels, the subscripts, E-7), `letter` (default x), `render` (default the module constant `RENDER`, so that tests can render both paths). The span fallback: the same terms in `<span>` with `<i>` and `<sub>`, `role="math"` and the same `aria-label`. What the specification left open: the plan's rules (5.5). Reason: they reproduce the forms of A.1 and M5 beat 5. Svelte 5.57.2 creates `<math>` and its children in the MathML namespace on the client (checked by mathml.spec.ts after a move); no `<svelte:options namespace>` was needed.

## 2026-10-10 P3-A5: default board, caption and state
Decision: default board A3 (M5 beat 5), start all ones, no moves; the only preset is `default`. Caption: "Play the numbers game on the left. The right board makes the same moves with letters in place of numbers, so every number fired is a linear form. Over a complete game each positive root of the reversed board is fired exactly once." The state is `{ schema: 1, tool: 'symbolic', board, coords: 'numbers', start, moves }`; view and mode are fixed by the tool and never written into links (`?z=1&g=B2&c=n&s=1,1&w=1.2.1.2`). What the specification left open: the plan's (5.2). Reason: 4.0 "default is the state described in this section"; CONTRACTS 6.

## 2026-10-10 P3-A5: links T7 refuses beyond 6.6
Decision: besides the codec's rules (decodeState with the instance prefix), a link loads the default with the codec's notice when: `c=p` (coords other than numbers); a start with an entry that is not a positive integer (T7 needs "a start with all numbers positive"; F6 fills the table only then); a move that legal play forbids at its point of the play (6.6 rule 6 for the mode in force: the tool's mode is legal, but since links carry no `m`, the codec cannot see it, so T7 replays with `firstForbiddenMove` and mode legal itself). The same rules make an authoring error (a page passing such a start or moves) fail the build with a message naming the instance, as T1 does. What the specification left open: plan reading of 5.2. Reason: the left board must always be a legal play from an all-positive start.

## 2026-10-10 P3-A5: the left board is T1's model; Big with no message
Decision: the left board is `T1Game` of `t01/model.ts` (numbers view, legal mode, numbers coordinates), imported and not changed: one engine call per move, step and play to the end lowest position first (E-5), and the silent switch to Big when a start or a play leaves the safe range (SPEC 4 T1), which also gives the long-number display of `Node.svelte` and `t01/longNumber.ts` (shortened on the node, exact in the tooltip, the table view and the export). The announcements are T1's (`t01/announce.ts`) in the numbers view. Every board T7 offers is finite with at most 120 moves, so play to the end runs on the main thread (E-9); the full recomputation after a move (symbolicPlay, n unit-start applyWord calls, positiveRoots of the transposed board) took a median of 3.2 ms on E8 along its 120-move longest word in Vitest here, against the plan's 25 ms bound. Reason: the instruction's "reuse T1's mechanism; do not write a second one".

## 2026-10-10 P3-A5: the right board is a T07 sub-component, with its own hooks
Decision: `Board.svelte` draws a numeral on each node and validates its value as a decimal (sign.ts throws on "2,1"), so the right board is `T07SymbolicBoard.svelte` (README 6: T07*.svelte), built from the board family's parts (draw/layouts.ts, the size rule of 6.1 in Board's CSS, Roads.svelte, keyboard.ts's arrow model). Each disc shows the sign of its entry by fill and a + or − glyph (6.3, A-5); the forms themselves are listed under the drawing, one line per node with LinearForm, so that a long E8 form never covers a neighbour. The node buttons are one tab stop with arrows, Home and End (A-1), `aria-disabled="true"`, `data-can-act="false"`; activating one changes nothing. Hooks: the left board is wrapped in `data-out="numbersBoard"`, the right in `data-out="symbolicBoard"`; the right board's buttons carry `data-board="numbers"` and `data-value` equal to the coefficients in label order joined by commas (for example `2,1`), plus `data-sign` (positive, negative, zero or mixed); each line of the list carries `data-entry` and `data-form`. Tests scope every node query by the wrapper. A request to P0-A5 through MERGE: a `content` snippet prop on Board.svelte would let a later tool draw non-numeric entries without a sub-component. What the specification left open: 4.0 names only `populations` and `numbers` for `data-board` and decimal or `p/q` for `data-value`; raised under openQuestions.

## 2026-10-10 P3-A5: A-3 wording on the right board
Decision: "Node 2, form x 1 plus x 2" (the LinearForm spoken text), with no "can be fired" state, since the right board does not act. The left board keeps the templates of A-3 ("Node 3, value 2, can be fired"). Reason: plan (5.6).

## 2026-10-10 P3-A5: the stacking width and the layout boxes
Decision: the two boards stand side by side when the tool's figure (its inline-size container) is at least 600 pixels wide and are stacked, left board first, below; each board's panel is its own size container, so the size rule of 6.1 measures the panel. The fired list keeps a fixed height of 8em and scrolls inside its box; the side table renders all N rows at build time and scrolls inside a box of at most 24em; the figure's grid column is `minmax(0, 1fr)` so that a long form never widens the page at 320 pixels (A-11). The three scroll boxes (the fired list, the side table and the list of current forms) are keyboard stops (`tabindex="0"`, the first two as named regions), so that their content can be scrolled without a pointer; axe's `scrollable-region-focusable` flagged the side table before this. Reason: 4.0 Small screens and 7.6 (no layout shift on hydration; measured equal boxes and CLS within 0.1 in T07.spec.ts).

## 2026-10-10 P3-A5: the side table and the fired list
Decision: the table's caption is "Positive roots of the reversed board" (the reversed board is not named, which avoids D19 questions); one row per root of `positiveRoots(transposeBoard(board))` in the engine's order, shown as a population in label order; an unused row reads "not yet fired"; a used row shows "move k", the form (LinearForm) and the number fired on the left at that move, read from the left board's play. Hooks: `data-out="rootTable"`; each row `data-out="rootRow"` with `data-root`, `data-used`, and `data-move` when used; the list `data-out="firedForms"` with items carrying `data-move` and `data-form`. Rows are matched by equal coefficient vectors (positions order equals label order on the 32 types). "Show as table" (A-10, `data-out="valuesTable"`) has one row per node with the label, the left number (exact digits), the right form and a "Fire node k" button, disabled when the number is not positive.

## 2026-10-10 P3-A5: the T1 colour-class panel
Decision: key `'colours'` in T1's `panels` (the key P1-A5 declared). Wording: "First class: nodes 1, 3; second class: node 2." ("node" for one label, "no node" for none), each class preceded by a glyph (a disc ● for the first, a square ■ for the second, `aria-hidden`) coloured `--edge-3` and `--edge-4`; node fill is untouched (it carries the sign, 6.3). ## 2026-10-10 P3-A6: the graph, its edges and the stated limits
Decision: one `orbitGraph(board, [rho], 'firing', cap, undefined, true)` per board, cap `CAPS.weylExplorerGroup` (F4 completes with exactly 1152 items, tested), vertices keyed by the entries joined with commas (`arith.show`, natively for SafeInt and Big), layer = depth. Edges: every legal move applied once more to every item, drawn once, downward; `|W| n / 2` edges (tested). `buildGraph(board, cap?)` takes the cap so a test can force a cut: then only layers 0 to `completeLayers` are drawn and counted, the sentence of SPEC 5.5 "stopped after N positions; layers 0 to L are complete" (N the number of items, L `completeLayers`) is shown in `data-out="limit"` and in the figure's text alternative, and no path count is given. A `null` count reads "count not offered". T8 passes no `maxDepth` and takes no `layers` bound: 4.0 "Growth off the finite types" names T2 and T4, and every board T8 offers is finite, so "stopped after L layers" never arises; the `layers` property is accepted and ignored. T8 never writes "not of finite type" (tested over the component's source, the captions and the sentences). Reason: instruction 5.3.

## 2026-10-10 P3-A6: the edge rule above 192 elements and the canvas
Decision: at most 192 elements (D4 included, the boundary is strict) every edge is drawn, coloured by node through `var(--edge-k)` and carrying the node label as text; above 192 (A5, B4, C4, F4) only the edges of the current game and the edges at the focused vertex, both directions (into it from the layer above and out of it to the layer below), are drawn. `data-out="edgeMode"` reads `all` or `game-and-focus`. Above 192 the figure is a Canvas 2D drawing after hydration; the server render (and the no-JavaScript reader) gets the SVG snapshot that `svgScene.ts` writes from the same `Scene` (layout.ts) in Node, `data-out="snapshot"`, `role="img"` and an aria-label naming the board, the positions and the layers. After hydration the snapshot stays in place, hidden under the canvas once it is drawn, and is rewritten one task after each draw: it is the mirror of the drawn edges (`data-out="edge"`) and what ToolFrame's SVG and PNG export take (ToolFrame exports the figure's visible SVGs; a canvas cannot be exported, see requests). The canvas is wrapped in an element with `role="img"` and the same label (Svelte refuses `role="img"` on a canvas). Reason: instruction 5.7; 7.1; 7.4.

## 2026-10-10 P3-A6: no long task on F4
Decision: the graph, layout and counts are cached per board (t08/cache.ts); a pick or a link that names a board not yet prepared computes them in four tasks (board and verdict, graph, layout, counts) before the state changes, the canvas is drawn in a task of its own after the DOM update (dots stamped from one small sprite instead of a thousand arcs), the colour tokens are read once per theme, and the snapshot SVG is rewritten in a later task. Measured in Chromium headless: no long task from the pick of F4 to the draw (the first version, all in one task, made one of 96 ms). Reason: 7.6; roster acceptance.

## 2026-10-10 P3-A6: geometry, hit areas, keyboard model and names
Decision: layout from `layeredLayout` (rank = number of moves). Hit areas are squares of 44 pixels when the widest layer has at most 6 vertices (A1, A2, A3, B2, C2, G2: 6 x 48 + 32 = 320), otherwise 24, with columns 4 pixels wider than the hit area and rows of 72 pixels (all edges) or 44 (above 192), so no two hit areas overlap; the box has a fixed height (the drawing's, at most 480 pixels) and scrolls in both directions (A-11). Keyboard (plan reading of A-1): at most 192 elements the vertices are real buttons in one group with one tab stop (roving tabindex, the current vertex first); above 192 one focus button outside the canvas moves to the focused vertex. Left and Right move within a layer in drawn order, Up and Down to the vertex of the previous or next layer nearest in x, Home and End to the top and the bottom vertex, Enter or Space jumps; the focused vertex is scrolled into view. Hover on the canvas is a hit test within the hit area. Accessible name: `Position 2, minus 3, 2, layer 3`, with `, on the game` for a vertex of the path. The details panel shows the vertex pointed at, else the current position, so it is never empty and holds the information itself (P2). Reason: instruction 5.10.

## 2026-10-10 P3-A6: the jump, announcements, highlight
Decision: activating a vertex (click, Enter, Space, or a table row's jump button) sets the moves to its shortest word from `wordTo` in labels; with `linkTo` the word is published to the Game Board with `publishToolState`. Moves on T8's board use the A-4 templates through T1's announce.ts unchanged (a move that ends the game adds `Game over after N moves.`; play to the end is one `Played N moves to the end. ...` sentence). Sentences without a template (plan): `Jumped to position 2, minus 3, 2 by 3 moves.`, `Loaded the play 1, 3, 2. Plays with this stack: 2.`, `Board B3: 48 positions in 10 layers.` (numbers from the engine). Hover or focus of a vertex sets the highlight to `{ kind: 'position', board, value }` (label order), hover of a separating root to `{ kind: 'root', ... }`, cleared on leave; a position highlighted by another tool of the page marks its vertex (`data-highlighted`). Reason: instruction 5.4, 5.10.

Decision: two wraps, no new item. E2 (beat 6): "Mozes introduced his game in 1990 as a generalisation of this puzzle, firing negative numbers." Fallback: "Later authors, Donnelly among them, describe the game Mozes published in 1990 as a generalisation of this puzzle." Mozes' sign convention appears nowhere else on the page: beat 1's convention sentence names Eriksson, the Olympiad problem and Gashi, Schedler and Speyer as firing negative numbers and does not name Mozes. The bare credit "The numbers game is Mozes'" (8.4) and "attributed to Mozes and Eriksson" (F3, [S2], cited) are not wrapped. E6 (beat 7): "The same table holds on the affine boards with multiple roads, which arrive in module six." Fallback: "On boards with multiple roads the same table was computed on every affine board the site offers, and the Affine Playground gives an argument for it beside it." The release build printed `open item E2 used on /modules/m4-numbers/ (fallback shown)` and the same for E6 (E6 is also registered by T15Route). The Olympiad's proposer is not named (E11); Proctor's restricted game is not mentioned (E17); Kac's Tits cone is not cited (E4).

## 2026-10-10 P3-A8: provenance and credit
Decision: the Seen box has six statements with provenance [W03c] section two (the rules; first published definition, which credits the numbers game to Mozes), [Eri95b] Definition 1.1 and [Don08] Theorem 2.1 (F3, attributed to Mozes and Eriksson), "verified by computation for every board of finite type of rank at most eight" (F4), "verified by computation on every board of finite type of rank at most eight" (CS_i = R_i C, the bridge sentence, the det C classes and det C = 1 on E8, F4, G2), and "verified by computation on every affine board the site offers" with [GSS12] Theorem 1.2, signs reversed (the level and the fate table on boards with single roads). Credit (8.4): "The numbers game is Mozes' [Moz90], with Proctor's earlier use of the same process [Pro84] and Eriksson's development of it [Eri95b]". [W-MS] is cited for Proposition 0.3, pp. 31-32 (q = −Cp, the gain) and p. 30 (Venus), and in Sources as "an unpublished manuscript, undated (circulated c. 2001 to 2004)". Conventions stated where quoted: the Olympiad (fires negative, a = −x), [GSS12] (fires negative, c = C^T), Donnelly (M = C^T, fires positive), Bourbaki (transpose).

## 2026-10-10 P3-A9: heights of coroots
Decision: beat 6 defines the coroots as the positive roots of the reversed board (2.5), the height as the sum of the coefficients, says that on A3 and E8 a coroot and its root have the same height, and that with double roads they can differ, "so the numbers fired are heights of coroots"; the Seen box and the B3 challenge say "heights of coroots". The theorem is cited to [Ste59] 9.1 for roots, [Kos59] and [Mac72] as reported by later authors, and the coroot version as verified by computation for every board of rank at most eight. Reason: F6, F7, SOURCES 11.5.

## 2026-10-10 P3-A9: the Lie theory paragraph
Decision: the graph of T8 is named the Hasse diagram of the left weak order: a move multiplies the element reached on the left (the play i_1, ..., i_k reaches w = s_{i_k} ... s_{i_1}, and the next move gives s_i w), and the separating roots of the position w rho are the positive roots made negative by w^{-1}, its inversion set ([Hum90] 1.7; checked on the example 1, 3, 2, whose roots (0,1,0), (0,1,1), (1,1,0) are those of the reduced word 1, 3, 2 of w^{-1}). The wave with class 0 fired first is the product ... c_1 c_0 of h factors, a power (c_1 c_0)^{h/2} only for even h. Reason: instruction 5.12.

Decision: dropped. Measured: alone (with the M2 swap built in, load 3.53 to 1.40) M0 420.1, M1 808.6, M2 933.7, M3 1253.6 ms TBT; together with remedy (c1) (load 0.69 to 1.37) M0 332.8, M1 680.3, M2 685.4, M3 1091.4 ms; LCP 0.44 to 0.62 s, CLS unchanged (at most 0.0017). Traces show why the gain is small: Chromium lays out a newly parsed block once before it decides the block is off screen; `content-visibility: hidden` on the same blocks was no cheaper.
Why dropped: the full browser suite failed 4 tests with it (M1 "no forbidden statement" and "writing rules", M2 "anatomy", M3 "no forbidden statement"): `innerText` of a skipped block is empty, and the lesson tests read the Lie theory paragraph, beat 5 and the whole article with `innerText`. Worse, checks that read `main.innerText` (for example "no em-dash in the text") would pass vacuously on the skipped blocks. Tests may not be loosened, and the lessons' tests are not mine, so the remedy goes. Lesson.astro keeps a comment saying so.

## 2026-10-10 P3-X1: remedy (c1), the render hint for the first view, kept
Decision: kept. Lesson.astro puts `<link rel="expect" href="#first-view-end" blocking="render">` into the head (through a new named slot `head` of Base.astro), and Beat.astro writes `<div id="first-view-end" hidden></div>` at the end of beat 1. A browser that knows the hint (Chromium 124 and later) paints once the end of beat 1 has been parsed instead of painting and laying out the first view again for every chunk of HTML; others ignore it; if the marker is missing the browser paints when the document has been parsed. Nothing changes without JavaScript (it is markup), nothing is per lesson, and M4 and M5 get it by using Beat as the anatomy says.

The gain is modest, of the order of 50 to 250 ms, and inside the spread of single runs on M0; it is kept because every pair of runs on M1 and M3 moved the same way and it costs nothing measurable.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A1: the folded board's labels and name (plan reading of E-7)
Decision: `fold` builds the folded board directly, not through `fromAdjacency`: `{ n: m, cartan: Cf, labels, kind, arith: SafeInt, name }`, frozen like every engine board. `cartan` stays in the order of the orbits, so `cartanNumbers(folded)` is the golden `folded_cartan`. With `id = identify(folded)`, `labels[id.order[k]] = k + 1` (position `id.order[k]` plays Bourbaki node `k + 1`) and `name = id.name`; `kind` is `boardKind(Cf)` (always `gcm` for a symmetry of a finite board). Fallback: when the folded board is in several pieces (possible because `requireFinite` admits a disconnected board whose pieces are finite, for instance three A1 nodes folded by the identity) or `identify` returns `null`, `identify` is not called or not used, the labels are `1..m` in the order of the orbits and `name` is absent. The eight rows that fold give: A3 flip `B2` labels `[1, 2]`; A5 flip `B3` `[1, 2, 3]`; A7 flip `B4` `[1, 2, 3, 4]`; D4 swap `C3` `[1, 2, 3]`; D5 swap `C4` `[1, 2, 3, 4]`; D6 swap `C5` `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`; E6 flip `F4` `[1, 4, 2, 3]`; D4 rotation `G2` `[2, 1]`. Listing the orbits in increasing label reproduces `folded_orbits_in_bourbaki_order` on all eight (tested). What the specification left open: E-7's row "folded board" says labels are in the Bourbaki order of the type `identify` names, without saying how the board object is built. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.3, traps 18, 19). Reason: `fromAdjacency` would give labels `1..m` in position order.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A1: guards of averagedSimpleCartan and applyWordFloat; no guard on symEig and classifyRestricted
Decision: `averagedSimpleCartan` and `applyWordFloat` call `requireGcm` then `requireFinite` (NeedsTwoWayRoads on a one-way board, NotFiniteType off the finite types), like `fold`, `averagedRootsType`, the geometry and the Wythoff functions. `symEig` (a matrix) and `classifyRestricted` (a set of vectors and a Gram matrix) have no guard; the board-taking functions that call them carry it. In every guarded function the argument shape is checked first (RangeError: a symmetry that is not a permutation of `0..n-1`, a vector of the wrong length, an unknown game, a position outside `0..n-1`, a bad `rings` or cap), then `requireGcm`, then `requireFinite`, the order P2-A1 and P3-A1 used. `symEig` throws RangeError on a matrix that is not square and does not check symmetry (as the oracle). What the specification left open: 5.6 names "fold, averagedRootsType, the Wythoff, Satake, representation and geometry functions" but not `averagedSimpleCartan`, and two of the functions take no board. Default used: the plan's readings (instruction 5.5, 5.6, 5.10, 5.13). Reason: `averagedSimpleCartan` belongs with `fold` and `averagedRootsType` in the 5.4 table; `applyWordFloat` stands in the Geometry table; finiteness is decided through `guards.ts` only (E-11).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A1: classifyRestricted's parameter type (a supertype of the contract)
Decision: `classifyRestricted(S, B, r)` in `src/restrictedType.ts` accepts vectors whose entries are `number`, `bigint` or `Rational` (exported type `RestrictedEntry`) and converts each entry to a `Rational` on entry; `B` is `readonly (readonly Rational[])[]`. S is treated as a set: a vector given twice counts once (the oracle's argument is a Python set; keyed by the rational text in lowest terms). It returns `RestrictedType = { name: string; classes: { class: string; roots: number; form_value: string }[] }`, classes in ascending squared length, `form_value` as `ratToString` text (rule 4). The oracle's decision table is ported in its order (non-reduced first; one norm A, D, E; two norms with the ratio 3 test for G2 before the rank 2 rule, which always says `B2`, and F4 before the B and C counts); every `assert` and `raise ValueError` becomes `throw new EngineError('classifyRestricted: ...')` with the oracle's message text (`unrecognised simply-laced system`, `unrecognised system`) or a sentence starting `not a root system` for the bare asserts, followed by the oracle's tuple values. What the specification left open: CONTRACTS.md 2.4 phase 6 writes `S: number[][]`, but `averagedRootsType` passes rational averages. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.4): a supertype of the contracted parameter, so both callers type-check. Reason: reported under `openQuestions` as a contract amendment to confirm, not as a deviation.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A1: wythoffFVector returns n + 1 entries
Decision: `wythoffFVector(board, rings)` returns `n + 1` bigint entries as the oracle does: `f[0]` vertices, `f[1]` edges, ..., `f[n]` = `1n` when some node is ringed and `0n` when none is; with no ring the result is `[1n, 0n, ..., 0n]`. Tests compare `f.slice(0, n)` with the golden `f_vector`. What the specification left open: the length. Default used: the oracle's (instruction 5.11). Reason: a port keeps the oracle's shape.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A1: wythoffEdges items, order and truncation
Decision: each item is `[u, v]` with `u` before `v` in the lexicographic order of their entries compared as integers (through `arith.sign(arith.sub(...))`, never as strings), entries converted to `number`; the visited set is keyed by the decimal text of both ends in canonical order (`u|v`); items are in discovery order: the seeds `{lambda, R_i lambda}` for `i` from 0 to n - 1 with `lambda_i != 0`, then breadth first over the pairs in the order found, firing both ends at each node in increasing position through `fire`. The cap acts when the search is about to add item number `cap + 1` (seeds included): `{ items, truncated: true }` with exactly `cap` items; otherwise every edge with `truncated: false`; a cap that is not a non-negative integer is a RangeError; cap 0 with a ringed node gives `{ items: [], truncated: true }`. On E8 with rings `(0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)` (1_42) and `CAPS.edgesAtRest` the result is truncated with exactly 70000 items. What the specification left open: the oracle's set has no order and raises at the cap. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.12, traps 11, 12). Reason: E-6, E-10.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A1: rings must be non-negative integers
Decision: `wythoffFaceTypes`, `wythoffFVector` and `wythoffEdges` throw RangeError unless `rings` has one entry per position and each entry is a non-negative safe integer. What the specification left open: the instruction names only the wrong length; the oracle does not check. Default used: plan. Reason: SPEC.md 2.14 takes "a dominant position lambda with numbers a_i >= 0" and T10 offers "a non-negative integer on each node"; the face rule and the polytope graph are meaningless on other input.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A1: the rounding helper and the minus-zero rule
Decision: `round6(x) = Math.round(x * 1e6) / 1e6`, then `-0` normalised to `0` (`r === 0 ? 0 : r`); radii are `round6(Math.hypot(x, y))`, grouped in a `Map` and sorted ascending; distinct points are counted on the text key `${round6(x)},${round6(y)}`. The body of `coxeterPlaneRings` is the helper `ringsOfPoints(points, h)`. Both `round6` and `ringsOfPoints` are exported from `geometry.ts` for the unit test of the rule and are not part of the public API (`index.ts` does not export them). The computed radii equal the golden radii exactly (not only within 1e-5) on all 31 types, checked once with a throwaway test. What the specification left open: the helper (5.4 says "rounded to 6 decimals and -0 counted as 0"). Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.8, traps 13, 14). Reason: `toFixed` would count `-0.000000` and `0.000000` apart.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A1: the order of a sub-board's Weyl group
Decision: `|W_K|` in `wythoffFaceTypes` is `1n` for the empty set and otherwise the product over the connected components of K (the oracle's `induced_components`, joined in either direction) of `BigInt(weylOrder(subBoard(board, component)))`, with the components' orders kept in a `Map` for the length of one call only (nothing is cached across calls, E-5). Counts are `W / (|W_K| |W_K'|)` in bigint with exact division (EngineError on a remainder, which cannot happen). What the specification left open: the oracle calls `weyl_order(sub_matrix(C, K))`, which equals this product on a disconnected K. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.11, trap 8). Reason: no `weylOrder` on an empty or disconnected board; `TypeError: Cannot mix BigInt and other types` avoided by converting first.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A2: the depth axis of the Coxeter view and the three turns
Decision: the Coxeter view is coordinates 0 (right) and n-1 (up) of y with coordinate 1 as depth for n >= 3 (toward the viewer is positive), and none for n = 2. The turning angles of the j value act on the frame in the order horizontal axis u (turn[0]), vertical axis v (turn[1]), viewing axis w (turn[2]), each about the axes as they stand after the previous turn. Signs follow the right-hand rule for turning the picture, with u, v, w right-handed: a positive turn[0] brings the top toward the viewer, a positive turn[1] takes what faced the viewer to the right, a positive turn[2] turns the picture counterclockwise on the screen. Each step turns two orthonormal vectors in their own plane (angles reduced modulo 360 before conversion to radians; a multiple of 360 is skipped, so the frame stays bit-exact), which keeps the frame orthonormal to 1e-12 (tested for n = 2 to 8). What the specification left open: SPEC 6.6 names the three axes but not the order, the signs, or which coordinate is depth in the Coxeter view. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.3). Reason: the round trip "a turn, then its negation in reverse order" is the identity, and the picture of the oracle's `coxeter_plane_points` is the view at zero turn.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A2: rank 2 and rank 1
Decision: on rank 2 `frameFor` returns `w: null` (never a zero vector) and `turnFrame` applies only turn[2]; turn[0] and turn[1] leave the frame unchanged, so the picture stays flat and u, v stay orthonormal. `parseProjection` still accepts three angles on rank 2 and `formatProjection` writes back what was parsed. Plan extension: rank 1 (A1, among the named types T10 offers) is a line: `frameFor(1, coxeter)` is u = (1), v = (0), w = null, no turn moves it, `parseProjection` accepts `coxeter` (with or without angles, as `urlCodec.ts` does) and never `xyz`, and `defaultProjection(1)` is `coxeter`. What the specification left open: SPEC 4 T10 says "rank 2 flat" and nothing about rank 1. Reason: a link `g=A1&j=coxeter` passes the codec, so the projector must read it.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A2: the default projection per rank
Decision: `defaultProjection(n)` is `coxeter` for n = 1, 2 and n >= 4 and `xyz:1,2,3` for n = 3, all with zero turn. What the specification left open: SPEC 4 T10 fixes the kinds of view per rank, not the default. Default used: the plan's (5.3). P4-A3 may fix another default per board in `registry/T10.ts`, and the state field `projection`, when present, overrides.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A2: "projection preserves the invariant form on the chosen plane"
Decision: read as: in y-space the form is the dot product (y . y' = (p, p'), tested within 1e-9 against `formValue` on 50 random population pairs for A3, B3, G2 and E8 with E from `choleskyBasis`, and from `euclideanBasis` too once the engine exports it); rotations in coordinate planes and the turns are isometries (dot products unchanged within 1e-12); the frame is orthonormal, so a vector y = s u + t v of the chosen plane is drawn at (s, t) with length preserved, and on rank 3 with xyz:1,2,3 the three coordinates hold the whole length. What the specification left open: the roster's wording. Default used: the plan's interpretation (5.3).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A2: the depth cue, its alpha floor, eight levels
Decision: `depthStyle(depth)` for depth 0 (far) to 1 (near) is width = lineWidth x (0.5 + d), radius = pointRadius x (0.6 + 0.8 d), alpha = 0.6 + 0.4 d, linear and so continuous and non-decreasing; `depthStyle(null)` (no depth axis) is the middle (d = 1/2). Base values: line width 1 CSS pixel, point radius 2.5 (plan). The alpha floor is 0.6: the road and text colours of both themes blended at 0.6 over their page keep 4.5 to 1 or more against it (light road 4.54, dark road 6.02 by the WCAG formula with sRGB blending; tested at 3 to 1, A-6), so a far segment is still a road. The cue works through width and radius first. Renderers quantise into eight levels (`DEPTH_LEVELS`), each drawn with `depthStyle` at the centre of the level, rounded to two decimals so that canvas and SVG carry identical numbers; a scene without depth uses the middle style for every level. What the specification left open: the mapping (T10 "points and segments with a depth cue"). Default used: the plan's (5.4, 5.6).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A2: the scale of buildScene and the depth of a scene
Decision: `buildScene` puts the origin of y at the centre of the box, one scale for both directions, y flipped once (downwards on the screen); the scale is (min(width, height) / 2 - margin) / radius with radius by default the largest norm of the unprojected vectors, which `project` records in `Point3.norm` (plan extension of `Point3`), so that no rotation or turn changes it and a picture does not jump while it is turned; margin defaults to the radius of the nearest point plus 2 pixels. Depth is z normalised over the scene's z range; a scene has no depth axis when the cue is off or when the z range is below 1e-12 times the radius (rank 2: every z is 0), and then every depth is 1/2. Segments carry the mean depth of their ends and are sorted far to near, ties in the order given (stable). `Scene` also carries `scale` (pixels per unit of y) for T10's pointer mapping; the renderers do not read it. What the specification left open: everything here. Default used: the plan's (5.5).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A2: the caps while turning, and above 70000 edges
Decision: `selectSegments(scene, turning)`: above `CAPS.edgesAtRest` segments nothing is drawn but the vertices, at rest and while turning alike (beyond that cap the edges are not enumerated at all, T10 "Limits"); at rest everything up to that cap; while turning everything up to `CAPS.edgesTurning`, otherwise exactly `CAPS.edgesTurning` chosen by the fixed stride floor(k m / cap), k = 0 .. cap - 1, through the far to near order, the same every frame. `drawScene` draws the first `CAPS.verticesDrawn` points in scene order. The caps are read from the engine's `CAPS` (exported again as `LIMITS` for the tests); a unit test scans the three modules for a retyped cap. What the specification left open: how the turning sample is chosen. Default used: the plan's (5.6).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A2: colours, background and the canvas context
Decision: segments use `--road`, points `--text`, the background `--page` (plan; CONTRACTS 8 lists the tokens but assigns none to T10's marks and SPEC 6.3 has no such mapping). `drawScene` receives the three concrete strings (T10 reads them with `getComputedStyle` at draw time and on a theme change); `renderSvg` writes `var(--road)`, `var(--text)` and `var(--page)` by default, or concrete strings for a file or an export. Neither module contains a colour literal (tested). The canvas fills its background with the page colour (`fillRect`, added to the plan's list of `Context2DLike` members) so that the picture is the same as the SVG's background rectangle; `strokeStyle` and `fillStyle` are typed `unknown` in `Context2DLike` so that a real `CanvasRenderingContext2D` fits. The device pixel ratio is applied once with `setTransform(dpr, 0, 0, dpr, 0, 0)` inside one `save`/`restore`. What the specification left open: the tokens of T10's marks. Default used: the plan's (5.6, 5.7).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A2: the j value
Decision: `parseProjection(text, n)` uses the same regular expression as `site/src/lib/urlCodec.ts` (`coxeter` or `xyz:` and three digit strings, optionally `@` and three integers, negative allowed) and adds the rank rules: xyz axes distinct and in 1..n (so never on rank 1 or 2); it returns null otherwise. It agrees with the codec on every input the codec accepts except that the codec does not check rank (it accepts `coxeter` everywhere, as the projector does) and both accept leading zeros (`xyz:01,2,3`). `formatProjection` writes axes from 1, angles reduced to 0..359, and leaves out `@0,0,0`; `formatProjection(parseProjection(s, n)) === s` for every normalised s. Angles are kept as parsed (for example -30) and reduced only when written or turned. What the specification left open: normalisation. Default used: the plan's (5.3).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A2: the SVG snapshot and its 200 kB guard
Decision: `renderSvg(scene, options)` returns one `<svg xmlns=... viewBox="0 0 W H" width height>` string: optional `<title>` and `<desc>` first (then `role="img"` and `aria-labelledby`), a background `<rect>`, one `<g>` of segments with one `<path stroke-width stroke-opacity d="Mx yLx y...">` per depth level far first, and one `<g>` of points with one `<g fill-opacity>` per level holding one `<circle cx cy r>` per point; every id is prefixed by `options.id` (default `projection`); coordinates rounded with `roundTo(x, decimals)` (default one decimal). It uses the same `selectSegments(scene, false)`, `levelStyles`, `segmentRuns` and `pointPlan` as the canvas, and a test checks that the canvas and the SVG receive the same rounded coordinates, widths, radii and opacities in the same order. Measured: the E8 root polytope (240 points, 6720 segments, depth cue off) in a 360 by 360 box is 135761 bytes at one decimal, under the 200 kB guard. Because P4-A1's `euclideanBasis` and the committed E8 file do not exist yet, that test builds the scene from the engine (`roots`, and the pairs at inner product 1 through the integral Gram matrix, a sample checked with `formValue`, every degree equal to the golden 56) with `choleskyBasis` in place of `euclideanBasis`; it switches to `euclideanBasis` by itself once the engine exports it, and the continuation may switch its source to the committed E8 file as the plan says. The size in the true Coxeter plane will differ by a few kilobytes and is to be re-measured then. What the specification left open: the markup (7.4). Default used: the plan's (5.7).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A2: distinct dots and rings
Decision: `roundTo(x, digits) = Math.round(x * 10^digits) / 10^digits + 0` (never -0); `countDistinct` keys on both coordinates rounded to 6 decimals; `ringsOf` keys on the radius `Math.hypot(x, y)` of the unrounded coordinates rounded to 6 decimals, sorted innermost first: the two different rules of the oracle's `coxeter_plane_rings`. This is not bit for bit Python's `round` (half to even on the exact binary value); the two can differ only within about 1e-12 of a rounding boundary. What the specification left open: the JavaScript rounding. Default used: the plan's (5.8).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A2: the preset file format, key naming and the configurations
Decision: `PRESET_CONFIGS` holds the seven configurations of the M7 figure table in this order: A2 highest root (`root-polytope`, `two-graphs`), A3 highest root (`root-polytope`), D4 highest root (`root-polytope`, `coxeter-plane`), A3 (1,0,0) (`rings`), B3 (1,0,1) (`face-table`), B3 (0,1,1) (`make-uniform`), E8 highest root (`showpiece`); the rings of a root polytope are computed as `toNumbers(board, highestRoot(board))`, never typed. Keys `<board>-r<rings joined by '.'>` (A2-r1.1, A3-r1.0.1, D4-r0.1.0.0, A3-r1.0.0, B3-r1.0.1, B3-r0.1.1, E8-r0.0.0.0.0.0.0.1, checked by loading the module in Node). A file holds, in this order and nothing else: schema, tool, key, board, rings, presets, counts {vertices, edges, moveEdges}, edgesEnumerated, fVector (numbers when safe, else decimal strings), vertices, adjacency and moveAdjacency (for each vertex the sorted larger neighbours), tree {parent, node as labels}, shortRoots (null in all seven files: the four root polytope configurations, A2, A3, D4 and E8, are simply laced, and the other three are not root polytopes; B3 has two root lengths, but its two configurations are not root polytopes. Corrected 2026-10-17 in the repair entry below). `serializePreset` is `JSON.stringify` with no spaces and a final newline; the manifest `index.json` is `{schema, tool, files: [{key, board, rings, presets, file, counts}]}` with bare file names. A repeated pair, a loop, or an edge end that is not a vertex throws; a truncated orbit or edge enumeration throws `PresetRefused`. The default configuration of T10 is P4-A3's to fix (deviation, see the report). The measured sizes of adjacency lists against pairs, and the committed files themselves, wait for P4-A1 and the continuation. What the specification left open: the format (plan). Default used: the plan's (5.9).

Decision: the reviewer's finding is right. `presets.test.ts > the rings of every root polytope configuration equal numbers_of_highest_root` asserted that the golden `highest_short_root` is absent for every board of `PRESET_CONFIGS`, with the comment "Every shipped configuration is simply laced"; B3 is in `PRESET_CONFIGS` (face-table, make-uniform) and the golden file has `types.B3.highest_short_root = [1,1,1]`, `simply_laced = false`. Fixes: (1) the golden check now applies only to the root polytope configurations (rings `'highest-root'`: A2, A3, D4, E8), and the check that every file has `shortRoots === null` stays for all seven, with the reason stated per kind of configuration; (2) the short roots branch of `computePreset` is now the exported function `presetShortRoots(config)` (the same code, moved; it needs only the engine of phases 0 to 3), and two new tests cover it without P4-A1: on every named type of the golden file but C2 (the board B2), a root polytope gets null on a simply laced board and otherwise the orbit of the highest short root, starting at golden `numbers_of_highest_short_root`, of size twice golden `n_short_positive`, each point an integer population of the length of the highest short root and, at rank 4 and below, plus or minus a golden positive root; and every configuration of `PRESET_CONFIGS` gets null, B3's included although B3 has short roots. In the scratch tree the files written after the move are byte for byte those written before it, and the preset tests pass 13 of 13 (projector, presets and presets-size together 41 of 41). Mutations, each run and restored in a scratch copy: removing the root polytope guard fails the second new test, the freshness test and, with the files regenerated, the kept `shortRoots === null` check of the corrected test; returning null always fails both new tests; starting from the highest root instead of the highest short root fails the first. ## 2026-10-17 P4-A2 (continuation): the drawing-time probe, its page and what is timed
Decision: `site/src/pages/dev/draw-time.astro` (layout `Page.astro`: `lang`, one `h1`, the navigation; linked from nowhere) mounts `DrawTimeProbe.svelte` with `client:load`. The probe fetches `import.meta.env.BASE_URL + 'presets/T10/' + 'index.json'`, finds the file whose presets include `showpiece`, fetches it, builds `boardFromName`, `euclideanBasis`, the populations of the vertices with `toPopulation` (floats, cached) and the edge list from `adjacency`, reads `--road`, `--text`, `--page` with `getComputedStyle`, sizes the canvas backing store to 360 x `devicePixelRatio`; all of that is outside the timed region. Then five times: `performance.now()`, the Coxeter frame, y = E p and `project` for every vertex, `buildScene` (360 by 360, depth cue off), `drawScene` at rest with the page's ratio, `performance.now()`. "The drawing time" is the median of the five (plan); the first is reported beside it (`firstDrawTime`), so a cold first draw is visible. Hooks: `data-tool="geometry"` and `data-moves="0"` on the root, `data-hydrated="true"` when the five draws are done or failed, `data-out` `drawTime` (median, one decimal), `drawTimes`, `firstDrawTime`, `segmentsDrawn`, `pointsDrawn`, `dpr`, `error` (empty unless something failed; the test requires it empty). Nothing animates (A-9); there is no control. Deviation from the plan's wording: the plan puts `role="img"` and the `aria-label` on the canvas; svelte-check reports `a11y_no_interactive_element_to_noninteractive_role` for that, so they sit on the box that holds the canvas (the canvas itself carries no role). Without JavaScript the probe shows the SVG snapshot of the same picture, which the page renders at build time with the projector and `renderSvg` from the committed manifest and E8 file (read with `import.meta.glob` and `?raw`, server side only) and passes as the island's default slot (rendered once, not serialised into the island's props); the probe hides it when the canvas is drawn. The plan said `nojs.spec.ts` would not visit the page; it does (every route of the built site is discovered), and the page passes it, `a11y.spec.ts` and `worker-on-demand.spec.ts` (run filtered to this route). What the specification left open: the probe (plan 5.10). Default used: the plan's, with the role moved as said.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A4: D19 for the folded and the averaged names
Decision: the names are printed exactly as the engine gives them (`folded.name` from `fold`, `averagedRootsType(...).name`), so the tested elements `data-out="folded-name"` and `data-out="averaged-name"` read `B2`, `C3`, `G2`, `BC2` and so on (set with `<sub>`, `data-name` holding the plain name). The D19 equality "B2 = C2" stands in a sibling element: `data-out="folded-name-note"` on the fold tab when the folded name is `B2` (the flip of A3), and `data-out="averaged-name-note"` on the average tab when the averaged name is `B2`. `G2` (rotation of D4) and `BC2` (flip of A4) carry no note. The captions write "B2 = C2" for a rank 2 name recognised from its shape. The board picker shows the name the reader chose (A2 to E6; no rank 2 B or C board is offered). ## 2026-10-17 P4-A4: the symmetry picker, the default symmetry, the identity
Decision: `symmetries(board)` is called once per board (default limit); the picker lists every symmetry but the identity, in the engine's order (lexicographic in the image tuples), each shown by its orbits in labels with its order (`{1, 3} {2}, order 2`; option value the images joined by dots, the `y` form). The default symmetry is the first one listed: the flip on A_n and E6, the swap of the last two nodes on D5 to D8, the swap `1.2.4.3` on D4. On D4 the five are `1.2.4.3`, `3.2.1.4` (swaps), `3.2.4.1`, `4.2.1.3` (rotations of order 3, folding to G2) and `4.2.3.1` (swap): three swaps fold to C3 in three orbit orders, two rotations to G2 (the instruction's sentence lists the two rotations last; the engine's order puts `4.2.1.3` fourth). A link whose `y` is the identity loads the default state with the notice (plan: a symmetry the tool does not offer, by analogy with 6.6 "a board that the tool does not offer"). `fold` does not check that its permutation preserves the board (as the oracle), so the tool checks `C[s(i)][s(j)] = C[i][j]` itself before folding (a RangeError, which an author sees as a build error naming the instance; a link never reaches it, the codec's rule 7 refuses first). The picker of boards, the symmetry picker and the view switch each reset the start and the moves; the board picker also resets the symmetry to the new board's default. What the specification left open: the order and default. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.2).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A4: one entry per symmetric move in `moves`
Decision: a symmetric move is recorded as ONE entry of `moves`, the smallest label of the orbit acted on; on replay each entry expands to the whole orbit in increasing position (E-5), and any label of an orbit in `w` names that orbit and is written back as its smallest label (`/tools/fold?g=A3&w=3` is written back as `w=1`; `?g=D4&y=3.2.4.1&w=4.2` holds two symmetric moves, on `{1, 3, 4}` and on `{2}`, and is written back as `w=1.2`). So `data-moves`, the History strip, undo, redo and reset count symmetric moves, and the folded board's word is the same list read through the orbit map (folded position s is orbit s). This is the one place where a T11 link differs in meaning from a T1 link. What the specification left open: 6.6 defines `w` for single moves only. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.3), reported as a deviation for MERGE to confirm.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A4: views, coords, the default start, and starts that are not symmetric
Decision: T11 plays one game at a time: `view` is `populations` or `numbers` and `coords` always equals it (the start is a position of the game shown). Default state of `/tools/fold`: `{ schema: 1, tool: 'fold', board: 'A3', view: 'numbers', coords: 'numbers', start: [1, 1, 1], moves: [], symmetry: [3, 2, 1] }`, fold tab. The populations default start is one Martian in every city of the orbit of city 1 (the orbit sum, which is the folded board's "one Martian in the first city"): `(1, 0, 1)` on A3 with the flip, `(1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1)` on E6, `(1, 0, 0, 0)` on D4 with the swap `1.2.4.3`. Link rules (plan): `v` and `c` name one game; a link with only one of them sets both, a link with both that differ loads the defaults with the notice; a link without `s` takes the tool's default start for the board, view and symmetry in force (the codec's own fallback, one Martian in the first city, is not symmetric); a start that is not constant on the orbits of the symmetry loads the defaults with the notice (an author's such start fails the build naming the instance). What the specification left open: 6.6 lists the codec's failures; these are the tool's. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.3).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A4: links with `v=l` or `m` (plan rules, for MERGE to rule on)
Decision: `v=l` asks for the linked view, which T11 does not offer: the instance loads its default state with the notice that the link could not be read. An `m` whose value parses (`f`, `l` or `r`) is ignored: it is removed from the query before the codec reads the link (so neither T1's table of views and modes nor the replay of rule 6 can refuse it), the rest of the link is read, there is no notice, and the URL written back has no `m`. An `m` that does not parse (`m=z`) fails in the codec like any known key and gives the defaults with the notice. Tested in `T11.test.ts` and `T11.spec.ts`. What the specification left open: 6.6 says only "An unknown key is ignored", and `v` and `m` are known keys. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.3); reported under deviations and open questions.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A4: no symmetric play when the board does not fold
Decision: on A2, A4, A6 and A8 (the flip is the only symmetry and its middle orbit contains an edge) the fold tab shows, in place of the folded board, `data-out="fold-message"`: `This board does not fold by this symmetry: an orbit contains an edge. The orbit {2, 3} contains an edge.` (the engine's `reason`, made sure to carry the phrase whatever the engine writes, then the orbits that contain an edge, in labels). The big board is drawn with its orbits coloured; every node has `data-can-act="false"`; a click makes no move and announces the same message. A link with moves on such a board loads the defaults with the notice; an author's moves there fail the build. `fold`'s NeedsTwoWayRoads and NotFiniteType are never caught. What the specification left open: what the first tab does there. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.8).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A4: announcements of a symmetric move (deviation for MERGE to confirm)
Decision: one announcement per symmetric move, built in `t11/model.ts` from `speak` and the punctuation of A-4. An orbit of one node uses the A-4 template unchanged (`Fired node 2. Numbers now 2, minus 3, 2. Move 2.`). Several nodes, on boards with at most four nodes: `Fired nodes 1 and 3. Numbers now minus 1, 3, minus 1. Move 1.`, `Fired nodes 1, 3 and 4. Numbers now minus 1, 4, minus 1, minus 1. Move 1.`, `Mutated cities 1 and 3. Populations now minus 1, 0, minus 1. Move 1.`; above four nodes the changed-nodes form (`Fired nodes 1 and 5. Node 1 now minus 1, node 2 now 2, node 4 now 2, node 5 now minus 1. Move 1.`). A move that changes nothing on a board above four nodes says `... Nothing changed. Move k.` (plan: A-4's changed-nodes form would print an empty list). Undo uses `undid` with the big board's values (`Undid move 1. Numbers now 1, 1, 1.`); a redo or a scrub forward reads the move again; reset reads like an undo to the start. Only the big board's values are read; the folded board shows the same numbers. What the specification left open: A-4 fixes templates for one node only. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.6).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A4: the orbit colouring
Decision: decoration only, in an overlay drawn in the same box and grid units as `Board.svelte` (T9's overlay technique) and placed BEFORE the board in the page, so that the board's buttons and their focus ring are painted over it (A-2): an outer ring of radius 0.41 grid units around each node, stroked in `--edge-k`, and on the big board a badge (a small box outlined in the same colour) holding the folded label of the node's orbit as text, at the first of the corners bottom right, bottom left, top left that no road leaving the node points into (the top right holds the node's label). Colour k belongs to the orbit at folded label k, and folded node k has the same ring; when the board does not fold, colour k is the orbit at index k (orbit order, plan). Never the fill (6.3) and never an accent (8.3); no hex literal. The legend `data-out="orbits"` lists each orbit in labels with its folded node as text (`Orbit {1, 6}: folded node 1`), in folded label order. `Board.svelte`'s `decoration` prop is not read by Board (types.ts), hence the overlay. What the specification left open: ring, badge or decoration row. Default used: the plan's (either; ring plus badge chosen).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A4: the tab is outside the link; the preset `average`
Decision: the tab list is data (`t11/config.ts`: `fold`, `average`, and `golden` with `released: false`, rendered nowhere in phase 4); a WAI-ARIA tab list with Left, Right, Home and End, disabled until hydration. The tab is not part of a link in schema 1 (6.6), so "Copy link" on the average tab gives a link that opens the fold tab; no key was added and nothing is stored in localStorage. The preset `average` (A5 with the flip, numbers, all ones, average tab) is therefore a state object but not a link: its state fields go in the link, its tab does not. This is a conflict between 4.0 ("every preset is also a state object and a link") and 6.6 (the tab of T11 is not part of a link), left for MERGE or the owner. Decision: `symmetry`, `construction`, `big-board`, `folded-board`, `folded-name`, `folded-name-note`, `fold-message`, `orbits`, `averaged-name`, `averaged-name-note`, `averaged-classes`, plus ToolFrame's `caption`, `notice`, `noscript`, `exportNotice`, History's `moveCounter`, `historyStrip`, `historyCounter` and Predict's `predictResult`, `predictReveal`. ## 2026-10-17 P4-A4: where the replays run (E-9), and the worker's board
Decision: everything T11 computes on load or on a move runs on the main thread (symmetries, fold, identify, averagedRootsType, one engine call per board per symmetric move), except a list of moves read from a link whose big-board word (the expanded word) or folded word exceeds 2000 moves (E-9 rule 2). Hints, built in `t11/model.ts`: `playHint(board, n) = { board, kind: 'play', moves: n }` with n the expanded length for the big board and the number of symmetric moves for the folded board; on A3 with 1001 symmetric moves the big hint says 2002 (worker), with 1000 it says 2000 (main). When either goes to the worker, both replays go through `engineCall('positionsOf', [state], hint)` (the site's replay, which P1-A2 placed in the worker API "so that a long link replay runs in the worker") instead of `applyWord`, because `positionsOf` returns every position of the play, which the History strip and undo need (deviation from the plan's `engineCall('applyWord', ...)`, same rule and hints). The folded board is sent as its Cartan matrix in orbit order (a custom spec, labels 1..m following its positions), not by its name: `workerWire.specOf` serialises a named board by name, and `resolveBoard('G2')` would rebuild G2 with its positions in Bourbaki order, exchanging the two nodes of the rotation of D4. While the worker runs, both boards keep the start, every node has `data-can-act="false"`, the History and the pickers are disabled and nothing is announced; errors are not caught. Moves the reader makes afterwards are played one at a time on the main thread from the positions kept. A configuration given by an author's properties is replayed at once (at build time, where E-9 does not apply, and again at hydration); no default needs the worker. The averaged roots: `whereToRun({ board, kind: 'enumeration', finiteKnown: true, expectedItems: <roots> })` with the number of roots known in advance (A_n: n(n + 1), D_n: 2n(n - 1), E6: 72), always `main` (instruction 5.7). What the specification left open: E-9 names the cases, not the calls. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.12), with the positionsOf deviation.

"Download data" writes, beside the state: `view`, `symmetry` (`images`, `orbits` in labels, `order`), `folded` (`name`, `labels` of its rows, `cartan` in orbit order as the golden `folded_cartan`, `orbitsInBourbakiOrder`) or `null`, `foldMessage`, `averaged` (`name`, `classes`), `averagedSimpleCartan`, `bigPositions` and `foldedPositions` (every position up to the cursor, in label order; integers as JSON numbers when safe, else decimal strings). "Export SVG" and "Export PNG" are ToolFrame's, of the figure holding both boards. `quasi_split_real_form` (golden phase 6) is not shown or exported in phase 4. What the specification left open: the derived tables. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.10).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A4: repair after the wave 4.2 review, the random plays run through the tool's play path
Decision: the acceptance test `for every folding row with a folded board, 200 random symmetric plays agree between the two boards in both games` now drives `FoldBench`, the class `T11FoldingBench.svelte` plays with, instead of a separate `replay()` function that the component never called. Per row with a folded board, per view (`populations` plays mutation, `numbers` plays firing) and per play (200, the same mulberry32 generator and `SEED = 20261017`): `new FoldBench({ board, view, symmetry, start })` with a symmetric start drawn in [-9, 9] per orbit, then 1 to 12 clicks, each on a random node of either board as the component maps it (a big node at position p is `act(ctx.orbitOf[p])`, a folded node s is `act(s)`); after every click every node of every orbit in `bigValues()` equals `foldedValues()` at that orbit (`intEq` of the harness, on the decimal text read as bigint); at the end `state().moves` holds one entry per click, the orbit's smallest label; `foldedValues()` equals `applyWord` on the folded board of the clicked word (played on its own matrix, not copied); and the same moves read as a link (`new FoldBench({ ..., moves }, { defer: true })`, `needsWorker()` false, `replaySync()`) give the same positions after each move. `replay()` is removed from `t11/model.ts`: the plan's `replay` (both positions by `applyWord`) is `FoldBench.advance`, one `applyWord` per board per symmetric move, which clicks, main-thread link replays and the test share, so no second play path ships. Evidence: with `advance` firing only the first node of each orbit (`expandMove(this.ctx, s).slice(0, 1)`, the reviewer's break) the old test passed (1 passed, 29 skipped) and the new one fails (`A3 symmetry 3.2.1 mutation start -6,-2,-6 clicks folded:0: intEq failed`); with the folded board's move broken (`[0]` for `[s]`) it fails too; restored, all 30 unit tests pass. What the specification left open: nothing; SPEC 4 T11 acceptance and COMMON 4.3 (a test guards the tool's own code). Default used: none.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A3: the largest ring
Decision: a ring is an integer from 0 to `RING_MAX` = 10^6 - 1 (six digits, `CAPS.formFinderDigits`, the cap of an entry typed into T3); the ring buttons, the number fields of the table view and links are held to it. What the specification left open: SPEC says "a non-negative integer on each node". Reason: no orbit of the 32 boards then leaves `SafeInt` (the largest root coefficient is 6), so no link can make the engine throw `EngineOverflow`; the shape depends only on which nodes are ringed. Every value from 0 to `RING_MAX` is reachable without a mouse (the two ring buttons and the number fields).

## 2026-10-17 P4-A3: make uniform
Decision: the constant c is the largest ringed integer, so the picture keeps its size; the option is off by default and is not a link field. It is disabled with the sentence "Equal numbers on nodes of one length are uniform already." exactly when every ringed node has the same d_i and the same integer (`uniformMatters`; one ringed node; B3 (1,1,0)); with equal d_i and different integers it still acts (it makes them equal). The replay runs along the tree of `orbitGraph`: vertex k is `applyWordFloat` of its parent's real position by the one move that reached it, the same sequence of float operations as replaying `wordTo(graph, k)` from the start (unit test compares the two exactly). ## 2026-10-17 P4-A3: the move graph and its labels
Decision: the move graph joins mu to R_i mu for every node i with mu_i != 0, derived from the vertex list "once more" (5.4) by `t10/graphs.ts` with the engine's `fire`, deduplicated as sorted index pairs; for a preset it is read from the file's `moveAdjacency` (each pair's node found again with `fire`). Every drawn move-graph edge carries the label of its node as text, at every size (no threshold), on the canvas, in the SVG of the view and so in Export SVG and PNG: a numeral of 10 CSS pixels at the midpoint, in the text colour on a 3-pixel halo of the page colour (4.5 to 1 for numerals, A-6), drawn after the edges and points; the edge colour is `--edge-k` of the label (palette.ts `edgeColour`, 6.3); the depth cue acts on the edge width only (opacity 1), so no edge colour falls below its 3 to 1 against the page. A legend lists colour and label, and the table view lists each edge with its node (graphs of at most 300 edges). Where two edges cross at their midpoints (the two diagonals of the hexagon of A2) their labels overlap; nothing was thinned. Deviation from the plan's routing: the derivation is not sent to the worker above 2000 moves (the worker dispatches engine functions only, and no engine function computes a move graph); it runs on the main thread in slices of at most 2000 moves, one task each.

## 2026-10-17 P4-A3: the snapshot without JavaScript, and the SVG of the view
Decision: during server rendering only (`import.meta.env.SSR`), the component computes the configured state in-process (`orbitGraph`, `wythoffEdges`, the move graph when it is the graph shown; E-9 at build time), projects it with the configured projection in a 360 by 360 box with the depth cue as the view asks, and renders it with P4-A2's `renderSvg` (polytope graph) or `t10/drawing.ts` `pictureSvg` (move graph with labels), with the colour tokens, a `<title>` naming the board, the rings, the counts and the polytope name in plain words, `role="img"`, inside `data-out="snapshot"`. In the browser the first value of that `{@html}` block is a placeholder string, so Svelte 5's hydration adopts the server's SVG nodes without recomputing them (no enumeration at hydration). The figure box is a square reserved in CSS (`aspect-ratio: 1`, at most 480 pixels), so the canvas replaces the snapshot without shift once the configured orbit is complete; after any change the canvas shows what is known at once (vertices while the edges come, an empty box for a refused or waiting orbit), so a picture of another state never stands in for the current one. The SVG stays under the canvas and is rewritten 400 ms after the reader's changes at rest (not at load), so that ToolFrame's Export SVG and PNG take the current view with the labels. The showpiece snapshot in the built HTML holds 240 circles and 6720 segments. What the specification left open: the mechanism. Default used: the plan's (5.11).

Decision: board names come from `site/src/generated/names.json` (KaTeX's markup with MathML, written by `scripts/names.mjs` at the start of every build) through `t10/typesetNames.ts` and `import.meta.glob`, which is empty when the file is absent (unit tests and the type check run before any build in CI): in-process during server rendering, so the HTML of every instance carries KaTeX's markup; in the browser the module is fetched when the reader first leaves the configured board (until then hydration keeps the server's markup), and where it is not loaded the name is written as plain MathML `<msub><mi>E</mi><mn>8</mn></msub>`, as T4 and T16 do. The module is not named after KaTeX, so that no script whose name says katex is ever requested; KaTeX is never imported by client code. Polytope names exist only for the 26 golden `wythoff` records, typed from their `name` fields into `t10/names.ts` (a unit test checks the table equals the file); each `p_qr` becomes MathML `<msub><mn>p</mn><mn>qr</mn></msub>` and each board name inside one a board name; "rectified 4_21" is not in the table. Text that cannot hold markup (aria-labels, the live region, the canvas, the snapshot's title, the export footer) uses plain words and digits: `E8`, `polytope 4 21`. Captions are ToolFrame's plain text props and name boards as `A3`, `E8`. No request to extend `names.json` was needed.

Decision: the face table (HTML, in the figure, rendered without JavaScript) lists, for each dimension 0 to n - 1, a total row and one row per face type K (its nodes as labels; "none (vertices)" for the empty set) with its count as the engine's bigint in full digits; the full node set (dimension n, count 1, the polytope itself) is not a row, so the totals are the n entries of the golden `f_vector`. ## 2026-10-17 P4-A3 (repair, wave 4.3): T10's main-thread work in tasks of its own (7.6)
Decision: every piece of T10's main-thread work after hydration runs in a macrotask of its own (`t10/studio.ts` `nextTask`, a message to a channel of its own, so no clamp of nested timers). A link is read one task after hydration (the colours of the drawing are read first in that task, while the layout is still the one hydration found, so that the first drawing forces no style and layout). A change (a link, the back button, a ring, the picker, the shortcut, undo, redo, reset) goes through `request`: the ring board, the picker and the ring table show the configuration asked for (`target`) at once; its facts are computed by `prepareInTasks`, one task each: the verdict of `classify` the first time on a board, the counts (`orbitSize`, `wythoffFVector`), the face table (`wythoffFaceTypes`), the other facts (golden name, short roots, make uniform), the vertices when they belong on the main thread; then, in one more task, the change becomes `current` (figure, counts, face table) and its orbit loads. The load runs the data file's reading and its drawing in two tasks, and `enumerateInTasks` runs the vertices, `wythoffEdges` alone, and the index pairs with the drawing, one task each; the move graph is derived in slices of at most 2000 moves, the first in a task after the one that completed the orbit (`t10/moves.ts` `deriveInTasks`, there so that the route's first scripts do not carry it). One board object per name (`t10Board`), so that the engine's verdict of `classify` (kept per object, E-11) is found by every later guard; the short roots once per board. The figure no longer redraws when the move graph is added to the data while the polytope graph is shown. A newer change stops the work of an older one at its next task. What the specification left open: how the work is scheduled. Reason: the gaps of the wave 4.3 review (the E8 loads were one task of 68 to 245 ms on this container, and a ring click on B6 node 4 ran `wythoffEdges`, the index pairs, two drawings and the move graph in one task). Measured on this container (4 processors, load average 5 to 18 from other agents) with Chrome traces, thread time of the largest task, four runs each on a warm cache: before, E8 refusal link 39 to 77 ms, showpiece link 47 to 75 ms, B6 ring click 28 to 41 ms; after, 16 to 23 ms, 16 to 20 ms, 18 to 29 ms. Decision: the reviewer's gap is real, and both predictions are replaced. (1) The question on `b4` asked how many vertices A3 has with nodes 1 and 3 ringed, but the table of solids sat above `b4` with the row (1, 0, 1), cuboctahedron, (12, 24, 14), and `b2` in beat 1 already showed A3 at (1, 0, 1) with 12 vertices and the name cuboctahedron. (2) The question on `b6` asked whether the two graphs share their edges, but its own figure prints "Shared with the other graph: 4" and six edges from the start, its graph switch (`graphMoves`) stays enabled while the prediction is open (T10 disables only the ring board, the picker and the ring buttons on `frozen`), and the prose and caption just above state six and four. What changed: `b4` now asks "If nodes 2 and 3 are ringed as well, how many vertices will the orbit have?" (answer `wythoff[type=A3;rings=1,1,1].f_vector[0]`, 24, through `gv`; the reveal explains that U is empty, so there is one vertex per element of the Weyl group, and names the polytope through `fmt`), and the table of solids moved from the prose of beat 2 into its figure column, after `b4`, as `<figure data-figure="solids">` with a figcaption (the pattern of M6's `roots-compared`, with M2's `margin: 0 16px` so it keeps the prose gutter on a phone). `b6` carries no prediction. The second prediction is on `b7` ("predict a yes or no"): "Rings on nodes 2 and 3 of B3 give edges of two lengths. If node 1 is ringed as well, will every edge have the same length?"; the correct option is computed from `types.B3.symmetrizer` as the number of distinct values of 2 d_i a_i^2 over the ringed nodes of (1, 1, 1) (4 and 2, so "No, two lengths"), and the reveal prints those values. Both questions are about a configuration that the reader reaches only by clicking nodes, and the ring board stays frozen until the reader answers or presses "Show me", so neither figure shows its answer while the question is open; nothing above `b7` states the edge lengths of (1, 1, 1) (the table of solids gives rings, names and face counts only). Reason: SPEC 8.1 P5 ("ask for a prediction before a reveal") and 8.5. Tests: `M7.spec.ts > a prediction asks about what is not yet on screen` (new: exactly `b4` and `b7` hold predictions; `b6` prints its shared edges at load with the graph switch enabled; for each prediction no row of the table of solids that would state the answer, no tool on that board with the target rings and no name of the target polytope comes before the question; the board is frozen at its start; after a right answer the reader's clicks reach the target and the figure shows the answer), and the updated `> predictions show a details fallback without JavaScript`, `> a prediction freezes its board until answered`, `> renders without JavaScript ...` (the table of solids follows `b4`, inside a figure of beat 2) and `> every figure states its expected result` (no "Show me" on `b6`; "Show me" on `b7` before its checks). Against the build of the branch as P4-A6 left it, these five tests failed; a temporary copy of the new test with the old question's target (A3 (1, 0, 1)) reported `rows: ["A3:1,0,1"], figures: ["b2"], named: ["cuboctahedron"]`, the three giveaways above; after the change all 25 tests of `M7.spec.ts` pass. ## 2026-10-17 P4-X2: the timing configuration and the one command
Decision: `site/tests/timing/vitest.config.ts` (project name `site-timing`) sets `root` to the repository, `include: ['site/tests/timing/**/*.timing.test.ts']`, `environment: 'node'` and `fileParallelism: false` (one file at a time; Vitest then uses one worker), and takes its `resolve.alias` from the `site-unit` project of the root `vitest.config.ts` (it imports that file and throws if the project or its aliases are missing), so `@engine`, `@components` and `@lib` resolve in both runs from one definition. The root `vitest.config.ts` is not changed: its `site-unit` project includes only `site/tests/unit/**/*.test.ts` and its other project is `packages/engine`, so `npm test` does not collect a timing file. Root `package.json` gains `"bench": "npm run bench -w packages/engine && vitest run --config site/tests/timing/vitest.config.ts"`: the 25 ms orbit benchmark of SPEC 7.6 first (P3-A2's `packages/engine/test/bench/vitest.config.ts`, unchanged), then the site's timing files, each run alone. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` gains the step `Timing checks, run alone` (`npm run bench`) right after `Type-check and test` (`npm run check`), so the benchmark that SPEC 7.6 asks to fail above 25 ms now runs on the runner (CI did not run it before). What the specification left open: the wiring of the benchmark and of the tools' main-thread bounds (7.6 names only the benchmark and its bound). Default used: the orchestrator's pre-approved script and step. Reason: one command runs every timing check alone, locally and in CI, and a failing timing check shows as its own CI step instead of inside the unit suite. The aliases are read rather than copied so that the two runs cannot drift apart.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-engine: the order of the guards of affineExtension (P3-RT-03-06)
Decision: `affineExtension` checks the kind of board (`NeedsTwoWayRoads`), then the class (`NotFiniteType` on every board that is not of finite type, in one piece or several), then connectedness (`NeedsConnectedBoard`, reached only by a finite board in several pieces). What the specification left open: SPEC 5.6 gives `affineExtension` `NotFiniteType` on every `gcm` board that is not of finite type and does not list it among the functions that need a connected board (E-10 names only `cartanClass`, `identify`, `identifyAffine`); it says nothing about a finite board in several pieces. Default used (SPEC section 10): none. The P2-A1 entries "`requireFinite` on a disconnected board" (connectedness for `affineExtension`, stated gap: a disconnected finite board) and "the order of checks inside each function" (connectedness "where required" before class) are kept for the case they were written for; for a board that is not of finite type the order now follows the 5.6 row, as the opening paragraph of COMMON.md requires when the plan and SPEC.md seem to disagree. Reason: SPEC 5.6 row `affineExtension` and E-10; the guard order of `guards.ts` (`requireFinite` itself checks kind, then class). The assertion of `guards.test.ts` row 8 that pinned `NeedsConnectedBoard` on the board "two components: A2 and the triangle" now asserts `NotFiniteType`; the finite board in several pieces keeps its `NeedsConnectedBoard` assertion in row 10.
