## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-engine: request, the return type of symbolicPlay (P3-RT-01-01, needs-decision)
Decision: no source change; the request below is for the owner or `MERGE`. What the specification left open: CONTRACTS.md 2.4 phase 3 fixes `symbolicPlay(board, word): number[][]`, while SPEC 5.6 (second table, first row) says `symbolicPlay` works on one-way boards and on `gcm` boards that are not of finite type, and E-2 gives those boards `Big` because their entries grow without bound. On `[[2,-3],[-3,2]]` in `Big` the oracle's `symbolic_play` returns `(23416728348467685, 8944394323791464)` at move 40, which a `number` cannot hold; the engine throws `EngineOverflow` (the plan reading recorded as "P3-A2: the overflow rule of symbolicPlay"). Default used (SPEC section 10): none. Options: (a) CONTRACTS.md 2.4 becomes `symbolicPlay(board: Board<number>, word): number[][]; symbolicPlay(board: Board<bigint>, word): bigint[][]; symbolicPlay(board: AnyBoard, word): number[][] | bigint[][]` (the forms in the board's arithmetic, as the preamble of 2.4 says of vectors); a prototype made the reproducer pass with the engine type-check clean, and needs two follow-on edits: `packages/engine/test/golden/p3b-kinds.test.ts` (two tests on `Big` boards expect numbers, for example `[[1, 0], [1, 1]]`, and would expect `[[1n, 0n], [1n, 1n]]`) and `site/src/components/tools/T07SymbolicGame.svelte` lines 155 and 156 (`symbolicView` passes the result to `matchRows` and stores it as `number[][]`; T7 offers only the 32 named types, so a narrowing to `Board<number>` suffices); (b) keep `number[][]` and the owner amends the first row of the second table of SPEC 5.6 to say that `symbolicPlay` throws `EngineOverflow` when a coefficient passes 2^53, after which the reproducer is rewritten to expect the throw. Reason for recommending (a): E-2 gives these boards `Big` so that exact values survive, the oracle returns them at every length, and the only reader path (T7 on named finite boards) keeps its numbers.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-garden-follow: where the phase-3 orbit total lives (P3-RT-01-02, P3-RT-03-02, P3-RT-06-01)
Decision: the rule of SPEC 4 T2 Interactions "from phase 3 on a finite-type board it gives the exact size from `orbitSize`" is applied in `gardenTotal` (`site/src/components/tools/t02/phase2.ts`), not in `totalOf` (`t02/garden.ts`) as the P1-A6 entry "counter without a total" foresaw ("`totalOf` is the one function phase 3 changes for `orbitSize`"). What the specification left open: the file. Reason: the finite test from phase 2 is the verdict of `classify` (SPEC 5.6), which P2-A7 placed in `phase2.ts` beside the roots total; `totalOf` keeps the phase-1 answer of the bounded search, which `gardenTotal` returns off the finite types. The component already calls `gardenTotal` for the counter and its announcement. The comment of `totalOf` now points there.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-garden-follow: an orbit size beyond the safe integers
Decision: when `orbitSize` throws `EngineOverflow` (its group order is formed in SafeInt; on twelve nodes it fits, E-4, but a named board such as `A20` reached by a link has an order beyond 2^53), the counter gives what the bounded search gives ("more than 2000", or the count when the search completed). What the specification left open: SPEC 4 T2 names no case where `orbitSize` cannot answer. Default used: none in section 10 applies. Reason: the statement stays true and no number is rounded (E-1); the `Total` type of T2 holds a `number`.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-garden-follow: a population's orbit size (P3-RT-01-02)
Decision: in the mutation game the orbit of a population p is measured by `orbitSize` of its numbers a = Cp (`toNumbers`). What the specification left open: SPEC 5.4 gives `orbitSize` on positions of the numbers game only. Reason: a mutation changes Cp exactly as the firing of that node changes a (SPEC 2.4), and C is invertible on a finite-type board, so the two orbits have the same size (the oracle agrees: `orbit_size(C, -end)` for the A6 population (2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 8) is 2520).

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-garden-follow: followers keep the followed play (P3-RT-04-04)
Decision: a T2 or T3 following a T1 through `linkTo` keeps the positions of the followed play and, on each published state with the same board, coords and start, applies only the moves after the longest shared prefix (`extendPlay` in `t02/follow.ts`, `followPlay` in `t03/model.ts`); another board, coords or start is a load, replayed from the start. Both subscriptions run untracked inside their effect. This supersedes, on this point, the P2-A2 entry "the meter reads `positionsOf` of the last published state" and the reading of the P1-A2 entry "a follower recomputes its own positions" as a replay per move; positions still never travel between tools. What the specification left open: nothing (SPEC 7.4 "extends it by one position per move"); recorded because two builder entries said otherwise. Reason: SPEC 7.4; E-9 rule 2.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-board-a11y: a frozen board stays one tab stop (P3-RT-05-02)
Decision: after hydration the `disabled` prop of `Board.svelte` no longer sets the HTML `disabled` attribute on the node buttons; it sets `aria-disabled="true"`, and activating a node calls no `onAct`. The roving tab stop, the arrow keys, the A-3 names (`cannot be fired` and the city states) and `data-can-act="false"` stay as they were, so a reader on the keyboard reaches the board and its values while the prediction waits, and no move is made. Before hydration the buttons are still rendered with `disabled` (7.4). The same holds while a tool passes `disabled` for a running play (`busy` in T1 and T9). What the specification left open: what "frozen" means for the board (4.0 Predict); A-1 and 4.0 "Each board is one tab stop" fix that the board keeps its tab stop. This replaces the words "and disabled" in the entry "2026-10-10 P1-A5: prediction check" for the node buttons; History and the step controls stay disabled while frozen. Reason: SPEC 7.5 A-1, 4.0 Keyboard and screen reader, 4.0 Predict, 7.4. No prop or hook name changed (CONTRACTS 5.1).

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-board-a11y: T16's import status spoken through the frame's region (P3-RT-05-07)
Decision: `data-out="importStatus"` (T16) and `data-out="counterStatus"` (T4) are ordinary text without `role="status"`, so each tool has the one polite live region of A-4, ToolFrame's `[data-live]`. T16BoardIO takes an optional `announce` prop (a component inside T16, not a contract of CONTRACTS 5) and speaks each status line through it; T16Sandbox passes `FrameApi.announce`. T4 already announced "Counting in the background." through the frame, so its line only loses the role. The wording recorded by P2-A5 ("The board could not be read: <reason>. The board was left as it was." and "Board imported: N nodes. The play starts again from the default start.") and both `data-out` names are unchanged; the parenthesis "(role status, ordinary text, no announcement of my own)" of the entry "2026-10-10 P2-A5: JSON import and export of boards" now reads "(ordinary text, announced through the tool's live region)". What the specification left open: nothing; A-4 fixes one polite live region per tool and 4.0 has that region announce each result. Reason: SPEC 7.5 A-4, 4.0 Keyboard and screen reader, CONTRACTS 5.1 ToolFrame.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-layout: which of the two edge-to-edge rules a lesson's tool figure keeps (P3-RT-05-01)
Decision: below 400 pixels Lesson.astro runs a figure at `100vw` only when the figure holds no ToolFrame (`[data-anatomy='figure']:not(:has([data-frame]))`); a figure that holds a tool stays in the page column and ToolFrame alone moves the tool's `<figure>` out by the page gutter, exactly as on the tool routes. The tool's title, controls and share row then keep the page gutter on lessons too. Static figures keep the `100vw` rule of decisions/P1-A4.md. A browser without `:has()` drops the whole rule, so its static figures stay in the column and no page scrolls sideways (the other order, an override that undoes the 100vw rule for tools, would bring the double breakout back in such a browser). What the specification left open: SPEC 6.1 [D] says only that the box runs from edge to edge below 400 pixels; the finding offered either rule. Default used: none (6.1 applied as written; decisions/P0-A5.md "negative margins equal to the page gutter" and decisions/P1-A4.md "100vw below 400 pixels" both still hold, each for its own kind of figure). Reason: the gutter-based rule is exact (`100vw` also counts a classic scrollbar), and it keeps lessons and tool routes alike.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-layout: the width of a number prediction's answer field (P3-RT-05-01)
Decision: Predict.svelte gives the answer field of a number question `width: 8em` (class `number`), the width T05 had set locally for the same reason. With the browser's default width (about 20 characters) the label and the field could not be narrower than about 323 pixels, so a tool with a prediction was 349 pixels wide; this was hidden on lessons while the figure was 352 pixels wide and failed the adopted test once the figure was 320. Position answers keep `size="4"`. What the specification left open: the field's width. Default used: none. Reason: A-11 (controls reflow at 320), 4.0 "Small screens".

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-layout: a lesson's Sources entries wrap long tokens (P3-RT-05-01)
Decision: Sources.astro sets `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on each entry, as Page.astro already does for the credits table. The W-MS entry holds the unbroken file name `MutationGameCoxeterGraphs.pdf`, which reached x = 326 at 320 pixels on M0, M1, M3, M4 and M5; like the Predict field it was hidden inside the wider figure and surfaced with the fix. What the specification left open: nothing beyond A-11. Reason: A-11.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-layout: every display formula of <Tex> is a tab stop (P3-RT-05-04)
Decision: Tex.astro adds `tabindex="0"` to the outer `<span class="katex-display">` of every display formula it typesets, and base.css gives it the focus ring of A-2. No role and no accessible name are added: on focus a screen reader reads the MathML inside (A-12), which an `aria-label` would replace. Every display box is a stop, not only those that scroll, because which formulas overflow depends on the reader's width and fonts and the layouts ship no script (P1-A4); this follows the scroll boxes of T7 (decisions/P3-A5.md, `tabindex="0"`). The build fails if KaTeX's display output no longer starts with that span, so that the stop cannot vanish silently on a KaTeX upgrade. Not taken: a script that marks only overflowing boxes (a script on every lesson); splitting the one formula of M2 beat 2 (the content would fit, the cause would stay). What the specification left open: how a scrolling formula is made keyboard operable (A-11, WCAG 2.1.1). Default used: none. Reason: SPEC 7.7 (no serious axe violation), A-11.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-layout: display formulas reflow at their break points, on every page (P3-RT-05-11)
Decision: the rule `.katex-display { overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: hidden }` moves from Lesson.astro and Page.astro to base.css, which every page loads, and display formulas may break between the pieces KaTeX already makes at the relations and binary operators of a formula's outer level (`.katex-display > .katex > .katex-html { white-space: normal }`), as TeX breaks an inline formula; a piece still wider than the column scrolls inside the formula's own box. The break is needed, not only the box: a formula written with `$$` goes through rehype-katex, cannot carry the tab stop of `<Tex display>`, and with the box alone a11y.spec.ts reported scrollable-region-focusable (serious) on /dev/math-check/ at 360. Wider than the column and without a break point, a `$$` formula would still be a box without a tab stop; giving those a stop needs a rehype step, which changes the mathematics route of decisions/P0-A3.md (left to the owner, see the report's open questions). What the specification left open: how a display formula reflows (A-11). Default used: none. Reason: A-11 on every route, SPEC 7.7.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-drawing: how the `roads` style draws more roads than the editor allows
Decision: `roadGlyphs` (site/src/components/draw/roads.ts) draws every road as its own curved arrow up to `CAPS.roadsEachWay` (4) roads in one direction, as before. A direction with more roads is drawn as one arrow (the first curve of that direction) with its count written beyond the apex in `var(--text)`, glyph kind `counted`. A pair therefore has at most 2 x 4 glyphs whatever its counts. What the specification left open: 6.2 [D] says that in the `roads` style "every road is drawn as its own curved arrow", and 5.6 caps the roads between two nodes at 4 each way in the editor only ("the engine accepts any count"); neither says how a board from outside the editor (a link with a `c:` matrix, which the codec accepts with any safe count) is drawn. Followed literally, 6.2 drew 2^53 - 1 arrows and hung the page (P3-RT-03-01). Reason: the orchestrator's direction for this cluster (the drawing must be bounded); the threshold is the editor's cap, so 6.2 holds unchanged for every board the editor, a preset or the golden file can produce (at most 4 roads each way), and the device for "too many to draw" is the one 6.2 already uses for the thick line of the `dynkin` style, which writes the counts as numbers. The `dynkin` style is unchanged (its glyphs were bounded already).

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-drawing: T16's import refuses more than four roads each way
Decision: the JSON import of the sandbox (T16BoardIO.svelte, `customSpec`) refuses a custom board with more than `CAPS.roadsEachWay` roads from one node to another, after the checks P2-A5 recorded, with the reason "it has N roads from node A to node B, and the editor allows at most 4 each way" inside P2-A5's sentence "The board could not be read: <reason>. The board was left as it was." The labels are the board's (`toLabels`, E-7). This extends the list of refusals in decisions/P2-A5.md ("JSON import and export of boards") by one item; nothing else of that entry changes, and the BoardEditor contract of decisions/P2-A3.md (props, `maxRoads` at most 4, the road selects 0 to 4) is untouched. What the specification left open: whether the editor's cap of 5.6 applies to an import. Reason: SPEC 4 T16 makes the sandbox "The editor of T4", T4's editor has "between two nodes, 0 to 4 roads each way", and 6.6 Validation refuses "a board that the tool does not offer"; both verifiers of P3-RT-03-01 read the texts the same way.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-codec-state: the 12-node cap on board names (P3-RT-04-01)
Decision: `resolveBoard` (site/src/lib/state.ts) refuses every board with more than 12 nodes, named or custom, with the RangeError "board has more than 12 nodes" that a custom matrix already got. A finite name (`A13`) and an untwisted affine name (`A12~`) are refused from their text (rank, plus one for `~`) before `boardFromName` builds a matrix, so that a 512-character name such as `A999...9` cannot freeze the tab; every other name (twisted, `pentagon`, `square`) is checked on the board built, which the engine bounds at 13 nodes. The codec turns the error into rule 2 as before; T16's import of a name above the cap gives the error's text as its reason ("The board could not be read: board has more than 12 nodes. The board was left as it was.") instead of "no board is named". What the specification left open: nothing on the rule (SPEC 6.6 Validation applies the 12 nodes to every board; CONTRACTS 4); the wording of T16's reason is plan wording. Reason: SPEC 6.6, 2.8 scope, CONTRACTS 4 resolveBoard comment.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-codec-state: a T5 link whose lambda the calculator cannot take (P3-RT-04-03)
Decision: a T5 link whose `d` parses but has a negative entry or an entry of more than 6 digits loads the whole default state with the notice, as every other link T5 cannot read does. This replaces the part of the entry "P3-A3: legal play only, and the link rules" (decisions/P3-A3.md) that kept the link's board, start and moves, reset lambda and showed the notice. What the specification left open: SPEC 6.6 allows only two outcomes, the whole link with no notice or the whole default state with the notice; the finding's two options were these. Default used: the second, because it keeps P3-A3's recorded rule that such a `d` is a link T5 cannot read (and its cap of 6 digits on a link), keeps every existing T5 test green (`a link is read with the legal rule and the lambda cap`), and needs no new behaviour in the calculator for a lambda it refuses. Reason: SPEC 6.6 Validation; finding P3-RT-04-03.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-codec-state: one board object per spec while a tool loads (P3-RT-03-05)
Decision: `resolveBoard` keeps the boards it builds in a map from the spec (a name, or the matrix as JSON; `xy` does not count) to the board object, and empties the map in a microtask queued when the first board of a run of synchronous code is stored. A tool loads its board in one such run (its script and its first render), so every `resolveBoard` of one spec in that load returns one frozen object and the verdict cache (keyed by object, E-11) is hit: one `classify` per load. What the specification left open: the scope of the reuse (SPEC 5.6 says "once when the board is loaded"; E-11 keys the cache by board object). Not chosen: a map kept for the life of the page, which the orchestrator's note suggested ("one board object per spec"). It would make the adopted reproducer read 0 calls instead of 1 for the triangle, which `t02/presets.ts` resolves when the module loads, so the reproducer (unchanged, as RT-FIX 5.3 requires) could not pass; it would also need a bound of its own choosing on the number of boards kept. Consequence for an existing test: `site/tests/unit/tools/T04.test.ts > T4 verdict > buildVerdict calls classify once per board object` obtained a second board object by resolving the same spec again in the same synchronous run, which now returns the same object; the test now awaits the end of the run first (`await Promise.resolve()`), and its assertion (`not.toBe(first)`) is unchanged. Reason: SPEC 5.6 last sentence, E-11; finding P3-RT-03-05.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-codec-state: the values of T9's caption of 2.12 (P3-RT-02-02)
Decision: T9's `EndPanel` (site/src/components/tools/t09/kostant.ts) gains two fields, `markedNumbers` and `markedReturnCounts`: the final number and the return count of each marked city, in the order of `marked`, read by `endPanel` at the position `toPositions` gives. `affineCaptionParts` pairs them with the marked labels instead of reading index `label - 1` of a list in label order. The data export of T9 names its fields one by one, so it does not change. What the specification left open: the shape of a tool's internal module (plan). Reason: E-7, "nothing else converts"; finding P3-RT-02-02.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-export-long: a rational whose denominator is 1 is an integer in the data export
Decision: `jsonSafe` in `site/src/lib/export.ts` hands the numerator of a `{ num, den: 1n }` rational to the integer rule of SPEC 6.6, so it is a JSON number when safe and decimal text otherwise; a fraction stays `p/q`. This replaces the words "`{ num, den }` rationals become `p/q` or `p`" of the entry "2026-10-10 P1-A2: data export". What the specification left open: whether an integral rational counts among the "integers" of 6.6 (SPEC 5.3 types the form values and the d_i as rationals, and 5.7 rule 4 stores the golden `form_value` as text, but that rule governs `golden_data.json`, not the export). Default used: none of section 10; the reading of the round's orchestrator ("rationals with denominator 1 are integers") and of the entry "2026-10-10 P1-A5: Download data" (safe integers as numbers, fractions as `p/q`). Reason: P3-RT-04-02, confirmed by both verifiers.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-export-long: tools hand values, not display text, to the export
Decision: T3, T4 and T6 convert the exact texts they show back to export values at their `derivedForExport` boundary: an integer text by the integer rule (T3 and T6 through their existing `exportValue`, T4 through `integerOut` of `lib/state.ts`), a fraction text as `p/q`. T3's small values export a typed whole number as that integer and an unfinished entry (empty, or a lone minus sign) as its text, which is not an integer. The display texts and every hook are unchanged. Reason: P3-RT-04-05 and the T6 half of P3-RT-04-02 (SPEC 6.6).

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-export-long: existing expectations that recorded the old export
Decision: two assertions written before the round expected integers as text and were changed to the integer rule: `site/tests/unit/export.test.ts` (`{ num: -4n, den: 1n }` exports as `-4`, was `'-4'`) and `site/tests/e2e/T04.spec.ts` (the star's weights export as `1`, was `'1'`). Both stay exact comparisons. Reason: they encoded the behaviour the two findings report; no assertion was removed or loosened.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-export-long: T5's long dimension (SPEC 4.0 Long numbers)
Decision: above 12 digits `data-out="dimension"` shows T1's `shortValue` (`1.0000... x 10^120 (121 digits)`), with the exact digits in its `title` (the tooltip), in the table view (the M / D cell, now marked `data-table-exact="dimension"` beside the existing `D` and `M`) and in the export (unchanged, a decimal string). In the MathML formula a long dimension is the same shortened text in an `<mtext>` (it is not a numeral); up to 12 digits it stays an `<mn>`. The live region's sentence `Dimension N.` keeps the exact digits: the live region is visually hidden and the A-4 sentences speak exact values, so nothing is "shown" there. What the specification left open: how a formula and a spoken sentence carry a long number. Reason: P3-RT-03-03.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-test-integrity: a scroll is not the first interaction for the worker check
Decision: `worker-on-demand.spec.ts` scrolls every island still waiting into view, in document order, and waits until Astro has hydrated it (`site/tests/e2e/hydrate.ts`), before it reads the worker requests; a scripted scroll is not counted as the reader's first interaction. What the specification left open: 7.6 [D] says the islands other than the first hydrate "when scrolled into view (client:visible)" and that the worker's script "is fetched when a tool first needs it. No tool may need it for its default state" (E-9 repeats the last sentence); it does not say whether a scroll is an interaction. Default used: none of section 10; the reading of P3-RT-06-02, which both verifiers accepted: the rule covers every tool of the page, not only those of the first screen. Reason: a client:visible island hydrates into its default state when it is scrolled into view and acts on nothing. The budget of `npm run size` ("without touching the page") is not changed by this: it still measures only what is fetched before any scroll. This replaces the comment of P1-A2's spec ("the others wait for a scroll, which would be touching the page"), which no decisions entry recorded.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-test-integrity: the worker check waits for the tools of an island
Decision: after the scroll, `worker-on-demand.spec.ts` waits for `data-hydrated="true"` on every tool root inside an `astro-island`, and fails when an island keeps the attribute `ssr`. What the specification left open: nothing; the test's own wording ("left alone until every tool has hydrated"). Reason: the stand-in root of `dev/lesson-check` (MERGE, phase 1 stage 1.1) is static markup, not an island, so nothing hydrates it; the previous spec asked `data-hydrated` only of the tools in the first screen, which the stand-in is not in.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-test-integrity: the default figure of the run without JavaScript
Decision: `nojs.spec.ts` accepts as the default figure of a tool root only the tool's own drawing, outside the table view's `<details>` and any `<noscript>`: a board (a `data-board-group` holding `data-node` buttons, drawn by an `<svg>` with content beside it), a drawing of role `img` with content and a name (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or `<title>`), or a snapshot `<img>` with a source and an `alt`. Any other `<svg>` (a decorative icon) no longer counts. Every node button of a game board carries the four hooks of 4.0 with a non-empty `data-value`; the nodes of the board editor (inside `data-editor`), which show no value (their `data-value` is empty by design), are left out of that check. A prediction's `<details>` must hold a non-empty `.answer-text` (the answer, as the lesson specs read it) and a non-empty reveal. What the specification left open: 7.4 asks the run to check that "every default figure" is present, and 4.0 Predict that the `<details>` holds "the answer and the reveal"; neither names a selector. This strengthens the predicate recorded in "2026-10-10 P1-A2: the run without JavaScript" (a builder's record, not a [D] choice or a default of section 10, as the refuting verifier of P3-RT-06-03 found). Reason: P3-RT-06-03. The entries of DECISIONS.md that made T2's one-vertex garden and T3's linked meter pass the old predicate stay satisfied: both tools have a named drawing of role `img` (the layer chart, the meter dial).

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-test-integrity: the default state's values, server markup against the hydrated default
Decision: a sweep test in `nojs.spec.ts`, "the server markup shows the default state's values", compares, for every route and every tool root, the hooks read without JavaScript with those of the hydrated default (every island scrolled into view through `hydrate.ts`, nothing clicked, polled until equal): `data-moves`, the four node hooks of every `data-node`, the caption, and on the tools of ToolFrame (`data-frame`) the text of every `data-out`, all outside `<noscript>`. A root outside ToolFrame is compared without its `data-out`. What the specification left open: how the run checks that "the default state of every tool is rendered to HTML and SVG at build time" (4.0). Reason: P3-RT-06-03 ("it checks that elements exist, not the default state") and its proposed fix. The drawing-time probe of `dev/draw-time` (P4-A2's entry; not a tool of section 4, no `data-frame`) fills its timing outputs only when it hydrates, by design, so outputs are compared on the tools of ToolFrame only.

Move 1."; recommendation: omit the empty clause), P3-RT-05-09 (answering a prediction drops the focus to the body; recommendation: aria-disabled on the controls that are done), P3-RT-05-10 (T7's Letters panel of the numbers game carries the Populations icon; recommendation: the Numbers icon and accent).

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-lesson-m3: how M3 quotes Donnelly and Eriksson's theorem
Decision: beat 7 reads "a connected board with roads both ways is of finite type exactly when its numbers game ends from some start with a positive number and no negative one [DE08] (Theorem 2.1)". This is SOURCES.md's record of the theorem ("a connected integer-weighted graph has a terminating game from some nonzero dominant start exactly when it is a Dynkin diagram of finite type") in the site's words: the integer-weighted graphs of [DE08] carry an amplitude in each direction of every edge, so they are the boards with roads both ways of SPEC 2.11 (on the board with one road of `one_way_counterexample` the game from (1, 0) ends after two moves, and that board is not of finite type); [DE08] fires positive numbers with a = lambda (SPEC 2.9), so a dominant start is one with no negative number (Appendix C), and a nonzero one has a positive number. What the specification left open: the wording (SPEC 3 M3 beat 7 prescribes none). Reason: finding P3-RT-09-01.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-pages: what a Sources list and a Cite title print (P3-RT-08-03)
Decision: `citeTitle(k)` in `site/src/lib/sources.ts`, which both `<Cite>` (link title) and `Sources.astro` (the text after each key) use, now returns the citation part of the entry's first line: the line up to the first sentence that carries a status label (`[S]`, `[S2]`, `[V]`, `[U]`, `[D]`, by the token rule of the sources page) or that gives the reading status in words ("Not read", "Not opened"). When the label stands in the first sentence, the cut falls before the bracket it would leave open, or else before the clause, after the last semicolon, that holds the label. A full stop ends a sentence unless the word before it is a single letter (an initial) or a capitalised word of letters (an abbreviation such as "Math." or "Soc."). Markdown is then stripped as before. What the specification left open: SPEC 7.3 asks for "the entry's text as the link's title" and 8.2 item 8 for "Sources for the module" with no format; P0-A4 had taken the whole first line (plan rule, decisions/P0-A4.md), which for one-line entries is the research record. Reason: SPEC 0.3 labels belong to the specification, 8.4 forbids dressing computation up as a citation, and 7.3 publishes the record only on the sources page, with the labels spelled out; the full record stays there unchanged. All 95 keys were checked: none keeps a label or a reference to the specification, and each title still begins as its entry does. Entries whose first line holds a note without a label keep it (for example [W-MS] "Project file ...; also at (link not re-checked)"); a removed autolink still leaves "Free: ." as P0-A4 accepted.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-toolchain-b: the internal-link check of the build (P3-RT-12-01)
Decision: `scripts/links.mjs` checks the built directory after every `npm run build`, through a root `postbuild` script (`node scripts/links.mjs`), so a preview build, a release build (`build:release` and deploy.yml both run `npm run build`) and the `BASE_PATH=/sub/path/ OUT_DIR=dist-basepath` build of `e2e:basepath` all fail on a problem; ci.yml needs no step of its own, since its two build steps run the check. It reads every URL attribute of every built page (`href`, `src`, `srcset`, `poster`, `action`, `xlink:href`, the island attributes `component-url`, `renderer-url`, `before-hydration-url`, and `data` on `<object>`), skips script and style contents and comments, resolves each against the page under the base, and reports a link that lies outside the base, one that names no file of the build (directory and `.html` forms accepted, as GitHub Pages and `astro preview` serve them), and one that names a page that is built but not released. The released flags are read from the sources by the rules of `site/src/lib/pages/released.ts` (a lesson of `src/content/modules` or a page of `src/content/pages` unless its front matter says `released: true`; a tool whose registry entry says `released: false`, both its `/tools/` and `/embed/` routes; a Markdown or MDX page of `src/pages` whose front matter says `released: false`, such as `dev/math-check`). Links to other origins are left to links.yml (SPEC 7.7); fragments are not checked against ids. No dependency. What the specification left open: how the build checks internal links (SPEC 7.7 Links row; DECISIONS.md "P0-A6: the Links row of SPEC 7.7 left open", passed to the orchestrator). Default used: none; the orchestrator's instruction for this cluster (a script under `scripts/`, run by a root npm script after the build, no new dependency), which pre-approved the root `package.json` script. Reason: "checked by the build" read literally, so the red team's three mutations now fail `npm run build` in both modes (exit 1, verified with redteam/rt12/run-mutations.sh m1 m2 m3). `site/tests/unit/scaffold.test.ts` lists `postbuild` among the root scripts it allows.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-nojs-phase4: data-measured marks an output that measures the reader's machine (P4-MERGE-04)
Decision: a `data-out` element whose text is a measurement taken on the reader's machine while the page runs (a time read with `performance.now`) carries the attribute `data-measured` (present, empty value). It is not part of any default state: the server markup renders the element empty and the hydrated tool fills it. The elements so marked: T10's `drawMs`, and the drawing-time probe's `drawTime`, `drawTimes` and `firstDrawTime` (`site/src/components/draw/DrawTimeProbe.svelte`, the only other component that times with `performance.now`). The comparison of `site/tests/e2e/nojs.spec.ts` ("the server markup shows the default state's values") lists such an element as `name (measured)` instead of `name=text`: the element must exist, with the attribute, both in the server markup and after hydration, and only its value is not compared; every other `data-out` is still compared by its text. The rule is driven by the attribute on the element, never by a list of names in the test. What the specification left open: SPEC 7.6 asks the drawing time to be recorded and 4.0 asks the default state to be rendered at build time; neither says how a measurement is told apart from the state. Default used: none of section 10; plan addition (the orchestrator's brief for this cluster). Reason: a time measured on the reader's machine can never appear in markup made at build time. The attribute is an addition to the hooks of SPEC 4.0 that no criterion reads; it is documented in the header comments of `nojs.spec.ts`, `T10GeometryStudio.svelte` and `DrawTimeProbe.svelte`. For MERGE: CONTRACTS.md 5.1 and 5.2 list the hooks; if MERGE counts this attribute as a hook, it belongs there.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-nojs-phase4: T10 reads its data files at build time and loads the orbit as the browser does (P4-MERGE-03)
Decision: during server rendering `t10/snapshot.ts` reads the files of `site/public/presets/T10/` (the manifest `index.json` and the data files the browser fetches) through `import.meta.glob` with `?raw`, inside the `import.meta.env.SSR` branch, as `pages/dev/draw-time.astro` does, so the browser build carries none of them (`npm run size`: `/tools/geometry/` 89.8 kB gzip against 89.7 on the base built on this machine, limit 90; `/tools/fold/` 81.7 against 81.6). The snapshot runs the browser's own decision `loadPlan(facts, manifest, 'load')`: when the manifest has a file for the configured board and rings, the server's orbit is that file read by `fromPresetFile` (source `preset`, both graphs, as the browser gets it); otherwise it is computed in-process as before, with the move graph when it is the graph shown or when the browser derives it at once (`moveGraphFitsOneTask`, the rule of the component's move-graph effect). A configuration that the browser leaves waiting for "Draw the orbit" (more than 2000 items, E-9 rule 1) starts in the state `wait` on the server too, with its vertices when they belong on the main thread, while the snapshot still draws the whole orbit (7.4). `data-out="source"` is shown whenever the orbit is complete, before hydration as after. What the specification left open: how the build-time markup learns which data file the browser will read. Default used: none of section 10; plan addition. Reason: SPEC 4 T10 Presets says the default's vertices and edges are shipped as data files that the tool fetches, so the default state is the one drawn from that file, and 4.0 asks that state to be the server markup.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict: a state loaded from outside withdraws an open prediction (P3-RT-13-03)
Decision: while an instance's prediction is still open, a state other than the configured one that reaches the instance from outside its own controls withdraws the prediction: the prediction block is no longer shown and the board is unfrozen, as for an instance without a prediction. A state equal to the configured one keeps the prediction open. In T1 the outside states are a link read on hydration, the back button, and a jump published by a linked tool (T2 or T8, through `followJumps`), all through `loadFromOutside` in `T01GameBoard.svelte`; in T3, T5, T9, T10, T11 and T15 they are a link and the back button (each tool's own `loadLink`, `applyLink` or `readLink`). What the specification left open: SPEC 4.0 Predict says the answer is computed by the engine and the board is frozen until the reader answers, and 6.6 that a link changes only what it names; neither says what happens when a link names another state for an instance with a prediction. The finding and both verifiers accepted either ignoring the link or dropping the prediction. Default used: none of section 10. Reason: a withdrawn prediction keeps what the link names (6.6, and "Copy link" after an answer and a move gives the reader's position to the next reader), while an ignored link would lose it; and no question then stands over a board it does not describe, nor shows its answer under an open question. T6, T7 and T8 also accept a prediction, but no instance on the site gives them one; their link code was not changed (an open question in the report).

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict: a following garden holds the whole play (P3-RT-13-04)
Decision: whenever T2 (re)starts its follow model, the model covers the play the garden holds: its start and every position up to the cursor, with the edge of each move, ranked by the bounded orbitGraph of the play's start (`followPlay` in `t02/follow.ts`, the model that `followStart` and one `followStep` per move give). This holds for the first state a linked T1 publishes (a garden that hydrates when scrolled to after the board was played), any load (a link, the back button, a picked board, another board, coords or start of the followed T1), the switch to follow mode and the switch of what grows; a reset holds only the start, as before. This replaces, in the P1-A6 entry "follow mechanics and ranking", the words "the garden starts with the position the board stands on when follow begins". What the specification left open: nothing; SPEC 4 T2 ("vertices appear as the reader visits them on the linked T1"), 3 M1 row 1 (6 populations) and M4 row 5 (3 positions) count every position the board reached. Recorded because a builder's entry said otherwise.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict: T8 follows a linked board by extending its game (sibling of P3-RT-04-04)
Decision: T8's subscription to `followToolState` is untracked, as T2's and T3's (it subscribed inside a tracked effect, whose immediate callback read and wrote the game, so the effect subscribed again after every move). Each published state with the same board, the numbers and the start all ones is applied in place to the game T8 holds (`followMoves` in `t08/link.ts`): the moves both share are kept, an undo or a redo moves the cursor, each new move is one legal firing; a move that is not a legal firing leaves the graph (the path is hidden, as before) and keeps the legal moves before it; another board, start or game is checked from the start with `followedGame` and loaded, as before. What the specification left open: nothing (SPEC 7.4 "extends it by one position per move, so a move costs one engine call however long the play is"). Reason: the orchestrator's note on P3-RT-04-04 asked whether T8 had the same cause; it had both parts of it.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict: done controls keep the focus (P3-RT-05-09 and its siblings)
Decision: after hydration a control that its own press makes inactive keeps the focus: it carries `aria-disabled="true"` instead of the HTML `disabled` attribute, and its handler does nothing in that state. This covers Predict's Check and Show me once the prediction is answered (P3-RT-05-09, the remedy the board-a11y fixer recommended); T8's graph vertices and its focus button while T8 is frozen (as Board.svelte since P3-RT-05-02); T4's "keep counting" while it counts, and, when the count is in and the button goes, a focus left on it moves to the counter section (`tabindex="-1"`), inside the tool; and Step, Play to the end and Play on of T1, T5, T7, T8, T9 and T15 while a play runs in the worker, at the end of the game, or at a cap (the "controls disabled while busy" of the board-a11y fixer's open questions; the end state is the same cause, since a play to the end ends the game under the pressed control). The `disabled` attribute stays for the time before hydration (7.4) and while a prediction freezes a board, as the entry "2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-board-a11y: a frozen board stays one tab stop" records for History and the step controls; Predict's answer fields stay `disabled` once answered, since the answer is given from the two buttons and the focus is never in a field then. On the play controls `aria-disabled` follows the state alone, so it is in the server markup too when the default state is already at its end (T5's default play), and hydration still only removes `disabled`. With T4's change, the notice of a count that could not be continued (`data-out="counterNotice"`) is now also spoken in the frame's one polite live region (A-4; 4.0 "a polite live region announces each result"), beside "Counting in the background." What the specification left open: SPEC 7.5 A-1 (with WCAG 2.4.3 among its criteria) names no focus target after an action. Reason: P3-RT-05-09 and the orchestrator's note on its residuals.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict: counting a follower's engine moves in the browser
Decision: the regression tests for a follower's cost per move (`site/tests/e2e/T02.spec.ts`, M1 and M2; `site/tests/e2e/T08.spec.ts`, M5) count the engine's moves made by one move of the leader through Chromium's precise coverage (`site/tests/e2e/engineMoves.ts`): the calls of the engine's `checkMove`, which every `mutate` and `fire` calls once, found in the bundle by its two error messages. They compare the count after a short and a long play, which must be equal (SPEC 7.4). Deviation: CONTRACTS 5.2 says Playwright tests read only the hooks of 4.0 and the live region; these tests read those hooks and, for this one measurement, the coverage counts of the page's scripts, as the timing tests read `performance.now()`. What the specification left open: how to check "a move costs one engine call however long the play is" on the built site. Reason: the orchestrator's note on P3-RT-04-04 (a partial revert of that fix passed every follower test, the timing test included); on a build with that revert the count is 602 against 3 (M1) and 603 against 4 (M2), on the fixed build 2 and 2.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-small-fixes: T9's road counts come from the engine (P3-RT-10-05)
Decision: the road counts back to the new city in T9's end panel, b_j = <beta^vee, alpha_j> (SPEC 2.12, data-out="returnCounts"), are `toNumbers(transposeBoard(board), coroot(board, end))`: the numbers of the coroot played as a population of the reversed board (2.5), three engine exports that `CONTRACTS.md` 2.4 already lists, so no engine export was added. This replaces the formula of the entry "P1-A7: the end panel and the return counts without coroot" (decisions/P1-A7.md), which built b = C^T beta^vee in t09/kostant.ts from `board.cartan` and found beta^vee through `highestShortRoot` or `highestRoot` of the reversed board; the switch to `coroot` that entry announced for P2-A7 is now made, and the values shown are the same (the recipe test against `affine[T].cartan_node0_first` for all 125 long starts still passes). `recipeMatrix`, which only T09.test.ts used, moved from t09/kostant.ts into that test file as a helper, unchanged, so that no T9 source reads a Cartan matrix. What the specification left open: which engine call gives the counts (the finding named three). Not chosen: the negated row 0 of `affineExtension(board, short).board.cartan`, which would put the sign and the node-0 offset of the recipe back into the component. Reason: SPEC 7.3 ("Components contain no mathematics beyond calling the engine"), CLAUDE.md Rules, the orchestrator's note for this cluster.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-small-fixes: a move that changes nothing above four nodes (P3-RT-05-08)
Decision: `announceTemplates.changedOnly` omits the clause of changed nodes when there is none, so a move that changes nothing on a board with more than four nodes reads "Fired node 3. Move 1." or "Mutated city 3. Move 1."; with one or more changes the sentence is the A-4 template, unchanged ("Fired node 4. Node 3 now 3, node 4 now minus 2, node 5 now 1. Move 7."). It is the reading T1's linked view above four nodes already used ("Mutated city 3 and fired node 3. Move 1.", t01/announce.ts). What the specification left open: SPEC 7.5 A-4 gives the changed-nodes template only for a move that changes something. Default used: the remedy recommended to the owner by the red team (omit the empty clause). T11's symmetric moves keep their own recorded reading (decisions/P4-A4.md: "... Nothing changed. Move k."), which returns before `changedOnly` is reached; the site therefore has two readings of a move that changes nothing, raised for the owner. Reason: A-4 templates are whole sentences; the orchestrator's direction for this cluster.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-small-fixes: the mark of T7's Letters panel (P3-RT-05-10)
Decision: the right panel of T7 ("Letters", data-out="symbolicBoard") carries the Numbers icon (the small numbered disc) and the Numbers accent (`--accent-numbers`, #CC79A7) on its border, as the left panel does. What the specification left open: SPEC 8.3 [D] and 6.3 [D] tie the city icon and #009E73 to the Populations view and the disc and #CC79A7 to the Numbers view; T7's right board is neither view by name but plays the numbers game with letters (SPEC 4 T7; its buttons carry data-board="numbers", decisions/P3-A5.md). Not chosen: a neutral mark, or recording the forms as populations of the reversed board (2.7 F6), which no record adopted. Reason: the board kind decides the mark (SPEC 4.0 data-board, 6.2, 6.3, 8.3); the orchestrator's direction for this cluster.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-small-fixes: a held road count above four in the editor (residual of P3-RT-03-01)
Decision: when the board in force holds more than four roads one way between the selected pair (a board from a link: the codec and the engine accept any count, SPEC 5.6), BoardEditor's roadsOut and roadsBack selects show that count as an extra option that is selected and disabled, after the options 0 to 4; the reader can still choose only 0 to 4, so the editor refuses more as 5.6 says. Choosing 0 to 4 for the held direction lowers it. A change of the other direction is refused while one direction holds more than four (`setRoads` of editor/model.ts checks both counts, unchanged, decisions/P2-A3.md), and the select then goes back to the count the board holds, so the select never shows a count the board does not hold. Export and import now relate as follows, with neither changed: the export (T16BoardIO `boardJsonText`) writes the board as it is held, more than four roads included, so the file and the link describe the same board; the import of that file is refused with the reason recorded by RT-FIX-P3-drawing ("The board could not be read: it has 5 roads from node 2 to node 1, and the editor allows at most 4 each way. The board was left as it was."); the editor shows the held count and lets the reader lower it to 0 to 4, after which the export reads back through the import. What the specification left open: how the editor shows a count above its cap that it did not produce. Reason: SPEC 5.6 ("Roads between two nodes, each way (editor only; the engine accepts any count) | 4 | editor refuses more"); the orchestrator's direction for this cluster. The regression test in site/tests/e2e/T16.spec.ts checks the export, the refused import and the round trip after lowering.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-duplicates: where the engine timing regression of P3-RT-07-02 lives
Decision: the lens's Node timing of one T4 load on the 12-cycle (four classify computations, the T4 panels and the bounded root counter, median of seven runs, at most 50 ms) is adopted as packages/engine/test/bench/t4-load-path.bench.ts, run by `npm run bench -w packages/engine` through test/bench/vitest.config.ts. What the specification left open: RT-FIX 5.3 puts a non-golden engine test in packages/engine/test/unit/, which `npm test` runs in parallel workers, and no file says where an engine timing check of a tool's load path goes. Default used: none of SPEC section 10 applies; the precedent of the benchmark of SPEC 7.6 (orbit.bench.ts) and of P4-X2's weyl-dimension.bench.ts, which run alone because a duration measured inside the parallel suite measures the load of the suite rather than the engine. Reason: the same; the test body, input, bound and assertion are the lens's.

## 2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-duplicates: the fixture-build lock in its own module
Decision: the lock of the Astro fixture builds (MERGE, P4 wave 4.2) moves from build-fixture.mjs into site/tests/fixtures/content/build-lock.mjs (lockPathOf, withBuildLock), keyed by the real path of the site directory; build-fixture.mjs imports it. What the specification left open: how the unit tests serialise their fixture builds (SPEC 7.7 asks only that npm test pass for every merge). Default used: none. Reason: released.test.ts and content-components.test.ts spell the site directory differently (without and with a trailing slash), so a lock keyed by the text gave them two locks; the module lets site/tests/unit/fixture-build-lock.test.ts test the lock without running a build (build-fixture.mjs runs a build, or exits, when it is loaded).

Decision: `packages/engine/test/unit/coverage-gate.test.ts` runs Vitest in a child process on a scratch copy of the engine project: the project's own `vitest.config.ts`, `test/golden/_harness.ts` and `test/golden/_coverage.setup.ts` copied (so the registrations and `coverage.json` of the child go to the scratch tree, never to the run in progress), links to `src/`, `reference/` and `site/src/tools/registry/` (for the phase in force), and one stand-in test file per golden test file that has a `covers(...)` call, holding that call as written and an empty test. ## 2026-10-24 RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf: what the residual of P3-RT-07-02 was, measured
Decision: the engine work of loading the 12-cycle by link into T4 and T16 is brought down by making the slow engine calls faster and by not computing what T16 does not show; nothing moves to the worker and no load is split across tasks. What the specification left open: SPEC 7.6 "Main-thread work" says only that no engine call on the main thread may become a long task (50 ms); it does not say how a tool's load should be shaped when hydration itself is long. Default used: none of SPEC section 10 applies. Reason: a Chromium CPU profile (DevTools protocol, 100 microsecond sampling, this container at load 1 to 2, unminified build so that functions keep their names) of /tools/lab/?z=1&g=<12-cycle> at 51a7e26 showed one task of 149 to 167 ms holding 53 to 70 ms of engine self time: the T4 root counter's orbitGraph (cap 2000, 40 layers, Big) 18 to 27 ms, smallestNonfiniteSubboard 20 to 26 ms (cartanClass in rationals on each of the 133 connected subsets), classify 10 to 15 ms (identifyAffine 5 to 9, nullVector about 1.3); the rest was the Svelte runtime 41 to 49 ms, browser work 13 to 18 ms, garbage collection 8 to 10 ms and the tool's own chunks about 15 ms. T16: one task of 136 to 143 ms with 27 to 39 ms of engine time, of which smallestNonfiniteSubboard 14 to 21 ms for a sub-board the sandbox never shows. The default board (A3) without a link already hydrates in one task of 62 to 98 ms here (long tasks of 70 and 75 ms in two of three loads), with 4 to 8 ms of engine work: the long task that remains on a link load is hydration and the render of 12 nodes, not engine work.

## 2026-10-24 RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf: four engine functions made faster without changing a result
Decision: (1) cartanClass decides on the leading principal minors of C instead of those of B = DC: D is diagonal with positive entries, so the k-th minor of B is d_1...d_k times that of C and has its sign; the minors are the pivots of a fraction-free (Bareiss) elimination on numbers, on bigint when a product leaves the safe range; the balance test is unchanged (symmetrizer). (2) smallestNonfiniteSubboard tests connectedness of the 2^n - 1 subsets on bit masks (n at most 30, the old walk above) and applies that rule to the induced matrix without building a sub-board. (3) symmetrizer writes all ones on a symmetric matrix (the walk gives exactly that). (4) orbitGraph on a SafeInt or Big board searches on plain numbers while every value is a safe integer, finding earlier positions by a hash of the entries and comparing them, skipping the two moves that can never give a new position (a node whose number is 0, and the move that found the position); when a value would leave the safe range the items found so far are written back with their keys and the generic loop goes on from that move (bigint on Big; on SafeInt that move throws EngineOverflow as before). What the specification left open: how the engine computes these results; SPEC 5.5, 5.6 and the oracle fix only the results, the order of search and of candidates, and the caps. Default used: none. Reason: SPEC 7.6 and E-9 on main-thread work. Every result, order, cap and interface is unchanged: the golden suite passes, and packages/engine/test/unit/mainthread-fast-paths.test.ts checks each function against the oracle rule it replaces (cartan_class through the minors of B, smallest_nonfinite_subboard, the generic search loop with decimal keys) on random boards, on values past 2^53 and on SafeInt overflow (same EngineOverflow message at the same move).

## 2026-10-24 RT-FIX-P4-lesson-m6: the round and move counts are golden values; part of "P4-A5: typed numbers" withdrawn (P4-RT-08-02)
Decision: the part of the entry "P4-A5: typed numbers" (decisions/P4-A5.md, folded in DECISIONS.md) that lists "the round counts 3, 4, 6" among the numbers with no golden value, and the sentence "The counts 'three rounds', 'eight moves', 'twelve moves' are words", are withdrawn. Why: a round of beat 2 is one mutation at each of two cities, the two-colour product of SPEC 2.14 on a rank-2 board, whose order is the Coxeter number; so the round counts 3, 4, 6 are `types.A2.coxeter_number`, `types.B2.coxeter_number` and `types.G2.coxeter_number`, and the move counts 8 and 12 are twice the last two (the oracle's alternating mutations return after 3, 4 and 6 rounds, and the golden values agree). SPEC 7.3 and 8.4 say such numbers are never typed. Now: the round counts are `{{types.<T>.coxeter_number}}` inside `<Tex>` in beat 2 and in the Seen box, and `fmt('types.<T>.coxeter_number')` in the props of b3 and b4 (caption, and the question, options and reveal of the b4 prediction); the move counts are the exports `B2_MOVES` and `G2_MOVES` (`2 * gv('types.<T>.coxeter_number')`), which also set the length of the two scripts (`scriptOf`) and of the play behind the b4 reveal (`alternation`), and the prose prints them as words through the export `inWords` (the way `DIFFERING` prints a count as a word), so the page reads as before ("after eight moves", "twelve moves", as `M6.spec.ts` checks). What the specification left open: how a number derived from a golden value (twice the Coxeter number) is printed in prose; SPEC 7.3 names `<G>` and `{{path}}`, which print the golden value itself. Other counts in the same paragraphs were checked for the same cause and left as they are: the products 1, 2, 3, 4 of `A_ij A_ji` (the hypothesis of the theorem, no golden value; written in `<Tex>`), the road counts "two", "three", "one" (they define the board, as SPEC 2.1 and the beat 1 line of SPEC 3 M6 do; the golden adjacency records the input, not a computed result), the start positions (2, 1) and (1, 2), and `rounds={2}` (two moves to a round, the number of cities).

## 2026-10-24 RT-FIX-P4-a11y: an answer Check cannot read is named in words (P4-RT-05-05)
Decision: when Predict's Check finds no answer it can read, it writes one sentence into the result line (`data-out="predictResult"`) and the tool's polite live region, and gives each field that holds the problem `aria-describedby` on the result line and, for a text field, `aria-invalid="true"` (a radio button takes no `aria-invalid`, which Svelte's check and ARIA 1.3 refuse for the role radio). The sentences: "Type a whole number." (a number question: empty, a word, a fraction, "+3"), "Type a whole number in each field." (a position question), "Choose one of the answers." (a choice question with no choice made, which also said nothing before). Editing a marked field (typing, or choosing an answer) removes its mark, and the sentence goes once no field is marked; answering or "Show me" replaces it by the result as before. The board stays frozen and Check stays usable. Check now also returns at once once the prediction is answered, so an answered Check with an empty field says nothing (RT-FIX-P3-residual-tools). What the specification left open: 4.0 Predict and 7.5 give no wording for an answer that cannot be read; WCAG 3.3.1 and 4.1.3 ask that the error be named in text and announced. Default used: none. ## 2026-10-24 RT-FIX-P4-a11y: one look for a control that cannot act (P4-RT-06-01)
Decision: one rule in `site/src/styles/base.css`, loaded on every page, gives every `button`, `input`, `select` and `textarea` that is `:disabled` (before hydration, and without JavaScript) or `aria-disabled="true"` (a done control, a frozen board's node) a dashed border and text toned towards the page: `color-mix(in srgb, var(--text) 65%, var(--page))`, which is 5.4 to 1 on the light page and 6.9 to 1 on the dark one, so A-6 holds for that text too. The two declarations carry `!important`, because every component sets `color` and `border` for the usable look in a scoped rule of higher specificity (and some, such as T11's selected tab, set `border` again in a state rule); no component rule overrides them, and T10 and T11 take the look without an edit to their files. A board's drawn nodes are not buttons (the node buttons are transparent hit areas over the drawing), so the rule changes nothing on a drawn board: its second ring of 6.3 ("may act here") is drawn on a board that is not hydrated yet or is frozen by a prediction as before, since a dashed circle already marks nodes in T9 and in the board editor. ## 2026-10-24 RT-FIX-P4-toolchain: the postbuild holds the release report (P4-RT-12-04)
Decision: the open-items report gains an optional field `linkCheck` (`running`, `passed`, `failed`). In a release build (`RELEASE` set, the rule of `isReleaseBuild`), `scripts/links.mjs` first marks a report that the Astro build marked complete as incomplete with `linkCheck: 'running'`, runs the check, and then marks it complete with `linkCheck: 'passed'` when the check passed, or leaves it incomplete with `linkCheck: 'failed'`; a check that stops on the way leaves `running` and the report incomplete. A report that the Astro build left incomplete is never touched, so a link check never completes the report of a build that failed. The build-done hook also marks the report of its build incomplete again when the build process exits with a code other than 0 after the hook. The Markdown report is rewritten each time, so it says "Incomplete" whenever the JSON does. To let plain Node do this, the report's file code (`isReleaseBuild`, the reports directory, the JSON and Markdown writers) moves unchanged from `unverifiedRegistry.ts` into `site/src/lib/openItemsReport.mjs`, which the registry imports and whose `isReleaseBuild` and `reportPath` it re-exports. `scripts/report.mjs` is unchanged: it refuses every report whose `complete` is not `true`. What the specification left open: what `npm run report` does after a release build that failed in postbuild (SPEC 7.3, 7.7 are silent; the decision RT-FIX-P3-toolchain-b "a complete release report" gives the reason). Default used: none. Reason: a release build is prebuild, the Astro build and the postbuild, and a failed release build is never presented as the release report; the existing assertions that the Astro build alone completes the report (the fixture build and the hooks test of `report-partial-release.test.ts`) still hold.

## 2026-10-24 RT-FIX-P4-engine: wythoffEdges past 2^53 on a Big board throws EngineOverflow (P4-RT-01-01 P4-RT-03-01)
Decision: `wythoffEdges` throws `EngineOverflow` when an edge it is about to return has an entry that is not a safe integer, on every arithmetic, instead of returning `Number()` of the bigint. The check is made when the edge is recorded, after the cap test, so a search that the cap stops before such an edge returns its items as before; on `SafeInt` the moves themselves throw, as they always did, and may do so earlier because `SafeInt` checks every product (`G2` with the ring 3002399751580330 on its long node: exact edges on `Big`, `EngineOverflow` on `SafeInt`). What the specification left open: SPEC 5.4 lists `wythoffEdges` as exact and E-2 gives `Big` exact values, while CONTRACTS.md 2.4 phase 4 types the items as `[number[], number[]]`, which cannot hold an entry beyond 2^53; decisions/P4-A1.md ("entries converted to number") decides the order and truncation only. Default used (SPEC section 10): none. Reason: E-10 names `EngineOverflow` for a value the result cannot hold, `SafeInt` already throws it on the same input, and the recorded rule of `symbolicPlay` (decisions/P3-A2.md "the overflow rule of symbolicPlay") is the same reading of a `number[]` contract; returning bigint entries would change the signature of CONTRACTS.md 2.4. Both reproducers accept the throw.

## 2026-10-24 RT-FIX-P4-engine: symmetrizer and gram read the entries through bigint (P4-RT-01-02)
Decision: `symmetrizer` and `gram` build the rationals of the Cartan entries as `rat(BigInt(x))` from the integer copy of the matrix, not `rat(x)`. The rule of decisions/P1-A1.md that a number argument of `rat` must be a safe integer is kept unchanged; the entries of a board are integers of any size (SPEC 5.6, first table: "the engine accepts any count"; `fromAdjacency` accepts any integer), so they go into bigint before `rat` sees them. What the specification left open: nothing about the values (the oracle and SPEC 5.6 fix them); this records why `rat` itself was not changed. Default used (SPEC section 10): none. Reason: the smallest change at the cause; `cartanClass`, `classify`, `smallestNonfiniteSubboard` and every guarded function reach the rationals only through `symmetrizer` (in `classOfConnected`) and `gram`, and the elimination of `classByMinors` already moves to bigint when a value leaves the safe range.

## 2026-10-24 RT-FIX-P4-engine: the hash of the orbit fast path and the export positionHash (P4-RT-03-02)
Decision: `searchOnNumbers` (search.ts) hashes a position as the sum, mod 2^30, of one share per entry, the share being the low 32 bits of the entry and the rest (entry = rest times 2^32 plus low) mixed with the position's odd seed by the finaliser of MurmurHash3 (two multiplications and three shifts). The sum keeps the update in the entries a move changes; the mix makes the share not linear in the entry, so a sublattice such as 2^30 Z^n no longer falls into one bucket. The positions the hash picks are still compared entry by entry, so every result, order and cap is the generic loop's, as decisions/RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf.md requires. `positionHash` is exported from search.ts (not from index.ts, so not part of the public API of CONTRACTS.md 2.4) for the counting test. What the specification left open: SPEC 5.5 keys the orbit hash set by the decimal text and says nothing on a faster equivalent; the residual fix recorded the method only as "a hash of the entries". Default used (SPEC section 10): none. Reason: the instruction of the round asks for a multiplicative mix per entry with a non-linear finaliser that keeps every result, order and cap. Measured on this machine (load 7 to 13 on 4 processors): E8, firing, from 2^30 (1, ..., 1), cap 40000: one hash for all 40000 positions and 799980000 comparisons before, 39999 hashes and 1 comparison after; the fast path took 13.6 to 19.6 s before and 0.05 to 0.22 s after (seeds 2^29 to 2^40 times (1, ..., 1)) against 0.6 to 0.9 s for the generic loop. Warm, interleaved in one process: the orbit benchmark's search (12-cycle with a chord, 2000 positions, Big) 1.94 ms before and 1.60 ms after, the T4 load path 11.7 ms before and 11.8 to 13.1 ms after; E8, firing, from (1, ..., 1) at 100000 positions 619 ms before and 254 ms after.

## 2026-10-24 RT-FIX-P4-engine: what the orbit benchmark measures, and request for its bigint case (P4-RT-11-02, needs-decision)
Decision: record and request; packages/engine/test/bench/orbit.bench.ts is not changed on this branch. Record: since the residual fix of P3-RT-07-02 (decisions/RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf.md item 4), `orbitGraph` on a `Big` board searches on plain numbers while every value is a safe integer, so the benchmark of SPEC 7.6 (the 12-cycle with the chord 1 to 7, a `Big` board, seeds 0 and 1, cap 2000, 40 layers, median of seven, 25 ms) times the search on numbers and no longer the bigint loop with decimal keys that it timed at G3; no entry recorded this until now. What the specification left open: SPEC 7.6 says "2000 positions on a board with 12 nodes in `Big` arithmetic", which can name the board (E-2: a board carries its arithmetic) or the computation timed (5.5 and `reference/bench_orbit.mjs` time bigint). Default used (SPEC section 10): none. The fix asked for this round (a second case on the same board with the seeds times 2^60, the same 2000 positions in the bigint loop, also against 25 ms) was written and it catches the lens's mutant F9 (bigint case median 588.54 ms, the first case 21.27 ms and passing), but on this machine the bigint case does not stay under 25 ms: medians at a one-minute load of about 2 (the quietest seen in about 50 minutes of waiting; the five-minute load was 4.6): 31.84, 24.29 and 30.02 ms (the first case 20.30, 13.91, 10.68 ms); at about 4.5: 29.12, 22.81, 21.60 ms; at about 10: 22.92, 34.23, 40.47 ms; at 11 to 12: 26.58 to 36.68 ms; under `nice -n -20` at 15: 37.34, 24.82, 30.80 ms. For scale, P3-A2 measured this container at about 2.3 times slower than the processor the 25 ms line was sized for, and the bigint loop with seeds 0 and 1 measured 19.75 to 21.60 ms alone at G3 (MERGE P3 stage 3.1; GATE G3 21.01 ms); the RT-11 lens measured the times-2^60 case at 21.68 ms at load 6. In one process at a load of about 2, alternating the engine of the base 967118d and of this branch, the times-2^60 search took a median of 19.93 and 20.98 ms over 30 runs (23.26 and 24.89 over the first seven) on the base and 19.45 and 20.49 ms (21.23 and 22.87) on this branch: the bigint loop is unchanged by this branch and sits just under the line warm. A threshold is not the fixer's to change, so the case is not committed and the branch stays green. Options: (a) keep 25 ms for both cases and make the bigint loop faster first (for example a key or hash built only from the entries a move changes, as the numbers path does), then add the case; (b) the owner reads "in `Big` arithmetic" as naming the board, records that the benchmark times the numbers path, and adds the bigint case with a line the owner sets for this container; (c) add the case as written and let GATE measure it alone on a quiet machine, accepting that it may fail there. Recommendation: (a), since the bigint loop is what the main thread runs on a custom or affine board once a value passes 2^53, and 7.6 sizes the 25 ms line for that case. Request, for whoever makes the change after the decision: in packages/engine/test/bench/orbit.bench.ts, after the closing `});` of the test "12-cycle with a chord: 2000 positions in Big within 25 ms", add a test "12-cycle with a chord: the same 2000 positions with the seeds times 2^60 (the bigint loop) within 25 ms" with the comment `// regression: P4-RT-11-02` that builds the same board, checks `board.arith` is `Big`, makes the twelve unit seeds and the same seeds times `2n ** 60n`, checks once that the scaled search has 2000 items, truncated true, the same `depth`, `parent` and `node` as the unit search and every item 2^60 times the unit item, then times seven runs of `orbitGraph(b, scaled, 'mutation', 2000, 40)`, writes `orbit benchmark, bigint loop (seeds times 2^60): median ... ms` with `process.stdout.write`, and expects the median to be at most 25 ms; this is the lens's packages/engine/test/bench/redteam-RT-11-big-values.bench.ts on branch worktree-agent-a19febfb0f4c5a241 folded into the benchmark file, with a header note that the first case times the numbers path and the second the bigint loop.

## 2026-10-24 RT-FIX-P4-shared: a link's state is not written before the reader acts (P4-RT-04-03)
Decision: site/src/lib/history.ts tells a link being applied from a reader's change, and writes only instances the reader has changed. An instance whose keys are in the address bar when it registers is "opened from a link". Until the reader acts inside its frame, its changes reaching `stateChanged` are recorded (Copy link and the back button use them) and not written; while such a link waits, the change of an instance the reader has not acted on (a follower that follows the linked tool through `linkTo`) is the link's too. The reader acts by a `pointerdown`, `keydown`, `click`, `input` or `change` event whose target lies inside a ToolFrame root (`[data-frame]`, read through its `data-instance`), heard once per page by capture listeners on the window that history.ts adds with its popstate listener; `exampleLoaded` also counts as the reader acting. A write encodes only the instances the reader has changed; every other instance keeps its keys as the bar holds them, so the bar is never normalised for an instance the reader did not touch. Copy link encodes the instance asked for and every instance the reader changed, and keeps the other instances' link keys, which give the states they show. What the specification left open: SPEC 7.4 says when the bar is written ("after a move") and 6.6 which instances ("only instances the reader has changed"); the plan (P1-A2 5.6) adds "Nothing is written on load or hydration". How history.ts learns that a change is the reader's is not specified. This refines the P1-A2 record ("appends each changed instance's keys"): "changed" now means changed by the reader, and an unchanged instance's keys are kept rather than stripped. No interface changes: the four exports of history.ts keep their signatures, and no tool needed a change (T10 and T11, which apply a link a task after hydration, are covered by the same rule). Reason: ToolFrame registers an instance before the tool applies its link (Svelte runs the child's effects first), so the link's state reached `stateChanged` as a change and was written half a second after load, normalised, on ten routes. Known limit: a touch that scrolls the page over a tool whose link is still being applied asynchronously (T10's facts computed in tasks, T11's long replay in the worker) counts as acting on it, and the link is then written normalised.

## 2026-10-24 RT-FIX-P4-shared: the KaTeX fonts a page uses are preloaded (P4-RT-07-03)
Decision: every generated page with KaTeX markup carries, just before the KaTeX stylesheet link, one `<link rel="preload" href="<BASE_URL>katex/<version>/fonts/<file>.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>` per KaTeX font its markup uses; a page without KaTeX markup is unchanged. site/src/lib/katex.ts reads which font a class selects from the installed katex.min.css (its @font-face rules and the rules that set a family, a weight or a style for a KaTeX class; a class that sets only a weight or a style is taken in KaTeX_Main), and site/src/middleware.ts (Astro middleware, which in a static build runs once per page while the build generates it, with `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`) adds the links to the generated HTML. The stylesheet and the fonts stay those of the installed KaTeX (7.2 item 2), with their `font-display: block`. What the specification left open: 7.6 [D] sets the lab thresholds, not how fonts load. Why this changes P3-X1's record ("no repeated layout from late fonts was large in the traces, so no preload was added"): P3-X1 measured M0 to M3, before M6 and M7 existed. On M7 (37079 pixels of lesson) the late fonts relaid and repainted the whole document after the first paint (Layout 62 to 158 ms, PrePaint and Paint 89 to 134 ms in the lens's traces), and the lens and its verifier measured Total Blocking Time 319 to 427 ms as built against 196 to 207 ms with the fonts preloaded (four times slowdown), against the 200 ms of 7.6. A page fetches the fonts its markup uses anyway (the first layout meets all its text), so the preloads move the same requests earlier and add none. The middleware was chosen because a layout writes its head before the page's content is rendered, and rendering the content first in Base.astro (Astro.slots.render) would move the head content Astro emits on first render into the body. Preloads in this build: M7 Main-Regular, Math-Italic, SansSerif-Regular (the lens's three); M0 also Size1 and Size2; M6 also Fraktur; tool routes other than /tools/geometry/, /about/ and /credits/ none.
Measurements (npm run lab -- --port 7652 --dist <dir> /modules/m7-geometry/ /tools/board/, three Lighthouse runs per route, median; /tools/board/ is a page without KaTeX markup, since every lesson has some): one run on the base build at load 17 to 20: M7 TBT 656.3 ms, board 342.6 ms.
