## 2026-10-24 RT-FIX-P4-shared: the credits page lists every package whose code ships, read from the build (P4-RT-08-04)
Decision: site/src/lib/pages/shippedPackages.ts holds an Astro integration (registered in site/astro.config.mjs) that adds a Vite plugin to the client environment and to the worker bundles. At the end of each bundle the plugin records every npm package one of whose modules has code in an emitted chunk (a module under node_modules belongs to the package of its last node_modules segment; the bundler's own modules, `vite/preload-helper.js` and `rolldown/runtime.js`, to vite and rolldown), with the chunks, the importing packages and the rendered length. Astro generates the pages after the client build and in the same process, so the credits page reads the list of that very build (kept on `globalThis` under a registered symbol); a build that publishes /credits/ also writes the list, when it is done, to site/src/generated/shipped-packages-<12 hex digits of the output directory>.json (generated, not committed), which the browser suite compares with the page. The fixture builds of the unit suite (site config, temporary output directory, no credits page) write nothing, so they cannot replace the site build's list. The credits page uses the list: lib/pages/dependencies.ts adds a row for each such package that no package.json names (version, licence and author from its installed package.json, "Used": its code is bundled into the scripts of the pages, imported by ...), and marks a named package that the list contains and SHIPPED does not describe. A production build fails if the list is missing when the credits page is generated. The page's sentence now says "and every other package whose code the build bundles into the scripts of the pages". What the specification left open: 7.9 [D] lists "the licences of bundled libraries" without saying how they are found; P0-A5's record took the three package.json files only. The lockfile's tree of the shipped packages was not used: astro's tree is the build toolchain and would mark hundreds of packages as shipped. Packages found in this build, with the length of their code in the chunks before compression: @astrojs/svelte 1879 bytes, nanostores 2894, svelte 168326 (all three named in site/package.json), and three that no package.json names, now with credits rows: clsx 2.1.1 (MIT, Luke Edwards; imported by svelte) 536 bytes, rolldown 1.2.13 (MIT; its runtime helpers, in the engine worker and one shared chunk) 710 bytes, vite 8.3.4 (MIT; its preload helper) 3221 bytes. The page now says 8 packages reach the reader (5 before). None of the three was added by an agent, so SPEC 9.3's DECISIONS.md record of an added dependency does not apply; MERGE may fold these lines as their record. The tests that read the build (credits-bundled.spec.ts) are browser-suite files, as RT-FIX-P3-perf-b did for registry-outs.spec.ts, because CI runs the unit suite before the build.

## 2026-10-24 RT-FIX-P4-shared: once the reader acts, every instance's change is written, leaders and followers included (P4-RT-04-03)
Decision: site/src/lib/history.ts replaces the per-frame rule of the first entry of this fragment. The page counts the reader's actions: each `pointerdown`, `keydown`, `click`, `input` or `change` event whose target lies inside any tool frame (`[data-frame]`, ToolFrame's root), heard by the capture listeners history.ts adds with its popstate listener, and each `exampleLoaded`. Every instance records that count when it registers. On a page opened from a link (some instance registered while the address bar held its keys), a change that reaches `stateChanged` before the reader has acted since that instance registered is the instance's load (its link applied, or a follower taking the linked state): it is recorded, so Copy link and the back button use it, and it is not written. Every other change is the reader's: the instance is marked changed and the bar is written half a second after the burst, as in the base 967118d. On a page opened without a link every change is written, as in the base. A write still encodes the instances the reader has changed and keeps every other instance's keys as the bar holds them; Copy link still encodes the instance asked for and the changed ones. The per-instance `fromLink` and `acted` flags, the page-wide test "some link still waits" and the walk from a frame to its `data-instance` are removed.
Why: the per-frame rule held a change back while the instance's own frame had not been acted on and any link waited. Through `linkTo` one press changes two instances, so a leader moved from its follower's frame (M5 `?b1.w=1`, a jump in b2's table; M1 `?b1.w=2.1`, a jump to the start in the garden), a follower moved by its leader while another instance's link waited (M1 `?b1.w=2&b3.w=1`, M6 `?b1.w=2&b11.w=1`), and a follower that came with its own link keys were never written, and Copy link gave a link that reopened at another state. That is against SPEC 7.4 ("Copy link always encodes the current state") and 6.6; the phase 4 confirmer found it. Whether the reader has acted is therefore asked of the page, not of a frame. It is asked from each instance's registration and not only once per page (the simplest rule, hold every write until the first action), because a tool that hydrates as the reader scrolls to it applies its link after the reader has acted elsewhere, and would write it at once: the finding again, on lesson pages. The gate "opened from a link" keeps a page without a link on the base rule: nothing is applied there on load (the confirmer found no write on load on all 21 tool and lesson routes without a link), so such a page does not depend on the event listeners at all. Events count only inside a tool frame, not anywhere on the page, because a key that scrolls the page or a touch on a lesson's text acts on no tool, and every control that changes a tool's state lies inside its ToolFrame (CONTRACTS.md 5.1). Why the bar then gives the current state of every instance: an instance the reader has changed is encoded from its recorded state; any other instance shows what loading the page gave it from keys the bar still holds, its own as they were and those of the instance it follows, which are rewritten whenever that instance changes, so the bar reopens to the same state.
Known limits: a press inside a tool frame between an instance's registration and the end of its load (T10's facts computed in tasks, T11's replay in the worker, a follower's later task) makes the rest of that load count as the reader's, so it is written normalised; it then encodes the state shown. A follower that hydrates after the reader moved its leader is not written until the reader acts again, but its leader's keys give it on reopening, and Copy link from it encodes it.
What the specification left open: as in the first entry, how history.ts tells a reader's change from a link being applied. No interface changes: the exports of history.ts keep their signatures, and no tool or ToolFrame changed. Tests: site/tests/e2e/history-after-action.spec.ts (the confirmer's examples: M5 jump in the follower, M1 jump to the start, M1 followers with their own keys and beside an untouched link, Copy link before and after an action) and four cases added to site/tests/unit/history.test.ts; history-no-write-on-load.spec.ts and the earlier cases of history.test.ts are unchanged and pass.

## 2026-10-24 P5-A1: the sparse helpers, their names and the key format
Decision: `rep.ts` exports `spKey(row, column)`, `spMul(X, Y)`, `spAdd(X, Y, cy = 1n)`, `spComm(X, Y)`, `spScale(X, c)` and `spEq(X, Y)`, ports of `sp_mul`, `sp_add`, `sp_comm`, `sp_scale` and of Python's `==` on zero-free dictionaries. A key is the row and the column as decimal integers joined by one comma, no spaces, no leading zeros (`"0,2"`, `"12,3"`); `spKey` throws `RangeError` unless both are non-negative safe integers. Every operation returns a new `Map` without zero entries (the oracle's final filter, applied after all sums, so the order of the entries is the oracle's insertion order); `spScale` by `0n` gives the empty `Map`. `spMul` parses each key once per entry; since the repair after review, every operation checks the keys of its inputs in the same way and throws `RangeError` on a key that `spKey` would not write (for instance `"0, 1"` or `"01,1"`), since such a key would silently miss its partner (entry "one key check in every sparse operation" below). What the specification left open: the names and the key format (SPEC 5.2 gives only `Map<string, bigint>`, key "row,column"). Default used (SPEC section 10): none; the plan's names (instruction 5.2). Reason: one key writer for the engine, T12 and phase 7.

## 2026-10-24 P5-A1: spEq ignores explicit zero entries
Decision: `spEq` compares the nonzero entries only: an explicit `0n` in either `Map` counts as absent, and the result does not depend on insertion order. What the specification left open: how to compare a `Map` that a caller built without the zero-free invariant. Default used (SPEC section 10): none; the plan's rule (instruction 5.2). Reason: on zero-free inputs it is exactly the oracle's `==`; on others it still answers the mathematical question.

## 2026-10-24 P5-A1: the RelationCheck list, its order, and the split of the Serre boolean
Decision: `chevalleySerre` returns one record per instance: for `i` from 0 to n-1, then `j` from 0 to n-1, the records `hh`, `he`, `hf`, `ef`, then, when `i != j`, `serre-e` and `serre-f`; that is 6n^2 - 2n records (20 on A2, 88 on D4, 280 on E7). The oracle's single Serre boolean is split into `serre-e` and `serre-f`. `left` and `right` are new `Map`s in every record: the right side of `ef` with `i == j` is a zero-free copy of `H[i]` (`spScale(H[i], 1n)`), `hh`, the other `ef` and both Serre right sides are new empty `Map`s, and the Serre left side starts from a copy of `E[j]` (or `F[j]`) and applies `ad(E[i])` exactly `1 - C[i][j]` times. `holds` is `spEq(left, right)`; the oracle's `chevalley_serre_ok` is true exactly when every record holds. What the specification left open: the order and the granularity of the records (SPEC 5.4: "a RelationCheck for every relation, with both sides"). Default used (SPEC section 10): none; the plan's (instruction 5.5). Reason: the oracle's loop order; T12 can show each Serre relation separately, and its link key `q` (6.6) names one relation with its nodes (`serre-e:2,3`).

## 2026-10-24 P5-A1: moves computed from fire, not as E + F + P0
Decision: `moves[k]` is the oracle's `S[k]`: for every basis vector `a`, the entry `(index of fire(a, k), index of a)` is `1n`, including the diagonal entries where `a_k = 0`. It is never assembled as `E[k] + F[k] + P_k^0`. On the 18 minuscule records the two agree (tested); on node 2 of D4 they differ at every node (tested), because entries 2 and -2 reach `moves` and `H` but neither `E` nor `F`. What the specification left open: the roster's wording "the move matrices E_k + F_k + P_k^0" against the oracle's `S`. Default used (SPEC section 10): none; the oracle (COMMON.md 2, extended by the plan to the roster's wording; SPEC 2.18 states the identity only for minuscule nodes). Reason: T12 shows the firing move for any node, minuscule or not.

## 2026-10-24 P5-A1: how the cap of minusculeMatrices is decided
Decision: `minusculeMatrices(board, i, cap = CAPS.repOrbit)` enumerates `orbit(board, [omega_i], 'firing', cap)` and returns `null` exactly when the result is `truncated`; by SPEC 5.5 an orbit of exactly `cap` positions is not truncated and is built (E7 node 7 at a cap of 56 is built, at 55 it is `null`). `orbitSize` is not consulted first: the enumeration stops at the cap anyway (at most `cap + 1` positions are found), so a second source of truth would only add a guarded play. `cap` must be a positive safe integer (`RangeError`). The oracle has no cap; the cap is the engine's own rule. The default is pinned by test on both sides (added in the repair after review): node 5 of A13 (C(14, 5) = 2002 positions) is `null` by default and built at a cap of 2002, node 2 of B32 (4 C(32, 2) = 1984 positions) is built by default; no board of at most 100 nodes has an orbit of omega_i of a size strictly between the two, and an orbit of exactly 2000 positions needs a board of 1000 nodes (node 1 of B1000, C1000, D1000), so the boundary itself is tested through the cases with a cap equal to the orbit size. What the specification left open: the method (the instruction allows either). Default used (SPEC section 10): none. Reason: one decision path, the search's own truncation, which SPEC 5.5 defines exactly.

## 2026-10-24 P5-A1: the guards, and their absence on signedMoves
Decision: `minusculeMatrices`, `chevalleySerre` and `stringThrough` check their arguments first (`RangeError`), then call `requireGcm` and `requireFinite` from `guards.ts`, in P2-A1's order: so a one-way board throws `NeedsTwoWayRoads`, an affine or indefinite board `NotFiniteType`, and a malformed argument `RangeError` even on a one-way board. `signedMoves` takes no board and has no guard: it works as defined on whatever matrices it is given. Each function that takes a board has the `AnyBoard` overload after the generic one, as P2-A1 and P3-A1 did. What the specification left open: 5.6 lists "the representation functions" in its last row without naming the one that takes no board. Default used (SPEC section 10): none; the plan's reading (instruction 5.4). Reason: a guard needs a board.

## 2026-10-24 P5-A1: RangeError cases added
Decision: `RangeError` on: a row or column of `spKey` that is not a non-negative safe integer; a key in an input of `spMul`, `spAdd`, `spScale` or `spEq` (and so of `spComm`, `signedMoves` and `chevalleySerre`) that is not two decimal integers joined by one comma, as `spKey` writes it (all four since the repair after review; at first only `spMul`); a node position outside 0..n-1 (`minusculeMatrices`, `stringThrough`); a `cap` that is not a positive safe integer (`minusculeMatrices`); `E` and `F` of different lengths, or a basis vector shorter than `E` (`signedMoves`); `E`, `F` or `H` without one matrix per node (`chevalleySerre`); `mu` without one entry per node, an entry of `mu` that is not a safe integer, and `mu_i < 0` (`stringThrough`, where the oracle asserts; the message names the node position and the value). What the specification left open: invalid arguments. Default used (SPEC section 10): none; `RangeError`, as every earlier phase did. Reason: E-10 reserves the engine's own classes for the theory; reaching the cap is reported by `null`, never thrown.

## 2026-10-24 P5-A1: stringThrough has no cap and checks each entry
Decision: `stringThrough` returns all `mu_i + 1` positions whatever `mu_i` is; the specification gives no cap, and T12 must bound what a reader can type (requested from P5-A2). Each position is the previous one minus column `i` of `C`, and each entry is checked with `Number.isSafeInteger` as it is computed (`EngineOverflow` otherwise, the `SafeInt` rule of E-2); successive subtraction gives exactly `mu - k * column` while every entry is safe, and fails only at an entry the result cannot hold. `-0` is written as `0`. What the specification left open: the length bound and the arithmetic. Default used (SPEC section 10): none; the plan's (instruction 5.6). Reason: the oracle has no bound; the contract types the result as `number[][]`.

## 2026-10-24 P5-A1: the bigint to number rule for basis
Decision: `basis` is `number[][]` on every board. On a `Board<number>` the entries are taken as they are (with `-0` written as `0`); on a finite `Board<bigint>` (a finite board built by hand) each entry is converted with `Number` after a check that it is a safe integer, and `EngineOverflow` is thrown otherwise, which a finite orbit within the cap never meets. The matrices are `bigint` on every board. The basis is the orbit sorted by a numeric comparator, entry by entry, largest first (never the default string sort), and is indexed by the entries joined with commas; `fire` is applied to the orbit's own vectors in the board's arithmetic, and `join` writes a number and a bigint with the same text. What the specification left open: the contract's `number[][]` on a `Board<bigint>`. Default used (SPEC section 10): none; the plan's (instruction 5.3). Reason: the contract type; the same rule as the overflow rule of `wythoffEdges` (decisions/RT-FIX-P4-engine.md).

## 2026-10-24 P5-A1: one key check in every sparse operation (repair after review)
Decision: `spMul`, `spAdd`, `spScale` and `spEq` check every key of every `Map` they are given with one parser (the one `spMul` already used), the keys of explicit zero entries included and whatever the answer would be, and throw `RangeError` on a key that `spKey` would not write: anything but two decimal integers joined by one comma, without spaces, signs or leading zeros, each a safe integer. `spComm` is checked through `spMul` and adds the two products without a second check. Before, only `spMul` checked: `spAdd`, `spScale` and `spEq` accepted such a key silently, so `"0, 1"` and `"0,1"` were two entries of a sum and `spEq` called them different matrices. As a consequence `signedMoves` (through `spAdd`) and `chevalleySerre` (through `spMul`, `spScale` and `spEq`) throw `RangeError` on such a key too. The cost is one regular-expression test per key per call: `chevalleySerre` on the 56 of E7 measured 26.98 ms in the bench run after the change (25.70 ms before; `minusculeMatrices` 4.80 ms), and `minusculeMatrices` itself writes its keys without a check. Tested in `p5-rep-units.test.ts > sparse operations > every sparse operation refuses a key that spKey would not write, in the same way (RangeError)` and `p5-guards.test.ts > argument errors > signedMoves and chevalleySerre: a matrix key that spKey would not write`; both fail on the code as first merged. What the specification left open: invalid keys (SPEC 5.2 gives only the key "row,column"). Default used (SPEC section 10): none; the review's finding 5. Reason: one rule for every operation, so that a caller (T12, phase 7) learns of a malformed key at once whichever operation it calls first.

## 2026-10-24 P5-A2: the default relation
Decision: `[E_i, F_i] = H_i` (code `ef:i,i`) for a minuscule node, for a node whose matrices are not built, and for an orbit whose relation list is computed in the worker (more than 27 positions; the default never waits for the worker); for a node that is not minuscule with at most 27 positions, the first failing check in the engine's order, so that a failing relation shows on load (`ef:1,1` on node 2 of D4). The checker's three selects write one code (6.6 `q`, labels); picking a Serre relation with i = j moves the other node to the first other label (Serre relations need i != j). A check is always found by its fields (relation, i, j), never by its index in the list. What the specification left open: which relation shows first. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.5).

## 2026-10-24 P5-A2: the verdict and the explanation (F11)
Decision: `minuscule` is `minusculeNodes(board)`, never read off the relation list. The explanation's number comes from legal play from omega_i (F11's third condition: the first number fired that is greater than 1, with its move), checked against `minusculeNodes` (an Error if they disagree). Wording: minuscule `Node i is minuscule: every number in the orbit of ωi is −1, 0 or 1, and all the relations hold.`; not minuscule `Node i is not minuscule: some number in the orbit is m (legal play from ωi fires a m at move t), so the steps E and F of the recipe miss some moves and the relations fail.` (when not built: `... would miss some moves.`). The phrase of SPEC 4 T12, "some number in the orbit is 2", stands verbatim (`someNumberPhrase`). A board without a minuscule node (E8, F4, G2) adds `This board has no minuscule node; its representations need more than the game.` (`data-out="no-minuscule"`). Above 2000 positions (`orbitSize`, before any enumeration) the tool shows the explanation alone with `The orbit of ωi has N positions, more than 2000, so the matrices are not built here.` (`data-out="limit"`), and `minusculeMatrices`, `signedMoves` and `chevalleySerre` are not called (unit test with a counting engine). What the specification left open: the wording. Default used: the plan's.

An edge whose upper end has mu_k of 2 or more is no entry of E_k or F_k: dashed (`data-step="false"`), and the legend says why. Up to 300 positions (CAPS.gardenDrawEverything, T2's bound) everything is drawn; above, the sizes of the layers are listed (`data-layer-count`) with a sentence. The drawing is one SVG string in two layers (edges, then vertices with role img and a title), inserted as markup (`orbitSvg`, a pure function) and drawn in two tasks; the orbit table of the table view holds the same data as text (capped at 300 rows with a sentence). ## 2026-10-24 P5-A2: the relation in MathML
Decision: the relation checker writes its formula with `t12/RelationFormula.svelte` in MathML (`math`, `msub`, `msup`, `mrow`, `mo`, `mn`, `mi`), with C_ij and the exponent 1 - C_ij evaluated and labels as subscripts (`[E1, F2] = 0`, `ad(E1)^2 E2 = 0`), an `aria-label` read in words (`E 1 F 2 commutator equals 0`, `ad E 1 to the power 2 applied to E 2 equals 0`) and the spans fallback of `LinearForm.svelte`'s `RENDER` switch. No KaTeX is involved. What the specification left open: the rendering of formulas inside a tool. Default used: the plan's (LinearForm has no commutator or power form, so a small component of T12's own).

## 2026-10-24 P5-A2: the string viewer
Decision: the string viewer plays free firing (the numbers game, every node can be fired) on a board of its own at the representation's node i, from a start that is omega_i by default and can be typed (one field per node, whole numbers of at most 40 digits; a sentence in `data-out="start-message"` otherwise). The line through mu: for mu_i > 0 `stringThrough(board, mu, i)`; for mu_i < 0 the same line read from mu upward (`stringThrough` of `fire(mu, i)`, reversed; the oracle asserts mu_i >= 0); for mu_i = 0 mu alone. Each position is marked in or out of the orbit of mu by comparing the ends of legal play (F3). More than 12 positions: the first and last six and a count; more than 2000 positions, or entries beyond 2^53 (stringThrough takes numbers only), the two ends (mu and R_i mu, from `fire`) and the count, with a sentence. Firing node i turns the line end over end; the list replays a short flip (none under reduced motion, A-9) and `data-flips` counts them. What the specification left open: the viewer's bounds and how mu is chosen. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.8).

Decision: five panels in this order, the preset's first panel moved to the top: orbit, matrices (with a node k picker of its own), relations, signed move (the move matrix of node k beside `E_k - F_k + P_k^0`), string. Presets `default`, `string-viewer` (A2 through (2, 0)), `relation-checker`, `signed-move`; the panel order and the matrix node are not part of the state nor of a link (6.6 has no key for them). Link keys read: `z g c s w k q`; the keys of other tools (`v m x t r j e y d`) are ignored; a `g` or `k` that changes the board or node takes that board's and node's defaults for every field the link does not name; `c=p` is refused (the viewer plays numbers); `c` without `s` keeps the start; a board T12 does not offer and a Serre relation with equal nodes are refused with the notice (the codec accepts the latter; request to P1-A2). ## 2026-10-24 P5-A2: where each call runs, and the relation list (the coordinator's ruling)
Decision: `chevalleySerre` over the whole list is computed on the main thread only for orbits of at most 27 positions (`RELATIONS_MAIN_MAX = CAPS.matrixGridDim`; the largest is E6 nodes 1 and 6) and in the worker above (`engineCall('chevalleySerre', ..., relationsHint(board))`, a hint without `expectedItems` that whereToRun sends to the worker). The configured state of an instance computes its list on the main thread whatever the size, at build time and on hydration, so that no default state needs the worker. `minusculeMatrices`, `signedMoves`, `orbitGraph` and `stringThrough` stay on the main thread up to 2000 items (E-9 rule 1, their hints carry `expectedItems` from `orbitSize`); `play` is a legal play on a finite-type board (rule 2); a link's move list above 2000 is replayed in the worker (`positionsOf`). A pick builds the representation one engine call per task (decide, enumerate, sign, and the relation list for a node that is not minuscule with at most 27 positions) and then draws the panels one piece per task after a frame; the worker's call is posted in a task of its own and its reply taken in another, its two sides drawn one per task. What the specification left open: E-9 names `minusculeMatrices` an enumeration but not `chevalleySerre`; SPEC 7.6 bounds a main-thread call at 50 ms on a phone. Default used: the coordinator's choice (move the full list to the worker above a measured size). Measurements (Node, warm medians, whole build of one node): A2 0.9 ms; E6 node 1 6.1 ms (chevalleySerre 4.6); E7 node 7 8.4 ms (minusculeMatrices 0.6, chevalleySerre 7.3); D4 node 2 1.9; E7 node 2 112; E7 node 6 133; E8 node 8 42; B8 node 5 442 (minusculeMatrices 22.7, chevalleySerre 405); C8 node 5 473. In Chromium the first chevalleySerre of E7 node 7 after a pick took 14 ms at full speed, about 56 ms with the processor slowed four times: over the budget, hence 27. Browser results with the processor slowed four times (`T12.spec.ts`, repeated in scratch runs): picking E7 (56 positions), E6 (27), D4, B3, C3, G2 and E8 gives no long task. Residual, reported: on the largest orbits built (B8, C8, D8 nodes of 1120 and 1792 positions) reading the worker's reply (368 records with 57120 entries for B8 node 5, deserialized by `lib/worker.ts`) is one task of 54 to 58 ms at full speed in some runs, and with the processor slowed four times `minusculeMatrices` on 1792 positions (about 25 to 33 ms at full speed) and that reply are tasks of 100 to 270 ms. Neither is `chevalleySerre` on the main thread; the requests ask for a verdicts-only or one-relation form of `chevalleySerre` (P5-A1) and for the E-9 sizing of `minusculeMatrices` (MERGE).

## 2026-10-25 P5-A2: hydration (review finding 4, request 10)
Decision: hydration computes the facts of the node only (`representationOf(spec, node, 'facts')`: minusculeNodes, orbitSize and legal play); no relation list, move matrix, signed move or grid is computed or drawn in the hydration task (unit test with a counting engine on E7 node 7, the configured state of M8). The five panels and the two tables of the table view are the server's markup: each is rendered on its own at build time (`t12/static.ts`, `staticMarkup` through `svelte/server` and `StaticHost.svelte`; the import is dropped from the client bundle) and kept as it is by an `{@html}` block that the client does not compare. The server writes a digest of the configured relation (board, node, code, holds, the counts and its two sides as `[row, column, value]`) as island data, `<script type="application/json" data-t12-digest="uid">`, read before hydration; captions, the verdict, the counts and Download data read it while the list is not computed. After hydration the parts are drawn from the state (`activate`): first the parts and pieces with form controls, in tasks that follow one another without waiting for a frame (the relation checker, the panel of E, F and H, the string viewer, its board, history and typed start), then, each after a frame, the matrices (the two sides, E, F and H), the line and the table view. A drawn MatrixView takes over the server's table (`adopt`) while its props are the ones it was first given, and a piece of the server's markup stands for a piece not drawn yet only while the state it shows is unchanged (`pieceKey`: board, node, and the node k or the relation). The relation list is computed when the reader asks for another relation (on the main thread within the bound, in the worker above) or for the data; the signed moves when the node k changes or for the data. The options of the two pickers are one markup string each. No `content-visibility` on a panel: a panel inserted later was laid out and then locked, a task of 37 to 44 ms measured; the matrix boxes keep theirs. `data-drawn="true"` on `.t12` when no run of steps is in progress (the suites wait for it). Why the controls first: Chromium's autofill reads every form control of the page about 100 ms after one is added or removed, and on M8, with twelve instances in the page, each reading was a task of about 70 ms with the processor slowed four times; drawn one per frame the controls caused three readings, drawn together two.

## 2026-10-25 RT-FIX-P5-history: on popstate the recorded state is the one the tool shows, and what it loads is not written (P5-RT-04-01)
Decision: site/src/lib/history.ts no longer replaces an instance's recorded state with the codec's reading of the bar on popstate. Each instance's handler still receives `decodeState(location.search, tool, defaults, { prefix })` and its notice, as the P1-A2 record says; the tool re-reads the bar by the codec or by its own rules (T10's `admit`, T11's and T12's `admitLink`) and loads what it admits. The recorded state stays the last state the tool reported through ToolFrame's `stateChanged`, so a tool that finds its state unchanged (T12 and T11 return early in `readLink`, T10 only restarts its load) keeps a recorded state that is on screen, and Copy link and the export footer (both `linkFor`) encode it. A state the tool loads reaches `stateChanged` like any other; history.ts records, for every instance, the count of the reader's actions at the popstate, and a change that arrives before the reader acts again is that instance's load: recorded, not written, on a page opened from a link or not. The next press, key or input inside a tool frame, or an example loaded, makes the next change the reader's, as in the rule of RT-FIX-P4-shared. What the specification left open: SPEC 7.4 says when the bar is written ("after a move") and that Copy link encodes the current state; the plan (P1-A2 5.6) adds "Nothing is written on load or hydration"; neither says how history.ts learns the state a tool shows after the back button. Why: the codec does not know the rules by which T10 to T12 admit a link (P5-A2 records T12's), so its reading was not the state shown: after one press of the skip link Copy link reopened T12 to another start and relation, a bare link, or LINK_NOTICE on T11. The same cause made the back button write: T12 loaded its link's state, which differed from the codec's reading recorded a moment before, so after a move it counted as the reader's change and the bar of the entry the reader returned to was rewritten half a second later (`/tools/rep/?k=2` became `?z=1&g=A2&c=n&s=0,1&w=&k=2&q=ef:2,2`); T10 and T11 share that path. On the plain-codec tools nothing changes: the state they load is the codec's reading, recorded before as it is now, and not written either way. No interface changes: the exports of history.ts, the props of ToolFrame and the handlers of T10, T11 and T12 are unchanged; no tool or ToolFrame needed an edit. The phase 4 rules hold: nothing is written on load or hydration, one replaceState per settled burst, the per-page count of the reader's actions (site/tests/unit/history.test.ts, history-after-action.spec.ts and history-no-write-on-load.spec.ts unchanged and passing).
Known limit, as in RT-FIX-P4-shared: a press inside a tool frame between a popstate and the end of an asynchronous load (T10's facts computed in tasks, T11's or T12's replay in the worker, T8's and T15's async loadLink) makes the rest of that load count as the reader's, so the bar is written with the state then shown, normalised.
Tests: site/tests/unit/history-popstate-copy-link.test.ts (the lens's four cases, T12 back to its link after a move, a plain-codec tool after back), site/tests/e2e/history-popstate.spec.ts (the lens's five T12 cases, the SVG export footer on T12, T11 and T10, and the back button after a move on T12) and site/tests/e2e/history-popstate-sweep.spec.ts (the lens's sixteen tool routes).

## 2026-10-25 RT-FIX-P5-toolchain: the prebuild holds the release report (P5-RT-12-01)
Decision: `site/src/lib/openItemsReport.mjs` gains `holdForReleaseBuild()`. In a release build (`RELEASE` set, the rule of `isReleaseBuild`) it rewrites a release report already on disk, JSON and Markdown, with `complete: false` and without its `linkCheck`, every other field (`generatedAt`, `buildId`, items and pages) unchanged; with no release report on disk, or outside a release build, it writes nothing. `scripts/katex-assets.mjs`, the first command of the root prebuild, calls it first, before it looks for KaTeX, so before anything of `RELEASE=1 npm run build` can fail. The Astro build's start hook then writes the report of the new build as before, its done hook marks it complete, and the postbuild holds and settles it (RT-FIX-P4-toolchain, unchanged). A release build that stops anywhere before the Astro build starts (in the prebuild, or while the site's configuration loads) therefore leaves the earlier report refused by `npm run report` ("comes from a release build that did not finish"), and, since its `linkCheck` is gone, a link check run by hand (`RELEASE=1 npm run postbuild`) does not mark it complete again. `scripts/report.mjs`, root `package.json` and the prebuild line are unchanged. What the specification left open: what `npm run report` does after a release build that failed before the Astro build started (SPEC 7.3 and 7.7 are silent; the decisions RT-FIX-P3-toolchain-b "a complete release report" and RT-FIX-P4-toolchain "the postbuild holds the release report" give the reason). Default used: none. Reason: a release build is prebuild, the Astro build and the postbuild, and a failed release build is never presented as the release report. Of the two fixes the finding proposes, this one (the first prebuild step marks the report) needs no change to root `package.json`, whose prebuild line `site/tests/unit/scripts.test.ts` asserts exactly, and no marker file for `report.mjs` to compare; a separate first prebuild command would have changed both. The report is marked rather than deleted, so that `npm run report` refuses it with the same message as after a failed postbuild and the owner can still read the earlier pages in `reports/open-items-report.md`, which then says "Incomplete". A preview build still never touches a release report (DECISIONS.md P0-A4).

## 2026-10-25 RT-FIX-P5-t12-content: the sentence for a board with no minuscule node (P5-RT-08-05)

## 2026-10-25 RT-FIX-P5-t12-content: the text of the panel of the move beside its signed version (P5-RT-09-01)
Decision: the panel's sentences depend on m, the largest number at node k in the orbit (`largestAt`; written by `signedNote`). When m is at most 1, as on every minuscule node: `Firing node k permutes the positions: its matrix is E_k + F_k + P_k, where P_k keeps the positions whose number at node k is 0. The group element exp(E_k) exp(−F_k) exp(E_k) is E_k − F_k + P_k: the same matrix with one sign changed in each pair. Its square multiplies each position by −1 to the power of its number at node k.` Otherwise: `Some position has the number m at node k, and firing node k moves it m steps at once, which the single steps E_k and F_k miss. So the matrix of the move is not E_k + F_k + P_k, where P_k keeps the positions whose number at node k is 0, and the signed matrix E_k − F_k + P_k is not exp(E_k) exp(−F_k) exp(E_k).` The condition is exact: firing moves mu by mu_k steps, so the firing matrix is E_k + F_k + P_k^0 exactly when every |mu_k| is at most 1; then the orbit splits under node k into pairs (mu_k = 1 and −1) and fixed positions (mu_k = 0), on which (I + E_k)(I − F_k)(I + E_k) = E_k − F_k + P_k^0 and its square is (−1)^{H_k}; a position with |mu_k| of 2 or more lies outside every entry of E_k, F_k and P_k^0, so E_k − F_k + P_k^0 is singular while the exponentials are invertible. The square sentence is therefore also shown on the nodes that are not minuscule where m is at most 1 (B3 node 1 at k = 1, for example), where it holds; the regression test checks every claim against the engine's matrices at every k of every built node of A3, B2, B3, C3, D4, D5, G2 and F4. The sentences are markup built from numbers and fixed words only, shown with {@html} (the same text written with fourteen subscripts in the template took /tools/rep/ over its 90 kB). The previous text (decisions/P5-A2.md records only the panel's order and content, "panels, presets, link keys") is replaced. What the specification left open: SPEC 4 T12 names the panel ("the move matrix beside its signed version") and not its text. Reason: finding P5-RT-09-01.

## 2026-10-25 RT-FIX-P5-t12-content: "Dimension" and the positions of the orbit (P5-RT-09-02, P5-RT-13-03)
Decision: the facts line shows `Dimension: N` with N the dimension of the representation whose highest weight is the fundamental position of the node (`representationDimension`, the engine's `weylDimension`; `data-out="dimension"`; 28 on D4 node 2, 248 on E8 node 8, 3875 on E8 node 1), and beside it `Positions in the orbit: M` with M the orbit's size, which is also the size of the matrices T12 builds (`data-out="orbit-size"`, a new name in `T12_OUTS` and in the comment block of `T12.spec.ts`). On a minuscule node the two are equal (F11); elsewhere the dimension is larger, by the positions the orbit leaves out. Download data's `dimension` is the representation's dimension on every node (it was the basis size, null on a node not built); `orbitSize` is unchanged. The SPEC uses "dimension" in two senses, the size of the matrices (4 T12 "as lists of nonzero entries above dimension 27"; 5.6 "Dimension for matrix grids | 27") and dim V(lambda) (4 T12 acceptance; 2.7 F9); which one a reader-facing "Dimension" should be is for the owner. Options: (a) as done, both numbers each under the name of what it counts; (b) "Dimension" on a minuscule node only and the positions of the orbit alone elsewhere (the finding's proposedFix; the reproducers of both findings then fail, since they read `data-out="dimension"` on nodes that are not minuscule); (c) (a) with a sentence on the positions the orbit leaves out. Recommendation: (a), which keeps "Dimension" for the representation's dimension, as the coordinator asked, and lets the reader set T12 against M8's 248 and 26. `weylDimension` was already in the engine chunk that /tools/rep/ loads (shared with T5), so the import costs a few bytes. This adds to decisions/P5-A2.md, "data-out names and the selects" (the name `orbit-size`) and changes the meaning of `dimension` in "Download data". What the specification left open: the readouts of T12. Reason: findings P5-RT-09-02 and P5-RT-13-03.

## 2026-10-25 RT-FIX-P5-t12-content: the default start (P5-RT-10-03)
Decision: the default start of T12 is all ones, as SPEC 6.6 gives the field `start` ("default: all ones for numbers"), on /tools/rep/ (the preset `default`: `start: [1, 1]`) and after a pick of a board or a node (`defaultsFor`, and so a link whose `g` or `k` changes the board or the node, admitLink unchanged); `defaultStart` replaces `omegaStart`. No [D] passage gives another value (4.0 Board pickers and Configuration defer to "the tool's defaults" without a value; SPEC 4 T12 names none), and no behaviour of SPEC 4 T12 depends on the start: the string viewer takes any position, and all ones has mu_i = 1 at every node. An author's start stays (M8's b1, b2 and b9). The presets `relation-checker` and `signed-move` keep (1, 0) and `string-viewer` (2, 0): they are figure configurations of M8 (b4 and b8 use the first two) and neither the default state of the route nor a pick, as the finding's proposedFix suggests ("keep omega_i for the presets and M8 instances that name it"). M8's instances that give a board and a node but no start (b3, b5, b6, b7, b10, b11, b12) take the tool's default for their board, as 6.6 says of an absent key, so their string viewers start at all ones; no sentence or test of M8 reads those starts. This replaces the start in two entries of decisions/P5-A2.md: "boards offered, the picker, the default state" (`start: [1, 0]` and "the start omega_i" on a pick) and "the string viewer" ("from a start that is omega_i by default"); their other choices stand. Request: the comment of `admitLink` in t12/model.ts still says "the start omega_k"; this fixer was asked not to edit admitLink, so the owner of the popstate hand-off of this round (or MERGE) changes "(the start omega_k, no moves, the default relation)" to "(the start all ones of SPEC 6.6, no moves, the default relation)". What the specification left open: nothing, by 6.6; decisions/P5-A2.md had recorded the start as left open (plan, instruction 5.2). Reason: finding P5-RT-10-03.

## 2026-10-25 RT-FIX-P5-t12-a11y: the string viewer's board box is as wide as the figure (P5-RT-05-01)
Decision: on T12 the board's box of SPEC 6.1 is the figure, as for every other tool ("2026-10-10 P0-A5: size rule and the reserved box"): the string viewer's `.board-host` runs over its panel's padding and border (12 and 1 pixels each side, `margin-inline: -13px`) and is itself the inline-size container from which Board.svelte reads its grid unit, so that W is the viewport width below 400 pixels (43 on seven columns and 38 on eight at 320; 43 on eight at 360). The panels keep their own container for the 600-pixel layout of the matrices. This holds at every width, so the unit is never read from a box narrower than the figure. What the specification left open: 6.1 [D] defines W as "the width of the board's box" and fixes it below 400 pixels only. Default used: none. ## 2026-10-25 RT-FIX-P5-t12-a11y: a scroll box keeps the focus when its panel is drawn again (P5-RT-05-02)
Decision: each drawing step of T12 (runSteps) notes the scroll box of the figure that has the focus (`role="group"`, `tabindex="0"`), by the data-out of its MatrixView or orbit drawing, and when the step leaves the focus on `<body>` it gives it to the box with that data-out drawn in its place (the server's box moved into the live panel, then the live MatrixView's box). Only scroll boxes are noted: before hydration they are the only tab stops of the server's markup, every control being disabled (4.0, 7.4). What the specification left open: 7.5 A-1 (WCAG 2.4.3) names no focus target when an element is replaced. Default used: none. Reason: P5-RT-05-02, the expected of the finding ("the focus stays on the box the reader is on, or on its live replacement").

## 2026-10-25 RT-FIX-P5-t12-a11y: which replies of the worker are announced (P5-RT-05-03)
Decision: when a relation pick is announced as "checked in the background" (its verdict is not known on the main thread), T12 keeps that representation and the pick's announcer; the worker's list for it then announces the relation sentence with its verdict ("...: the two sides are equal." or "not equal."). A list that arrives after a board or node pick, or after a link, is not announced: the pick sentence (which already says whether the relations hold or fail) is announced then, and the announcer of `site/src/lib/a11y.ts` keeps only the last text given within 500 ms, so a second announcement would often replace it; for the same reason the move to the first failing relation (failingDefault, C5 to C8 node n) is not announced. A failure of the worker is shown ("not checked" and the line below it) but not announced: announcing it (with a longer selector of the focus rule, dropped at the same time) cost 70 bytes of the shared limit of /tools/rep/ (below). What the specification left open: 4.0 "a polite live region announces each result" does not say which results of a background computation are announced, nor how two results within the coalescing time of A-4 are joined. Default used: none. Reason: P5-RT-05-03 and the 90 kB limit of /tools/rep/ (7.6, never raised): 89757 bytes at the base of this branch, 89905 with this branch (148 bytes for this rule and the focus rule of P5-RT-05-02), and the content fix of the round adds about 72 more (89830 at its own base, by the coordinator's measure), which leaves about 20 bytes after both.

Reason: P5-RT-06-01; a T12 root was accepted as "board" through its string viewer alone.

## 2026-10-25 RT-FIX-P5-t12-perf: a link's state reads the facts of its node, and the rest is built one engine call per task (P5-RT-07-01)
Decision: `admitLink` validates a link with `new T12Tool(configOf(state), { defer: true })`, the facts of the node only (it used `need: 'staged'`: `minusculeMatrices` and the signed moves of every node at once), and finds the board and node of the link (`targetOf`) before it computes any default, so that a link whose `k` names another node of the board named by `g` no longer computes the defaults of the board's default node too. `load()` builds the tool with the facts only and swaps it at once (the facts line, the string viewer and History show the link's state on hydration, as before); when the panels are drawn from the state (`stage`), the steps of `representationSteps` (decide, enumerate, sign one node per task above 300 positions, the list on the main thread) run first, one per task, the panels waiting meanwhile, then a step that tells the derived values the matrices are there, then the panels piece by piece; on the node shown (a link that changes only the start, the moves or the relation, read on hydration, when the configured state has the facts only) the matrices are built in a task of their own before the relation is drawn. `representationSteps` returns no step when everything it computes is computed, so a load after a pick adds no task. What the specification left open: SPEC 7.6 bounds an engine call at a long task and says nothing of how a load is shaped; decisions/P5-A2.md records that a pick builds the representation one engine call per task and that hydration computes the facts only. Default used: the lens's proposed fix (validate with 'facts', build in `load()` with 'facts', run the steps before the panels). A first variant that built the representation before reading the link (the figure keeping the configured state meanwhile, as a pick keeps the previous one) was dropped: two tests of `T12.spec.ts` read the link's state right after hydration (the dimension of G2 node 1, the end of a play of 2001 moves replayed in the worker). Residual, by design: a link to a node that is not minuscule whose relation list stays on the main thread (at most `RELATIONS_MAIN_WORK`, 2500 units of work, positions times records: node 2 of D4 is 24 by 88) still computes its matrices and that list where the link is read, through `defaultsFor`, because its default relation, a field of the state when the link has no `q`, is the first failing relation of that list; the configured state of an instance does the same through `configuredState`. Measurements (Chromium at full speed, 360 by 800, medians of three runs against a link to E7 node 7 as control, the adopted test): before, at `b6b538d`, load 0.5, the hydration task of a link to E7 node 6 was 77 ms (control 0), C8 node 7 78 (52), B8 node 7 72 (0), D8 node 3 66 (0); after, at load 0.5 to 1.0, it was not a long task in every run, and the lens's script (`redteam-RT-07-t12-link-task.mjs`, run from the scratch directory on the build) found no long task after hydration in 15 link loads of E7:6, C8:7, B8:7, D8:3 and E8:8. With the processor slowed four times the island's hydration task stays long whatever the link (Svelte's hydration, the panels taken down, the facts): E7 node 6 192, 222, 285 ms after against 400, 403, 569 before; E8 node 8 237, 344, 454 after against 291, 312, 356 before (the island's own hydration, about 100 to 150 ms there, dominates the noise).

## 2026-10-25 RT-FIX-P5-t12-perf: one board object per name in T12 (P5-RT-07-02)
Decision: `t12/model.ts` keeps the board object of each name it has resolved (`boardOf`, a map of at most the 32 names of `t12/boards.ts`; boards are frozen), and every board T12 uses comes from it: `representationSteps`, `representationOf`, `defaultsFor`, the `T12Tool` constructor, the link's target and the default node of a picked board. A pick then classifies a board once when it is first loaded and never again on the page; the instances of M8 share the objects. `forgetRepresentations`, the test seam of a new page, empties the map too. `site/src/lib/state.ts` (`resolveBoard`, `resolvedThisRun`) is unchanged, so no other tool changes. What the specification left open: SPEC 5.6 says "once when the board is loaded" and E-11 keeps the verdict per board object; neither says how a tool whose load spans tasks keeps the object. Default used: the lens's second proposal (keep the object), as a map by name rather than per generation, which is smaller and bounded. Test method: the browser test counts the engine's `classifyUncached` with a DevTools breakpoint whose condition counts and never pauses, set by URL on the statement that checks the board, which the test finds in the engine's chunk (`_astro/src.*.js`) by the message that statement throws; the lens's script placed the same logpoint through a source-map build, which the suite does not make. Before: 3 computations per pick (E6), as the lens found; after: 1 for each of E6, E7, D4, B8, G2 and for C8 after a link.

## 2026-10-25 MERGE: the phase 5 red-team round, fixes merged

## 2026-10-25 P5-A2: the steps of a pick, split again (G5 rerun repair)
Decision: the steps of a pick that made tasks over 50 ms with the processor slowed four times are split or lightened. What the traces showed (Chromium's tracing through the DevTools protocol, devtools.timeline and the V8 sampling profiler on a source-map build of 00e6a4c, 360 by 800, a pick from the default A2 page as `T12.spec.ts` makes it, at a load of 0.5 to 1.5): on E6, node 1, each of the seven grids of 27 by 27 (E, F, H, the two sides of the relation, the move and the signed move) was written, parsed and drawn in one task of 20 to 61 ms, of which parsing its markup took 10 to 22 ms; the first of them (E) took 35 to 62 ms with a minor collection of 6 to 10 ms, and the observer's long tasks of the traced picks were these grids and, once, the mount of the string viewer's Board. Further steps of 21 to 56 ms on E6 and E7: the orbit panel together with its layout (23 to 56), the task that loads the state at the end of a pick with the pickers' options (21 to 46), the take-down of the previous panels (21 to 39), the board's resolution with its default node (22 to 36), the two tables of the table view (25 to 29). Thread time equals wall time in these tasks (the throttling is spent on the thread), and the same work varies by a factor of two between picks, so any task of 25 ms or more can pass 50 ms.
What changed (no change to what T12 shows when drawn, its hooks, link keys, the engine, the history layer or another tool): each grid is built outside the page (MatrixView `adoptableTable`: `matrixTableParts`, about `ADOPT_CELLS` = 250 cells parsed a task, in tasks that follow one another) and its MatrixView takes the table over (`adopt`) only when its props are those it was built from (`matrixInput`, the one function the view and the builder use); the orbit's layout has a task of its own and its SVG layers are written when shown (`orbitSvgLayers`); a picked board is resolved in a task before its default node is found; the state and the tool loaded at the end of a pick are made, with the string viewer's line and the dimension (now kept per representation), in a task of their own, and the pickers show the board and node being built one task before the state loads (`picked`), so that the loading task writes no option; the previous panels are taken down in two tasks; the orbit's table is drawn 20 rows a task and the board's table a task after it. What the specification left open: SPEC 7.6 bounds a task, not how a pick is shaped. Default used: none of section 10; the plan's rule of one engine call or one piece per task, carried further.
Measurements: the two long-task tests of `T12.spec.ts`, `--repeat-each 40 --workers 1`, against `astro preview` on port 7030 (failures of 40 runs, E6 then E7, the load average before and after): before (00e6a4c) at the root 3 and 2 (1.15 to 1.45), at the CI base `/mutation_game/` 3 and 0 (1.06 to 1.34); after at the root 0 and 1 (0.83 to 1.47), at the CI base 1 and 2 (1.30 to 1.46). Each failing task was a single task of 50 to 60 ms. Runs of the same picks without a trace, with a MutationObserver telling the steps apart, at the CI base after the change (load 1.0 to 1.3): E6 no long task in 40 picks; E7 a long task in 3 of 40, each the step that mounts the string viewer's shared Board (54, 54, 87 ms). Before, at the root (30 picks of E7, load 0.9 to 1.6): the Board's mount (75, 66), the take-down (51), the loading task (57), the orbit panel (66, 53).
Residual, reported: the mount of the shared Board of the string viewer (Board.svelte with seven Node.svelte, Roads.svelte with six roads and seven hit buttons, on E7) is one Svelte component mount, 21 to 60 ms with the processor slowed four times in 50 traced picks (median 32), no collection in it; the sampling profiler puts about half in Node.svelte, a quarter in Roads.svelte (its attributes spread) and a sixth in the buttons, a third of it in the DOM calls (setAttribute, cloneNode, insertion). After two earlier picks on the page the same mount takes at most 26 ms (8 picks): the cost is the first runs of the Board's code. T12 cannot split one component's mount; drawing the string panel first changed its median from 27 to 25 ms in 20 picks each, within the noise, and was not kept. The task that follows the change of the picker is Playwright's `selectOption` (its injected script about 60 percent of the samples) with T12's handler and the building line, 20 to 43 ms in traces. The 170 ms task of the G5 rerun (`14b-e2e-ci-base.log`) began within a few ms of the pick, where only that task runs; with two workers the suite's other worker was loading tool pages at the time; with a second browser loading tool pages here the same task took 20 to 31 ms, so the 170 ms was not reproduced at a load of 2 or less. The test, its threshold and its throttling are unchanged. Size: `/tools/rep/` and M8 87831 B of 90000 (86803 at the base).

## 2026-10-25 P5-A2: what a choice does while a pick builds (G5 rerun repair)
Decision: a choice made while a pick builds acts on what the pickers show, and the pickers always show the pick in progress or the state. Cause (the review of the first G5 repair, results 2e): that repair lists the picked board's labels in the node picker one step before the state loads (`picked`), but `pickNode` built `spec`, the board of the state shown. A node chosen in that frame was built on the board shown: a label that board lacks threw `label 3 is not on this board` inside a step, so the run of steps stopped and the tool stayed on `Building A2, node 3.` with `data-drawn="false"` and its panels waiting; a label it has built the wrong board (from E7 node 7, node 4 chosen from E6's list built E7 node 4). Checking every control found two more causes, also on 00e6a4c: the board picker's value followed the state only, and Svelte writes a select only when its value changes, so a load that ended a pick on the board shown left the board picker on the board picked (a node of the board shown chosen just after a board; a typed start in the frame before the panels are taken down); and `load()` left the line `Building E6.` when a link (popstate) or a typed start ended a pick.
What changed: (1) a node of the node picker is built on the board whose labels the picker lists (`pickerSpec`): the board shown until the picked board's labels are listed, that board after; a node chosen while the list is still the board shown's ends the pick of the other board (the reader's last choice wins, as with a link), and a label the list does not hold is refused (only a script can send one). (2) The pickers' values follow the pick from the reader's choice (`aim`: the board, and the node once known) until the state loads, then the state; `build()` writes them in the reader's task (`flushSync`), so that two choices within one task still move the selects; a pick of another board in the frame after `picked` lists the board shown's labels again until its own are known. (3) A load ends a pick in progress: its line goes and the pickers show the state loaded (a link by popstate, a typed start, the pick's own end). Unchanged, checked: the relation selects, the node k select, the board's nodes, the table's buttons and undo (the button and the key u) act on the state shown in the frame before the previous panels are taken down, and the pick then replaces that state; from the next frame the panels holding them are taken down, so none can be reached later in the pick. Not changed: a link whose state is the state shown is ignored by `readLink` as before and the pick goes on; the address bar then keeps the link until the reader acts (the history layer's rule after a popstate, RT-FIX P5-RT-04-01). Making such a link end the pick would also end a pick on every T12 instance of M8 whenever the reader follows a fragment link, which fires popstate in Chromium. What the specification left open: what a control does while a pick builds. Default used: none of section 10; the reader's last choice wins.
Tests (`T12.spec.ts`, regressions): `a node chosen while a pick builds is built on the board whose labels the node picker lists, and the pickers show it` (node 3 chosen as soon as the node picker lists E6's labels while the facts still name A2 gives E6 node 3; node 2 chosen in the task of the pick gives A2 node 2 with both pickers on it) and `a link or a typed start that loads a state while a pick builds ends the pick: its line goes and the pickers show the state` (popstate to `?g=D4&k=2` in that frame and in the task of the pick; a typed start (2, 0) in the task of the pick). On a build of 68d93ef both fail (E6 expected, A2 received; the line `Building E6.` left); both pass after. The review's `race.mjs` and `link-race.mjs` and a scratch script of 24 cases (a node in that frame and in the pick's task, a second board in that frame then a node, every other control in both moments, links at 40 and 300 ms, in that frame and in the pick's task, a link to the state shown): on 68d93ef 8 cases end on the wrong board, with the pickers and the state disagreeing, with the building line left or with the page error; after, all 24 settle with the pickers on the state, no building line and no error. The settled states of the review's `compare.mjs` (12 scenarios and M8's instances) and the server HTML of `/tools/rep/` and M8 are identical to 68d93ef's.
Measurements: the two long-task tests, `--repeat-each 20 --workers 1` at the root, four batches of each build in alternation (1-minute load 0.8 to 2.1 during the batches): after, E6 77 of 80 and E7 75 of 80 (single tasks of 50 to 63 ms); 68d93ef, E6 79 of 80 and E7 78 of 80 (50 to 102 ms). Traced picks (the first repair's `pick-trace.mjs`, base and repair in alternation, 30 picks of E7 and 15 of E6 each): on both builds the long tasks are the mount of the string viewer's shared Board (E7: median 32 ms on both, longest 57 ms at 68d93ef and 63 ms after), and the task of the reader's change, in which this repair now writes the pickers and the building line, takes the same time (E7 median 28 ms at 68d93ef, 27 ms after). The difference between the counts is the noise of a shared machine (one-sided Fisher test about 0.1); the residual of the first repair stands. The tests, their thresholds and their throttling are unchanged. Size: `/tools/rep/` and M8 87910 B of 90000 (87831 at 68d93ef).

## 2026-10-25 P6-A1: the order of checks in the five functions
Decision: each of `theta`, `shadow2`, `admissibility`, `satake` and `restrictedBoard` first checks the shape of its arguments (RangeError: `tau` not a permutation of `0..n-1`, `black` with a repeated, fractional or out-of-range position, a population of the wrong length or with a non-integer entry), then calls `requireGcm` and `requireFinite` of `guards.ts` (NeedsTwoWayRoads, NotFiniteType), before any computation; `satake` and `restrictedBoard` then judge admissibility and throw `NotAdmissible`. What the specification left open: the instruction says "Decide through guards.ts (requireGcm, requireFinite) as the first statement, never by running an enumeration into a cap"; P2-A1 recorded the engine-wide order "argument shape, then kind, then class", which P3-A1, P4-A1 and P5-A1 kept. Default used: the engine-wide order, reading "the first statement" as "before any computation" (the argument checks are a few comparisons and run no enumeration). Reason: one order across the public API, so that a malformed argument is a RangeError on every kind of board, as for `fold`, `minusculeMatrices` and the rest. Reported under `deviations` so that MERGE can decide; no acceptance test depends on the order (the guard tests use well-formed diagrams).

## 2026-10-25 P6-A1: the Reason records (codes, nodes, value)
Decision: `reasons` has an entry only for each failed item, in the order `symmetry`, `condition_1`, `condition_2`, `condition_3`. Nodes are positions, increasing, never labels (E-7):
- `symmetry`: `{ code: 'not-a-symmetry', nodes }`, the positions `i` for which some `j` has `C[tau[i]][tau[j]] != C[i][j]` (on A4 with nodes 1 and 2 exchanged: `[0, 1, 2]`).
- `condition_1`: `{ code: 'not-an-involution', nodes }` with the positions `i` such that `tau[tau[i]] != i` whenever tau is not an involution (it takes precedence, as in the oracle); otherwise `{ code: 'moves-black-set', nodes }` with the black positions whose image is white.
- `condition_2`: `{ code: 'differs-from-minus-wX', nodes }`, the black positions `i` with `w_X(alpha_i) != -alpha_tau(i)` (the oracle's `bad2`).
- `condition_3`: `{ code: 'not-an-integer', nodes, value }`, the white positions fixed by tau whose `<alpha_i, rho_X^vee>` is not an integer (the oracle's `bad3`); `value` is the fraction through `ratToString` when one node fails (`'-1/2'`), and the fractions in the order of `nodes` joined by `'; '` when several fail (A5, black nodes 1, 2, 4: nodes `[2, 4]`, value `'-3/2; -1/2'`, the oracle's own separator).
No other code carries `value`. What the specification left open: SPEC 5.2 gives the codes and one `value`, not the nodes of the first three codes nor the format for several failing nodes. Default used: the plan's readings (instruction 5.5 table and the paragraph on several nodes). Reason: the tool writes the sentence from these data with labels (SPEC 4 T13, E-7). Named in `openQuestions` for confirmation.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A1: NotAdmissible and the oracle's asserts
Decision: `satake` and `restrictedBoard` throw `new NotAdmissible(record, 'not admissible: <key>')`, the key being the first failed item in the oracle's order `symmetry`, `condition_1`, `condition_2`, `condition_3` (oracle `admissible`), with the full `Admissibility` record as `data` (P0-A2's field). The oracle's asserts inside `satake` and `restricted_board` are kept as `EngineError` with the oracle's text (`theta does not preserve the roots`, `theta is not an involution`, `theta(positive non-compact root) must be negative`, `multiplicity not constant on a length class`, `a simple restricted root is never twice a restricted root`; the count check of compact roots as the oracle's tuple `(n_compact, phiX)`; a restricted Cartan entry that is not an integer). None is reachable with an admissible pair of a finite board (the golden suite runs all of them on the 167 records). What the specification left open: the message. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.2 "Errors"). Reason: E-10.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A1: restricted_board is named by identify, not by classifyRestricted
Decision: `restricted_board` and `restricted_orbits_in_bourbaki_order` come from `identify` on the restricted board (the oracle's `identify_labelled(Cbar)`), called only when there is at least one orbit and the restricted Cartan matrix is connected; otherwise both are `null`. `restricted_type` is `classifyRestricted`'s name (`BC1`, `BC2`, `B2`, ...). So a BC_r system has `restricted_board` `B_r` (`A1` for r = 1) with no special case, and every rank 2 board with two lengths is `B2`; the C2 renaming and the reversed orbit list are `satakeRecord`'s (P6-A2), never `satake`'s. What the specification left open: the roster says "restricted_board named by classifyRestricted (B_r for BC_r, A1 for r = 1)". Default used: the oracle and SPEC 6.4 (instruction trap 24). Reason: wiring `classifyRestricted` to `restricted_board` would store `BC2` where the golden record has `B2`; the roster phrase describes the result, not the function.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A1: the restricted board object (E-7 row "folded board, restricted board")
Decision: `restrictedBoard(d).board` is built directly, as P4-A1 built the folded board: `{ n: m, cartan, labels, kind, arith: SafeInt, name }`, frozen, `cartan` in the order of the orbits (so `cartanNumbers(board)` is the golden `restricted_cartan`), `kind` from `boardKind` (always `gcm` here); when `m > 0` and `components(board)` has one entry, `identify` gives `labels[order[k]] = k + 1` and the name; otherwise labels `1..m` in orbit order and no name. A compact form gives `orbits`, `simpleRestrictedRoots2`, `cartan`, `compositeWords` all `[]` and a board with `n: 0`, labels `[]`, no name; `satake` then reports `restricted_cartan` `[]` (an empty list, as the golden record of su(4)), not `null`. The composite word of orbit O is the word of w_X followed by the longest word of X u O, played left to right on populations with `applyWord(..., 'mutation')`; its reduced length is `length - 2 * wx.length` (tested also as the number of positive roots it sends to negative ones). What the specification left open: the board object, and the result for a compact form. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.7). Reason: E-7 and T13's drawing in Bourbaki order.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A1: shadows, classes and multiplicities
Decision: shadows are kept doubled (`shadow2`, integer vectors) everywhere: the multiset `restr` is keyed by the doubled shadow, `classifyRestricted` is called on the distinct doubled shadows with the board's `gram` (norms are 4 times the oracle's, the classes, their order and the name the same, since the classifier uses only norm ratios, counts and the "double is in the set" test), and each class's `mult` is the common count of the shadows whose norm, as `ratToString` text, equals the class's `form_value` (classes in `classifyRestricted`'s ascending order). `m_2lambda` is read at twice the simple doubled shadow. `real_rank` is the number of tau-orbits of white nodes (the oracle), and the span of the shadows is checked by test on all 167 records. What the specification left open: the scaling. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.6, traps 5, 14, 15). Reason: exact integers, no halves in the engine (trap 23).

## 2026-10-25 P6-A1: boards in Big arithmetic and the population argument
Decision: the contract types the diagram's board as `Board` (numbers), as every named finite board is. A finite board built by hand may carry `Big` (E-2: `fromAdjacency` gives `Big` unless the matrix equals a standard one); the five functions then work on a private SafeInt copy of its integer matrix (never returned), so `theta` and `satake` give the same numbers on a Big copy of a board (tested in property 9), and the guard is still called on the caller's board object (E-11 cache). A population entry may be a number (a safe integer, else RangeError for a fraction or EngineOverflow) or, tolerated at run time, a bigint in the safe range. Every result is plain numbers with `-0` written as `0`. The word of w_X is computed once per call with `finite.ts`'s unguarded `longestWord` after the function's own guard (as P3-A1's unguarded helpers), and nothing is cached across calls (E-5). What the specification left open: the arithmetic of the Satake functions (5.4 types `theta` as returning `number[]`). Default used: plan (E-2: entries are small on a finite board). Reason: T13 offers named boards; the copy costs nothing there and keeps a hand-built finite board from mixing bigint and number.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A5: the dynkin form, the arrows and the refusals
Decision: `exportLaTeX('dynkin', { type, black?, tau? })` writes `\dynkin`, then `[involutions={...}]` only when there is at least one arrow, one space, the family letter of `type` (never the rank), and the marks in braces: one character per label 1..n in Bourbaki order (label k is Bourbaki node k, E-7), `*` for a black node and `o` for a white one. An arrow is a pair {i, tau(i)} with i < tau(i) and both nodes white (2.15, 6.4 "pairs of white nodes"), written as the two labels concatenated, smaller first; pairs are joined by `;` with no space, in increasing order of the smaller label. A tau that moves black nodes adds nothing (the 3 and 5 of e6(-14), the swap of so(1,7), the flip of su(4)), so T13's screen toggle "show tau on black nodes" [D] does not change the export (plan reading). Refusals, each a `RangeError` naming the fault: data that is not an object; a `type` that is not one of A1..A8, B2..B8, C2..C8, D4..D8, E6..E8, F4, G2 (affine, twisted, `pentagon`, `square`, custom boards, other ranks); a label of `black` or `tau` that is not an integer from 1 to n; a label repeated in `black`; a `tau` of the wrong length, not a permutation, or whose square is not the identity; an unknown kind. Whether tau is a symmetry of the board and whether the pair is admissible are left to the caller (T13). A pair with a label above 9 throws rather than writing `{110}`; no type of the list reaches it. The package's named diagrams (`\dynkin E{VI}`), its short forms (`\dynkin E8`), ellipsis marks and the `fold` option are never written. What the specification left open: the punctuation beyond the three forms and the refusals. Reason: SPEC 6.7, 2.15; the instruction (5.1). Checked against all 167 records of the golden key `satake` (marks equal `black_nodes`, option equal `arrows`).

The letter is that of the name given: `C2` gives `\dynkin C{oo}`, `B2` gives `\dynkin B{oo}`; C2 is never normalised to B2. Default used: D19 (the name of the board the reader chose). Reason: 6.7 "explicit marks"; the instruction (5.1).

## 2026-10-25 P6-A5: the TikZ forms
Decision: `tikz-graph` (`{ nodes: { x, y, label? }[], edges: [i, j][], directed? }`): a `tikzpicture` holding one `\node[circle,draw,inner sep=1pt] (n<k>) at (x,y) {<label>};` per vertex in the order given, then one `\draw (n<i>) -- (n<j>);` per edge in the order given; a directed graph writes `\draw[->] (n<i>) -- (n<j>);`. `tikz-points` (`{ points: [x, y][], edges?, labels? }`): one `\fill (x,y) circle (1pt);` per point, a labelled point followed by `\node[anchor=south west,inner sep=1pt] at (x,y) {<label>};`, then one `\draw (x1,y1) -- (x2,y2);` per edge. Lines inside the picture are indented by two spaces; no `\usetikzlibrary`, no style. Coordinates are in the caller's units (centimetres), y up (a caller converting from SVG screen coordinates negates y), no scaling inside `exportLaTeX`; a number is written with at most 4 decimals, trailing zeros removed, minus zero as `0`; a coordinate that is not a finite number below 1e15 in size throws `RangeError`, as does an edge that does not join two given vertices or a label list of the wrong length. A label is written in full in math mode (`{$1$}`, as the instruction's example), with the TeX special characters escaped in forms valid in math mode with no package beyond TikZ: `\#`, `\$`, `\%`, `\&`, `\_`, `\{`, `\}`, and `\mbox{\textbackslash}`, `\mbox{\textasciitilde}`, `\mbox{\textasciicircum}`; an empty label gives `{}`. Deviation from the plan's wording: the plan says "`->` instead of `--` when directed"; `\draw (a) -> (b);` is not a TikZ path and would not compile, so the arrow is the option `[->]` on the same `--` path. What the specification left open: everything beyond "plain TikZ coordinates". Reason: the instruction (5.2) and the owner's compile check at G6.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A5: the Cite text
Decision: `citeText({ title, siteName, commit, date, link })` is one line, `<title>. <siteName>, site version <commit>, <date>. <link>`; a title that already ends with `.`, `?` or `!` gets no second stop. `citation(document.title, linkFor(instanceId))` composes it at the click: the title is the page's `document.title` without the suffix `: Two Games on a Dynkin Diagram` that Lesson.astro and Page.astro add (the tool routes and the embed routes use the tool's title alone); the site name is `SITE_NAME` in export.ts; the commit is `GIT_COMMIT`, the constant `exportJSON` writes, so the two never disagree; the date is the reader's local date at the click, ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` (reading: the access date of a web citation); the link is `linkFor(instanceId)`, the string Copy link copies, which carries no version (6.6). The text is shown in `data-out="citeText"` and copied with the Clipboard API inside `try`; the live region says `Citation copied.`, or `Citation shown below the tool.` when the copy fails (`The citation could not be made.` if export.ts could not be loaded). No shared constant of the site name existed (Base.astro, Page.astro, Lesson.astro and index.astro type it as text), so `SITE_NAME` is defined once in export.ts; request: a shared constant that the layouts read too. Default used: D1 (the working title of SPEC 1.7). Open question for the owner: whether the date should be the access date (as built) or the build date.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A2: the order of checks
Decision: `satakeCatalogue(name)`: `boardFromName(name)` (NotABoard on a name it does not know), then `requireGcm` and `requireFinite` (NeedsTwoWayRoads, NotFiniteType), before any entry is built. `satakeRecord(name, entry)`: `boardFromName(name)` (NotABoard), then the shape of the entry (RangeError: not an object, `tau` not a permutation of `0..n-1`, `black_nodes` with a repeated, fractional or out-of-range position), then the guard, then `satake` (NotAdmissible). `canonicalPair(d)` and `matchCatalogue(d)`: the shape of the diagram (RangeError), then the guard, then (matchCatalogue only) the name of the board (RangeError, below). What the specification left open: the instruction says "Decide through guards.ts as the first statement"; MERGE accepted for P6-A1 the engine-wide order "argument shape, then kind, then class", both before any computation. Default used: that order, so a malformed pair is a RangeError on every kind of board. Reason: one order across the public API (P2-A1 to P6-A1). A one-way board without a name still gives NeedsTwoWayRoads from matchCatalogue, as the guard runs before the name check.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A2: error classes of satakeCatalogue and satakeRecord on names
Decision: an unknown name (`Q7`, `A0`, `B1`, `D3`, `E9`, `BC2`, the empty string) throws NotABoard from `boardFromName`; an affine, twisted or preset name (`A2~`, `C2~`, `G2~`, `D4^(3)`, `pentagon`) builds a board that the guard refuses with NotFiniteType; both are `EngineError`. Ranks beyond 8 follow the parametric rules (`satakeCatalogue('A9')` has 8 entries, `D9` 11). What the specification left open: 5.6 speaks of boards, while these two functions take a name (plan). Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.2). Reason: the name is the board; named in `openQuestions`.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A2: matchCatalogue on a board without a name, or with a name that is not its own
Decision: `matchCatalogue` throws `RangeError('matchCatalogue needs a board built by boardFromName')` when the board has no `name` (a custom board of finite type, a sub-board, the C2 matrix built by `fromAdjacency`, the sum of two A2), and also (plan addition, defensive) when the board's integer matrix is not the standard matrix of its name (`cartan(name)`), so that a hand-made object carrying another board's name cannot match the wrong catalogue. `canonicalPair` needs no name and works on every finite board, in several pieces included. What the specification left open: 5.4 and T13 do not say what a board without a name matches. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.6); the matrix check is mine. Reason: the catalogue is organised by board name (6.4); T13 offers only named boards. Named in `openQuestions`.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A2: satakeRecord fields and the C2 adjustment
Decision: the record is a plain object built field by field in the oracle's order (`dynkin_type`, `cartan_label`, `real_form`, `black_nodes`, `tau`, `arrows`, `tau_moves_black_nodes`, `restricted_type_display`, then the 19 fields of `satake` copied by name), which is also the key order of the golden records. `dynkin_type` is the name given; `black_nodes` a sorted copy; `tau` a copy; `arrows` the pairs `[min(i, tau[i]), max(i, tau[i])]` for white `i` with `tau[i] != i`, each once, sorted lexicographically; `tau_moves_black_nodes` is true when some black `i` has `tau[i] != i`. The adjustment of 6.4 "Names in rank 2" is keyed on `entry.restricted_type_display === 'C2'`, as the oracle's `satake_record`: it checks `satake`'s `restricted_board` is `B2` (else `EngineError('restricted board of a C2 record is not B2')`, the oracle's assert), sets `restricted_board` to `C2` and `restricted_orbits_in_bourbaki_order` to a reversed copy (inner lists copied too). `restricted_type` stays `B2`, and every other field keeps `satake`'s orbit order. The arrays of `satake`'s result are placed in the record as they are (each call of `satake` builds fresh ones). What the specification left open: nothing beyond the plan's field order. Reason: SPEC 5.2 ("records with the golden field names"), 6.4.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A2: canonicalPair and matchCatalogue
Decision: the class representative is the least `(sorted g(X), g tau g^-1)` over every symmetry `g` of `symmetries(board)` (default limit; at most 6 on a finite board, D4's rotations included), with `t[g[i]] = g[tau[i]]`, comparing the black lists first and then tau, lexicographically on integers (Python's tuple order). No admissibility check. `matchCatalogue` computes `symmetries(board)` once per call and passes it to the private helper for the diagram and for every entry, and calls `satakeRecord(name, entry)` only for the matching entries (at most two), in catalogue order; it never throws NotAdmissible, since a pair that is not admissible matches no entry. The examples of the instruction (D4 black 3, 4 or 1, 3 or 1, 4 with the identity giving `{ black: [0, 2], tau: id }`; so(1,7) giving `{ black: [0, 1, 2], tau: [2, 1, 0, 3] }`; su(1,3) its own pair) and six more were checked against the oracle's `canonical_pair` by a script in the scratch directory. What the specification left open: nothing (5.5 verbatim). Reason: E-5.
