## 2026-10-25 P6-A2: names.json sections, TeX spellings and the alt field
Decision: `scripts/names.mjs` keeps P0-A3's `names` object (exactly the 32 type keys in golden order), the four KaTeX options, the resolution of KaTeX from `site/`, `texOfName`, `writeNames` and `catalogueNames`, and adds beside `names` three sections, each mapping a data spelling to `{ text, tex, html }`, read from the golden key `satake` (read only) in first-appearance order:
- `realForms` (167): TeX by the plan's spellings, `sl(N,R)` to `\mathfrak{sl}(N,\mathbb{R})`, `su*(N)` to `\mathfrak{su}^*(N)`, `su(p,q)`, `so(p,q)`, `sp(p,q)` and `su(N)`, `so(N)`, `sp(N)` with `\mathfrak{su}`, `\mathfrak{so}`, `\mathfrak{sp}`, `so*(N)` to `\mathfrak{so}^*(N)`, `sp(N,R)` to `\mathfrak{sp}(N,\mathbb{R})`, `e6(-14)` to `\mathfrak{e}_{6(-14)}` and likewise `e7`, `e8`, `f4`, `g2`; any other spelling throws, naming it (exported `texOfRealForm`). Each `su*(2m)` entry carries `alt: { text: 'sl(m,H)', tex: '\mathfrak{sl}(m,\mathbb{H})', html }` (SPEC 6.5, exported `altOfRealForm`): su*(4) with sl(2,H), su*(6) with sl(3,H), su*(8) with sl(4,H).
- `cartanLabels` (24): TeX `\text{<label>}`, `\text{compact}` for the compact form (exported `texOfCartanLabel`, which accepts `A` to `F` followed by a Roman numeral I to IX, `G` and `compact`).
- `restrictedTypes` (36): every non-null value of `restricted_type_display`, `restricted_type` and `restricted_board`, scanned in that order within each record (the order of the fields in the file); typeset by `texOfName`, whose grammar now also accepts `BC` followed by a rank (`BC2` gives `BC_{2}`).
`writeNames` returns `{ count, version, realForms, cartanLabels, restrictedTypes }` (`count` still the number of type names) and the script prints `names: 32 types, 167 real forms, 24 Cartan labels, 36 restricted types typeset with katex 0.16.47`. Affine and twisted names (`C2~`, `D4^(3)`) are not added: `texOfName('A4~')` still throws (P0-A3's note against its own test; named in `openQuestions`). The `sp(2p,2q)` note of 6.5 is the Atlas's text, not a name. What the specification left open: the section names, the TeX source spellings and the field name `alt` (plan). Default used: the plan's spellings (braces round every argument, `\mathbb{R}`, `\mathfrak{e}`), which render as the 6.5 display names. Reason: SPEC 7.3 and 6.5; the test pins the spellings only so that the output is stable.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A6: D4, the licences, and where the footer and the credits page read them
Decision: content licence `CC-BY-SA-4.0` (the D4 default, still open), code licence `AGPL-3.0-only` (the owner's, recorded by P0-A1; not the MIT default). Neither identifier is typed. The content licence is the identifier on the line `SPDX-License-Identifier: <id>` of `LICENSE-content` (a whole line, so that the second mention, of the code licence for code samples, is not taken); the code licence is the `license` field of the root `package.json`, which carries it (all three `package.json` files say `AGPL-3.0-only`; the reader falls back to the site's and then the engine's only if the root's field is missing). A file without an identifier, or a field that is not an SPDX expression, fails the build with a message naming the file. Short and long names (CC BY-SA 4.0, the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International licence, GNU AGPL version 3, and those of CC BY 4.0, MIT, Apache-2.0 and AGPL-3.0-or-later) are looked up from the identifier; any other identifier is shown alone. If GATE replaces `LICENSE-content` or the `license` fields on the owner's instruction, the footer and the credits page follow without an edit. The few lines that read the two files are in both `Footer.astro` and `credits.mdx`: a shared module would be a new file outside this agent's four files (request to MERGE below). The credits page links `LICENSE` and `LICENSE-content` in the repository at `PUBLIC_REPO_URL`, else `https://github.com/johnjanik/mutation_game` (the pattern of `open-problem.mdx`), with `/blob/HEAD/`.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A1: a restricted root system in several pieces (repair after review)
Decision: MERGE ruling (1) applied. `satake` throws `NeedsConnectedBoard` (an `EngineError`, E-10) with the message `satake needs a restricted root system in one piece; the restricted board of this pair is in K pieces` when the restricted Cartan matrix of an admissible pair has more than one component. The check runs after the admissibility check and the oracle's asserts, just before `classifyRestricted`, which is where the oracle's `classify_restricted` raises; the restricted board is computed there (once per call, as before). `restrictedBoard` is unchanged: on such a pair it returns the restricted board with labels 1..m in orbit order and no name (`identify` is called only on a board in one piece). Checked against the review's oracle dump (scratch, not committed): of the 267 admissible pairs on the 32 named boards, 7 renumbered boards and 6 direct sums, the oracle's `satake` raises on 26, the oracle's restricted Cartan matrix is in pieces on the same 26, and the engine throws `NeedsConnectedBoard` on exactly those 26 and on no other pair; on all 26 `restrictedBoard` gives labels 1..m and no name; the review's `compare.mjs` reruns with 117733 checks and 0 failures. On a board in one piece the restricted root system is in one piece, so the 167 records and the 7 admissible pairs that are not records are unchanged. Pinned in one test, `p6a-guards.test.ts > a board in pieces > the split form of A2 + A2: satake throws NeedsConnectedBoard; restrictedBoard gives labels 1..4 and no name` (the class, the message, and the orbits, Cartan matrix, labels `[1, 2, 3, 4]`, no name and two components of the restricted board), beside complex sl(3,C) on the same board, which is still computed (`A2`, multiplicity 2, the check of `reference/verify.py`). This replaces the entry "disconnected boards (not pinned in a test)" above: `satake` no longer lets `classifyRestricted`'s `EngineError` through on such a pair. What the specification left open: the behaviour on a board in pieces; MERGE ruled. Reason: E-10 gives `NeedsConnectedBoard` to `identify` on a board in several pieces, the step the oracle cannot take here.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A2: canonicalPair refuses a board with more symmetries than the cap (repair after review)
Decision: a private helper `allSymmetries(board, fn)` in `satakeCatalogue.ts` asks `symmetries(board, CAPS.relabellingsDefault + 1)`; when more than `CAPS.relabellingsDefault` (10000) come back it throws `RangeError('<fn>: the board has more than CAPS.relabellingsDefault = 10000 symmetries, so the class of a pair is not computed')`. `canonicalPair` calls it after the shape check and the guard (order of checks unchanged: shape, kind, class, then this domain check); `matchCatalogue` calls it too, where it is never reached (a named finite board has at most 6 symmetries, and the name check comes first). Before the repair the minimum was taken over the first 10000 symmetries only, without warning, so two pairs of one class could get different representatives (the review's case: 8 isolated nodes, black `[6, 7]` gave `[0, 2]` and black `[0, 1]` gave `[0, 1]`). The sentence 'canonicalPair ... works on every finite board' of the entry 'matchCatalogue on a board without a name, or with a name that is not its own' and the words 'at most 6 on a finite board' of the entry 'canonicalPair and matchCatalogue' are corrected in place. Test: `p6b-guards.test.ts > a board with more symmetries than the cap (repair after review)`: on 8 isolated nodes `canonicalPair` throws `RangeError` whose message names `CAPS.relabellingsDefault` and 10000, for black `[6, 7]`, `[0, 1]` and a tau exchanging two nodes (red before the fix: 'expected null to be an instance of RangeError'); on 7 isolated nodes (5040 symmetries) it gives the oracle's `canonical_pair` on four pairs. What the specification left open: the domain of canonicalPair (SPEC 5.5 says 'every symmetry'). Default used: MERGE's ruling (1), a refusal rather than a truncated field (E-10 reports truncation of an enumeration, which this is not). Reason: the review's finding 1; CLAUDE.md 'Every enumeration has a cap'.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A2: ranks 9 to 16 tested against the closed forms of SPEC 6.4 (repair after review)
Decision: a new file `packages/engine/test/golden/p6b-beyond-rank-8.test.ts` (no golden key, so no `covers()`). One test per board A9 to A16, B9 to B16, C9 to C16, D9 to D16 (32 tests) checks every entry of `satakeCatalogue` and every `satakeRecord` against the parametric table of SPEC 6.4 written in the test in labels (Cartan's label, the real form, black nodes, tau as identity, flip or swap, the restricted roots, the pair (m_lambda, m_2lambda) at each simple restricted root by its orbit, dim k), the multiplicities by length class of the oracle's `satake_catalogue` (`em`), dim g, and the identities `reference/verify.py` checks: the multiplicities sum to |Phi| - |Phi_X|, character = 2r - n - |Phi_X| = dim p - dim k, real rank = number of tau-orbits of white nodes = the rank of the restricted type, dim k + dim p = dim g; `restricted_type` is the display (C2 written B2), `restricted_board` is B_r for BC_r (A1 for r = 1); arrows and `tau_moves_black_nodes` by their definitions; the compact form's empty lists and nulls; and `matchCatalogue` on the entry's own pair returns exactly that record. Three more tests check `canonicalPair` on A11, A13 and D12: worked cases where the integer order and the order of the decimal text differ (A11 black 0, 2, 10; A13 black 10 gives black 2; a 3-cycle through position 10 on A11, conjugated by the flip; values confirmed with the oracle's `canonical_pair`), and on every catalogue entry plus 48 pseudo-random black sets meeting positions 9 and above (a linear congruential generator with a fixed seed, no clock) times 14 taus (the symmetries, transpositions and a 3-cycle through positions 9 and 10, eight random permutations), the result equals the least image over the symmetries written out in the test (the identity and the flip of A_n, the identity and the swap of D_n; checked equal to `symmetries(board)`), and every image, given with its black list in descending order, has the same result. Each test carries `{ timeout: 60000 }` (the engine suite's convention); measured alone the file runs in about 13 s of test time, the largest board (D16) in 1.3 s. The review's eight surviving mutants (its `mutate.mjs`, indices 0 to 7) are each killed by the p6b tests now (4 to 31 failures each, 175 tests); before the repair all eight passed 137 of 137. The ninth, ties kept to the last symmetry (`<=`), still passes, as the review classed it equivalent. What the specification left open: nothing; the ruling chose the checks. Reason: the review's finding 2; MERGE's ruling (2); instruction 5.2 and trap 9.

## 2026-10-25 P6-size: three causes put every engine module into one chunk that every route fetched
Decision: all three are removed. (1) `site/src/lib/worker.ts` spread the engine namespace into its main-thread table (`export const engineApi = { ...engine, positionsOf, firstForbiddenMove }`), which made every export of the engine live. (2) `site/src/components/lesson/Challenge.svelte` imported the whole engine dynamically (`await import('@engine')`) for the two functions of its input check; a dynamic import of the engine's index.ts made Rolldown put every engine module into that dynamic entry's chunk (`_astro/src.<hash>.js`), which every static importer then shared. (3) The bundler assumed the engine's modules have side effects, so an import of one name through index.ts reached every module the index re-exports, and all engine modules had the same importers. What the specification left open: 7.6 [D] says what a route carries ("the tool's own code with the engine functions only it uses"), not how. Reason: each cause alone kept the whole engine in the shared chunk, which is why RT-FIX-P3-perf-b measured no change on `/` when it removed (1) and (3) but not (2). Measured on this build (Vite 8.3.4): with (2) left in place, removing (1) and (3) leaves `_astro/src.<hash>.js` at 72 kB raw with every module; with all three removed the engine splits into chunks by the routes that use its modules (`board`, holding the core every tool uses, then `weyl`, `geometry`, `fold`, `wythoff`, `heaps`, `rep`), `rep.ts` lands only in T12's closure, and satake.ts and satakeCatalogue.ts only in `engineAll` (no route uses them before T13).

## 2026-10-25 P6-size: engineCall's main-thread table is filled by its callers through provide()
Decision: worker.ts imports no engine function at run time; `EngineApi` is computed from `import type * as Engine from '@two-games/engine'` plus positionsOf and firstForbiddenMove, so `engineCall<F extends keyof EngineApi>(fn, args, hint)` keeps its signature and its E-9 routing exactly. A new export `provide(fns: Partial<EngineApi>): void` adds functions to the main-thread table, which starts with positionsOf and firstForbiddenMove. Every caller provides, in its own script, the engine functions it calls by name, imported by name: T1 `play` (imported as `enginePlay`, since T1 has a `play` state) and `raisingPlay`; T4 `orbitGraph`; t09/playOn.ts `raisingPlay`; T10 `orbitGraph` and `wythoffEdges`; T12 `chevalleySerre`; T15 `applyWord`; T11 calls only positionsOf. playFate is not provided anywhere: E-9 runs it in the worker by name (ALWAYS_IN_WORKER), so the main-thread table never runs it in a browser (in Node it runs from the whole engine, unreported), and a provide would only tie a route to its module. A name not provided still runs: in Node, or when E-9 says 'main', engineCall loads the whole engine on demand (`import('./engineAll')`, a module that is `export * from '@two-games/engine'`, emitted as `_astro/engineAll.<hash>.js`) and calls it there; the error for a name the engine lacks stays a TypeError. When E-9 keeps such a call on the main thread it is recorded (`__testing.fallbacks()`) and, in a development build, warned in the console (the warning is removed from the production build). A call that E-9 sends to the worker and that runs in-process in Node (tests, build time) is not reported, since it stands in for the worker. What the specification left open: CONTRACTS 4 fixes engineCall's signature and nothing about how its main-thread table is filled; the orchestrator's brief offered an exported provide or an optional extra argument. Default used: the exported provide, because an added optional argument changes a signature of CONTRACTS 4 (RT-FIX 5.5). Reason: the table holds only what the route's code already imports, and a forgotten provide is caught by site/tests/unit/worker-provide.test.ts (a scan of every engineCall by name) and, for a default state, by site/tests/e2e/engine-fallback.spec.ts, instead of failing the reader.

## 2026-10-25 P6-size: the engine's modules are free of side effects for the bundler
Decision: site/astro.config.mjs exports `moduleSideEffects(id)`, false for a file of `packages/engine/src/` and true for every other module (the default), and passes it as `vite.build.rolldownOptions.treeshake.moduleSideEffects`. What the specification left open: nothing on bundler options. Reason: the engine's modules only declare at the top level (pure functions, E-5) and none registers anything in another when it loads, so the bundler may link an import through index.ts to the module that defines the name. The standard place for this statement is `"sideEffects": false` in packages/engine/package.json, which would also serve any other bundle of the engine; that file is the engine's and outside this brief, so the rule sits in the site's build configuration. Option for the owner or MERGE: move it to packages/engine/package.json and drop the function (site/tests/unit/worker-provide.test.ts > "the build treats the engine modules as free of side effects" then checks the field instead).

## 2026-10-25 P6-size: Challenge.svelte imports boardFromName and mutate by name
Decision: the input check of a challenge takes `{ boardFromName, mutate }` from a static import of '@engine' instead of `await import('@engine')`. What the specification left open: nothing; P1-A4's comment said the dynamic import kept the engine away from other challenges. Reason: the dynamic import of the engine's index was cause (2) above. The two functions sit in the engine chunk that the tool the challenge reads has already loaded (every tool imports them through lib/state.ts), so a challenge fetches nothing more; a lazy import of a small module re-exporting the two names was measured too and cost every tool route about 0.6 kB, because Vite's preload helper then became a chunk of its own. site/tests/unit/worker-provide.test.ts fails if a module of site/src imports the whole engine at run time again (namespace import, dynamic import or `export *`), except engine.worker.ts and engineAll.ts.

## 2026-10-25 P6-size: the fallback costs 0.2 to 3 kB on some routes, kept
Decision: the fallback to the whole engine stays in production. What the specification left open: nothing; the orchestrator's design keeps it ("correct, only slower"). Reason and cost: the fallback chunk's `export *` keeps every export of every engine module alive, and a bundler places a module whole in one chunk, so a route that uses part of a module carries all of it. Measured with npm run size on two builds that differ only in the fallback: / 40.7 against 41.4 kB, /tools/board/ 69.3 against 69.5, /tools/rep/ 84.0 against 84.8, /tools/mirror/ 66.3 against 69.3, /dev/draw-time/ 36.3 against 39.2, /tools/fold/ 66.9 against 68.1, /tools/geometry/ 78.6 against 79.6. Option: a production build without the fallback (a missing provide would then reject); not taken, since every route is within its limit and a missing provide would break a tool for the reader.

## 2026-10-25 P6-size: what T13, T14 and later tools do to call the engine by name
Decision: none; a rule for later agents. Import every engine function by name from '@two-games/engine' (or '@engine'); never `import * as`, `import('@engine')` or `export *` of the engine in site/src (worker-provide.test.ts fails). A module that calls `engineCall('<name>', ...)` calls `provide({ <name> })` in its own script with the function imported by name, unless the name is playFate, positionsOf or firstForbiddenMove; a call by a computed name provides every name it can take. This holds for calls the hint sends to the worker too, so that Node runs them in-process from the provided function (only playFate is exempt). A satake call with kind 'satake' runs on the main thread except on E7 and E8 or with `expectedItems`, so T13 provides satake, satakeRecord and whatever else it calls by name. engine-weight.spec.ts lets only a route that shows T13 (`data-tool="satake"`) or T14 (`data-tool="atlas"`) carry satake.ts and satakeCatalogue.ts; engine-fallback.spec.ts fails if a default state loads `_astro/engineAll.<hash>.js`. A new engine module keeps its top level free of side effects (astro.config.mjs moduleSideEffects).

## 2026-10-25 P6-A1: restrictedCoordinates, the shadow in the simple restricted roots (follow-up for T13)
Decision: `satake.ts` gains `export function restrictedCoordinates(d: SatakeDiagram, rb: RestrictedBoard, shadow2: Vec<number>): number[]`, exported by name from `index.ts` (a line of its own under the phase 6 block) and pinned in `PHASE_6_NAMES` of `test/unit/p1-api.test.ts` (the edit MERGE pre-approved). It returns the integers c, one per orbit in the order of `rb.orbits` (the order of `rb.simpleRestrictedRoots2`, `rb.cartan` and `rb.board`'s positions, never the Bourbaki order of `rb.board.labels`), with the sum of `c[k] * rb.simpleRestrictedRoots2[k]` equal to `shadow2` exactly; both sides are doubled, so c are the coordinates of the shadow itself in the simple restricted roots, and a composite move at orbit k changes them as `mutate(rb.board, c, k)`. Method, exact throughout: the normal equations `G c = S v` (G the integer dot-product Gram matrix of the doubled simple restricted roots, in bigint, invertible because they are independent) solved by `linalg.ts`'s `solve` over `Rational`, then the combination recomputed entry by entry with `ratEq` against `shadow2`, then the denominators checked; no float anywhere. Order of checks (the engine-wide order "argument shape, then kind"): the diagram's shape as for the other Satake functions (`checkDiagram`, RangeError), `shadow2` of the board's length with integer entries (RangeError, the message names the lengths), `rb` belongs to the diagram (RangeError: its orbits are exactly the tau-orbits of the diagram's white positions in `restrictedBoard`'s order, and each simple restricted root has n integer entries), then `requireGcm` and `requireFinite` (NeedsTwoWayRoads, NotFiniteType); then the arithmetic: RangeError "is not a combination of the simple restricted roots" outside their span, "is not zero, but this diagram has no simple restricted root (a compact form ...)" for a nonzero vector on a compact form (which gives `[]` for the zero vector), "is not an integer combination ...: its coordinates would be (1/2, 0)" with the fractions; EngineOverflow for a coordinate beyond the safe integers (unreachable on a finite board). Admissibility is not judged again: `rb` comes from `restrictedBoard`, which throws NotAdmissible, and the function stays cheap enough to call once per root on the main thread (it computes no root and no word of w_X). Pure: the arguments are read through copies, the result is a new array. The module keeps its top level free of side effects (a function declaration and one more named import from `linalg.ts`, already an engine module; P6-size). What the specification left open: SPEC does not name the function (P6-A3 instruction 5.8, plan name `restrictedCoordinates(d, rb, shadow2)`); the orchestrator asked for a check that rb belongs to the diagram's board size, and the orbit comparison is the plan's reading of "belongs", as cheap as the size check and it catches a restricted board kept from an earlier decoration. Default used: none of SPEC section 10. Reason: SPEC 7.3 "Components contain no mathematics beyond calling the engine": T13 draws the shadow picture, `data-out="shadow-coordinates"` and the values on the restricted board's nodes from this function instead of a solver of its own.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A1: the tests of restrictedCoordinates (follow-up for T13)
Decision: `packages/engine/test/unit/satake-coordinates.test.ts`, 16 tests, no `covers()` (no new golden key; it reads `golden.satake` and `golden.types[T].n_roots` through the harness, `boardOf`, `toPositions`, `labels`, `intEq`, `matchRecord`, as `p6a-restricted.test.ts` does). (1) Every root of the 167 records (10928 roots, counted against the golden `n_roots`): the coordinates are integers, those of a positive root all >= 0 and of a negative root all <= 0 (the stronger form of "all of one sign"), they recombine to `shadow2(d, root)` exactly, and they are all zero exactly when the root's support lies in the black set. (2) The 135 records of positive real rank, every root and every orbit k (34190 pairs): playing `rb.compositeWords[k]` on the root with `applyWord(..., 'mutation')` and taking the coordinates of the new shadow gives `mutate(rb.board, coords, k)`; `rb.cartan` and `cartanNumbers(rb.board)` equal the golden `restricted_cartan` by `intEq`, the orbits the golden `restricted_simple_orbits` by `labels`. (3) e6(-26): orbits `[[1], [6]]`, alpha_6 gives `[0, 1]`, restricted node 2 of the A2 is that orbit, and after the composite word of the orbit of node 6 the coordinates are `[0, -1]`; su(1,2) (BC1): coordinates +-1 four times and +-2 twice; e6(-14): orbit order `[[1, 6], [2]]`, alpha_1 and alpha_6 give `[1, 0]`, alpha_2 `[0, 1]`. (4) RangeError for a wrong length, an entry that is not an integer, half a simple restricted root on sl(3,R) (`[1, 0]`, message with `1/2, 0`), twice alpha_2 on e6(-26) (outside the span), a nonzero vector on three compact forms (su(3), e6(-78), so(5); `[]` for the zero vector and for every root), a restricted board of another diagram (fewer orbits, another board, the same number of other orbits) or with simple restricted roots of the wrong length, a malformed diagram; NeedsTwoWayRoads on a one-way board, NotFiniteType on A2~, G2~ and an indefinite board; frozen arguments unchanged, no shared array, two calls equal, black in another order. Red before: on the first run with the function absent, 15 of the 16 failed (TypeError: restrictedCoordinates is not a function); the 16th, the export check, passed on `undefined === undefined` and now also asserts `typeof` is `'function'`; rerun with `satake.ts` and `index.ts` put back to 89e37ec (scratch script, both files restored byte for byte), 16 of 16 fail. Green after: 16 passed, the file alone in 4.9 s (tests 3.2 s), E7 and E8 records included. Mutants (scratch script, satake.ts restored byte for byte, sha256 checked), each killing at least one test: coordinates in Bourbaki order (killed by tests 1, 2 and e6(-14)); the sign of the last coordinate flipped (tests 1, 2, both E6 examples, purity); every sign flipped (test 1, the examples, the split-form refusal, purity; not test 2, which is linear on both sides and so cannot see a global sign); no span check; no integrality check; no orbit check (killed only after the third case of the other-diagram test was added); no guard. Checks run: `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/engine` exit 0; `npm test -w packages/engine` 88 files, 2728 tests passed. The whole `npm test` ran twice under a shared machine's load (load average 13 to 16 on 4 processors): the first run failed 1 of 3733 tests and the second 3, each a 5000 ms timeout in a site unit test that does not reach `satake.ts` (T11's random symmetric plays; history.test.ts on load; the two tests that import `playwright.config.ts`), each file a different one between the two runs; T11 and history.test.ts pass when rerun alone, the two Playwright-config tests time out alone too at that load (they import `@playwright/test`) and passed in the first full run. No engine test failed in either run. `reference/` unchanged: the three sha256 of CONTRACTS.md 9 recomputed and equal, so `npm run verify` was not run. What the specification left open: nothing. Reason: COMMON 4.3 (a test must fail when the behaviour it guards is removed).

## 2026-10-25 MERGE: P6-A1 follow-up, restrictedCoordinates
Decision: merged (c029e25). satake.ts exports restrictedCoordinates(d, rb, shadow2): the integer coordinates of a doubled shadow in the simple restricted roots, in the order of rb.orbits, by exact normal equations over Rational, with RangeError for a wrong length, a vector outside the span, a non-integer combination, a nonzero vector on a compact form and an rb of another diagram. ## 2026-10-25 P6-tikz: T2 exports the garden as drawn, a tikz-graph
Decision: T02OrbitGarden.svelte passes ToolFrame's `latexForExport` a function, read at the click, that returns `gardenLatex(...)` of the new pure module `t02/latex.ts` for the garden as drawn now: `{ kind: 'tikz-graph', data: { nodes, edges, directed: false } }`. Nodes: every vertex drawn, in the order of the drawing (the order of `items`, of the follow model or of the positive view, whichever is shown), at the centre the layered layout of `t02/drawing.ts` gives it (`cx`, `cy`, SVG units, that is CSS pixels, y down), converted to centimetres at 96 CSS pixels to the inch with y negated (y up, so layer 0 is the top row of the picture as on screen), and scaled down uniformly when the drawing is wider than 16 cm (`MAX_WIDTH_CM`; plan: about the text width of an A4 page; only the width is bounded, as the request says, so a deep garden such as the triangle at 40 layers is tall). Label: when the drawing labels its vertices (at most 300 positions and the labels toggle on, SPEC 4 T2 Size), the population or numbers of the vertex in label order, every digit (4.0 Long numbers: no shortening in an export), entries joined by commas with no space and written with the ASCII hyphen-minus (never U+2212, which the screen shows and pdflatex cannot set in math mode); export.ts writes it in math mode. A vertex drawn as a dot (above 300 positions, or labels off) gets no label (`{}`), as on screen. Edges: the edges drawn now, in the drawn order, as vertex index pairs; above 300 positions these are the edges along the current play (pressing Export LaTeX moves the focus to the button, so the edges of a focused vertex are no longer drawn at the click). What the specification left open: everything beyond "plain TikZ coordinates" (6.7). Reason: the request ("the graph as currently drawn ... in the layered layout of t02/drawing.ts"); P6-A5's tikz-graph form.

## 2026-10-25 P6-tikz: undirected, and what the TikZ form leaves out
Decision: `directed: false` always (plan reading of "directed or not as the drawing shows moves"): the garden draws each move once, as a line with no arrowhead, because a move is an involution (SPEC 5.4: the edge from v to w by node i is the edge from w to v by i); the positive view also draws its raising edges as plain lines, the layers showing the direction. Not written, because P6-A5's tikz-graph form has no field for them: the colour of an edge by node (6.3), the node label every edge carries (A-5; harmless in the export, whose edges are all black, so colour is never a cue there), the double and triple lines and the `+k` numerals of a rise in the positive view, the chart and the board. Request (for P6-A5's area, optional): an edge label or style field in `TikzGraphData` if the owner wants them.

## 2026-10-25 P6-tikz: T10 exports the projection as drawn, tikz-points
Decision: T10GeometryStudio.svelte passes `latexForExport` a function that returns `projectionLatex(lastPicture, CAPS.edgesAtRest)` of the new pure module `t10/latex.ts`: the picture the canvas drew last (t10/drawing.ts `buildPicture`, P4-A2's scene in CSS pixels, y down, in the square box of the canvas), `{ kind: 'tikz-points', data: { points, edges } }`. Points: every point of the scene, the vertices then the short roots when shown (on screen hollow squares; written as the same dots, since the form has one marker), measured from the centre of the box, in centimetres at 96 CSS pixels to the inch, y negated, scaled down uniformly when the larger side of the box exceeds 16 cm (`MAX_ACROSS_CM`), so the picture is at most 16 cm across in both directions. Edges: the segments drawn at rest, in the scene's order (far to near, the painter's order of the canvas), none when there are more than `CAPS.edgesAtRest` (as canvasScene's `selectSegments`: the tool then draws vertices only). An export is a click, so the picture is at rest; the subset of 8000 drawn while turning is never exported. No labels: the studio draws no label on a point; the move graph's node numerals at the midpoints of its edges, the edge colours and the depth cue have no field in the tikz-points form (same optional request as above). Null before the canvas has drawn once (after hydration, while the configured orbit's data file loads, a fraction of a second; the snapshot SVG is shown meanwhile): ToolFrame then shows and announces `nothing to export as LaTeX`. What the specification left open: everything beyond "plain TikZ coordinates". Reason: the request ("the points and the drawn edges of the current view, centimetres, y up, at most 16 cm across").

## 2026-10-25 P6-A3: the Reason sentences and the failure note
Decision: one sentence per red light, written from the engine's Reason record with labels (positions converted with toLabels), subscripts and superscripts as markup: `not-a-symmetry` "τ is not a symmetry of the board (it breaks the roads at nodes 1 and 2)."; `not-an-involution` "τ applied twice is not the identity (nodes 1, 2 and 3)."; `moves-black-set` "τ sends black node 1 to a white node, so it does not keep the black set." (plural: "black nodes 1 and 2 to white nodes"); `differs-from-minus-wX` "On the black node 1, τ differs from −w_X." (plural "black nodes"); `not-an-integer` "At node 2 the number ⟨α_2, ρ_X^∨⟩ is −1/2, which is not an integer.", and with several nodes one clause per node in the order of the nodes, reading the value as the fractions joined by "; " (MERGE ruling (2) on P6-A1): "At node 3 the number ⟨α_3, ρ_X^∨⟩ is −3/2 and at node 5 the number ⟨α_5, ρ_X^∨⟩ is −1/2, which are not integers." Each light states its condition in one line and its verdict as `holds` or `fails`, with a disc or a cross beside it (A-5). The failure note: always "This decoration is not the Satake diagram of any real form, so the Studio shows no data for it."; when conditions 1 and 2 hold and condition 3 fails, also "Conditions 1 and 2 hold, and θ = −w_X∘τ can still be played: it permutes the roots, and playing it twice gives back the root. But no involution of the Lie algebra acts as this θ on the Cartan subalgebra and fixes the root vectors of the black nodes." The unit test checks on every such pair of rank at most 4 that theta permutes the roots and is an involution, so the sentence holds; no text of the tool says that theta is not an involution, and the [U] sentence on sl(3,R) and Vogan diagrams (E15) is never printed. The two optional facts on A2 with node 1 black (order 4, dim k 5) are not printed (they are not computed by the engine). Default used: the plan's wording (instruction 5.4, 5.5), the second sentence of the note reworded so that it says what is true for every such pair. Reason: SPEC 2.15 "What a failed condition 3 means"; M9 beat 4.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A3: the C2 drawing rule
Decision: `assembleData` builds one complete record of SPEC 6.4 per record `matchCatalogue` returns, with the numbers of `satake` on the reader's own pair and the names, Cartan's label and `restricted_type_display` of the record; the C2 adjustment is applied record by record (where the record displays C2 and satake says B2, the restricted board is named C2 and satake's orbits in Bourbaki order are reversed). The restricted board is drawn by the record whose black nodes and tau equal the reader's pair, otherwise by the first record: on D4 with black nodes 3 and 4 that is so(2,6), drawn B2; with black nodes 1 and 3 it is so*(8), drawn C2; with black nodes 1 and 4 (a pair of the class that is no record's own) so(2,6). The drawn board is `boardFromName` of that name, and its node with label k stands for the k-th orbit of the record's Bourbaki list; values, pairs, composite words and reduced lengths are found by orbit in `rb.orbits`, never by index (on e6(-14) drawn node 1 is the orbit {2}, the second in orbit order). The unit test checks, on the 135 records of positive real rank, that the drawn board's Cartan matrix read through the orbits equals the golden `restricted_cartan`. The plan's signature `assembleData(sat, rb, records, board)` takes the diagram instead of the board, since the record fields black_nodes, tau and arrows are the reader's pair. What the specification left open: which record decides the drawing when two match. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.6). Reason: SPEC 6.4 "Names in rank 2"; an open question for MERGE.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A3: the values on the restricted board's nodes and the shadow coordinates
Decision: the coordinates of the chosen population's shadow in the simple restricted roots come from the engine's `restrictedCoordinates(d, rb, shadow2(d, p))` (P6-A1's follow-up, merged at cac8b1e; one integer per orbit in the order of `rb.orbits`), read by orbit into the Bourbaki order of the drawn board. They are shown as `data-out="shadow-coordinates"` ("(0, 1)"), as the values of the restricted board's nodes (sign encoding by Node.svelte, `data-value`), and give the points of the shadow picture (mapped by `choleskyBasis` of the drawn board, floats for drawing only). ## 2026-10-25 P6-A3: where the Satake data are computed
Decision: `satake`, `restrictedBoard` and `matchCatalogue` go through `engineCall` with `{ board, kind: 'satake' }` (t13/load.ts, which provides the three by name), so that `whereToRun` sends E7 and E8 to the worker and keeps every other board on the main thread; `satakeRecord` is not called (the records come from `matchCatalogue`). On the main thread the three calls run each in a task of its own after the task that draws the decoration and the lights; in the worker they are posted together. A pair with no white node gets the empty restricted board without a call. `admissibility`, `theta`, `shadow2`, `restrictedCoordinates`, `satakeCatalogue`, `canonicalPair`, `positiveRoots`, `symmetries` and `mutate` run on the main thread. The server render computes the data at once (Node, where E-9 does not apply), and so does the first render in the browser on a main-thread board, so that hydration finds the server's markup; on E7 and E8 the browser always asks the worker (an instance configured on E7 or E8 shows "computing the data in the background" for a moment after hydration). While the data are computed, the lights are shown and the data panel says "computing the data in the background". Measured in Chromium with the processor slowed four times (scratch scripts, not committed; a shared, loaded machine): picking D8 gave long tasks of 255, 96 and 53 ms (the first is the picker's change with its rendering, the others satake and matchCatalogue; before the split one run gave 214 and 246 ms), picking E6 76 and 50 ms, painting a node of D8 none, opening the shadows of e6(-26) 75 ms; no long task after loading the default route. In Node, warm, satake takes 11.8 ms and matchCatalogue 8.3 ms on the split form of D8. Open question for MERGE: whether E-9 should also send Satake data of the larger boards (rank 7 and 8 of A to D) to the worker. Default used: E-9 as written, the plan's routing of matchCatalogue (instruction 5.12). Reason: SPEC 5.1 E-9, 7.6; open question for MERGE below.

No file under `components/atlas/` or `pages/atlas/` imports `reference/golden_data.json`, the harness, `lib/golden.ts`, `<G>`, `<Tex>` or the content barrel `@components/content` (whose `G.astro` and `Tex.astro` import the golden file); mathematics is typeset with `renderTex` of `lib/katex.ts`, and `Unverified` and `Cite` are imported from their own files. `atlas.test.ts > no golden data in the build path` scans the sources for all of these. Reason: roster trap ("the Atlas is a test of the engine, not a copy of the file").

## 2026-10-25 P6-A4: the tool links (plan)
Decision: the item-to-tool map of the instruction's 5.2, each link a query of SPEC 6.6 with bare keys written by `encodeState` from a state that names only the board and the fields of the item (`{ schema: 1, tool, board, ...fields }`, not `defaultState`, whose coords, start and moves would be written too). For B3: Cartan matrix and roads `board?z=1&g=B3`; weights `form?z=1&g=B3`; roots `garden?z=1&g=B3`; highest roots `kostant?z=1&g=B3`; exponents and h `numbers?z=1&g=B3`; |W| `weyl?z=1&g=B3` (T5 off the 14 boards of T8); det C `board?z=1&g=B3&v=l`; minuscule nodes `rep?z=1&g=B3&k=3` (no `k` where there is none); -w0 `board?z=1&g=B3&v=n&m=l&c=n&s=1,0,0`; orbit sizes `garden?z=1&g=B3&c=n&s=1,0,0`; complete games `weyl?z=1&g=B3` (T1 `v=n&m=l&c=n&s=1,...,1` off the 14 boards); Coxeter plane `geometry?z=1&g=B3&r=0.1.0&j=coxeter` (none on A1); affine board `affine?z=1&g=B3~` (the constructor name, `B2~` on B2); real forms `satake?z=1&g=B3&x=2.3&t=1.2.3` and so on. The page builds each href with `linkIfReleased({ kind: 'tool', id, query })`, so a link to a tool not registered on the build is left out (7.3): on this branch the T13 links are absent until P6-A3's branch is merged, and they appear with no edit. The link texts say where each goes and, where 6.6 keeps an option out of a link (the tab of T5, the growth mode of T2, the counter of T8), what to do there ("choose its Wave tab", "grow its orbit", "choose its counter"); none claims to open the option. `atlas.test.ts > tool links decode` decodes every link of every page with `decodeState` against the route defaults of its tool (its registry `default` preset over `defaultState`) and requires no notice.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A4: the tool root of an Atlas page is its opening figure (plan reading)
Decision: the element with `data-tool="atlas"`, `data-instance=""` and `data-moves=""` (4.0; plan: an empty list) is the opening figure of the page: the drawing of the board (an SVG with role img and a text alternative naming every road with its counts each way, A-10), the caption (`data-out="caption"`, the page's opening sentence stating what the sheet shows) and the noscript line. The items follow it; their `data-out` elements (with `data-exact`) lie outside the root. What the specification left open: which element is the root of a static sheet. Reason: `nojs.spec.ts` checks every `[data-tool]` element of every route for a default figure with a text alternative, a caption, a noscript line, and no enabled control before hydration; the convention switch is a radio group that works before and without JavaScript, so it must not sit inside the root, and the drawing gives the root its figure. No element of an Atlas page carries `data-node`, `data-board` or `data-can-act`; the only `data-value` hooks are MatrixView's own, on its matrix cells.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A4: the convention switch
Decision: both matrices are in the HTML (MatrixView rendered on the server with no client directive); a native radio group (fieldset with legend "Show the Cartan matrix as it is printed by", options "This site, Kac and SageMath" (checked) and "Bourbaki and Humphreys (transposed)") chooses which is shown through CSS `:has(input[value='bourbaki']:checked)`, which sets `display: none` on the other, so a screen reader skips it too. No script, no island. The transpose is `cartanNumbers(transposeBoard(board))`. The note beside the switch states this site's convention in words and that the numbering is the same in both. Kac's numbering of E6, E7, E8 and G2 is stated in one sentence on those four pages, inside `<Unverified item="E4" fallback="Other books may number the nodes of this board differently; compare the Cartan matrices before reading off a node.">` on all four (wrapping E6 too, as the plan allows); nothing is renumbered. Reason: SPEC 2.9; roster; Appendix E item 4.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A4: the note on Wildberger's names
Decision: the row of the table of 2.10 that applies, in the site's words, under an h3 inside the Cartan matrix item: B2 and C2 the same board with the same numbering; B_n (n at least 3) his "C_n" reversed, his vertex k is node n + 1 - k; C_n his "B_n" reversed; F4 his "F4" reversed, his vertices 3 and 4 long; G2 the same numbering, vertex 1 short; D_n his vertex k is node n - k and his 0 is node n; E6 and E7 his path 1, 2, 3, ... is nodes 1, 3, 4, ... and his 0 is node 2. A_n and E8 (no row) say only that the site uses Bourbaki's names and numbering. The provenance is in words ("checked by computation against the printed lists of positive roots", with the lists compared per row), never as a citation; [W20] and [W-MS] are cited for the texts. The sentence that for rank at least 3 the letters B and C are exchanged is on every B and C page. No list of Wildberger's roots is shown, so no misprint of 2.10 can be reproduced; `atlas.test.ts > no misprinted Wildberger list` checks that the note data holds no list and that the misprinted form of Example 8.6 is absent from the sources.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A4: names
Decision: board names on the Atlas pages and the index are the KaTeX markup of `names.json`; real-form display names (with "also shown as" for su*(2m)), Cartan's labels and restricted types are those of `satake-names.json`. The affine name (`C2~`, `B3~`) is shown as its plain data text, because names.mjs typesets no affine name (P6-A2's decision; `texOfName('A4~')` throws): a request to P6-A2 to add the 32 untwisted affine names is in the report. The picker of /tools/atlas shows the plain names ("B3"), as the other board pickers do, so that no KaTeX markup is sent as JavaScript. D19: the B2 page is titled B2 and the C2 page C2; each says that B2 and C2 are one board with the nodes exchanged, writes "B2=C2" (two typeset names) where one name could mislead, beside the affine name C2~, and links to the other page. The index links carry `aria-label` with the plain name, since an accessible name is not computed from MathML (axe link-name).

## 2026-10-25 P6-A4: the downloads (plan formats)
Decision: generated at build time and offered as `<a download="atlas-<T>.<ext>" href="data:<type>;charset=utf-8;base64,...">` (base64 keeps the UTF-8 bytes exactly and the HTML smaller than percent-encoding the JSON); no endpoint file. JSON: `exportJSON(defaultState('atlas', T), atlasDerived(sheet))`, the derived values keyed with the golden field names where one exists (`cartan`, `cartan_transposed`, `adjacency`, `symmetrizer`, `n_roots`, `n_positive_roots`, `positive_roots`, `highest_root`, ..., `n_reduced_words_w0` (null above the cap), `coxeter_plane_rings` (null on A1), `affine` {name, constructor_name, labels, marks, comarks}, `real_forms` [{cartan_label, real_form, black_nodes, tau, restricted_type_display}]). CSV: UTF-8, header `item,label,value`, one row per scalar (empty label: `coxeter_number,,6`), one row per entry of a vector indexed by nodes (label = node label, 0 first on the affine board), one row per matrix row (label = the row's node, value the entries joined by commas, quoted: `cartan,3,"0,-2,2"`), one row per entry of a list (label = 1-based index: `positive_root,5,"0,1,2"`, `exponent`, `minuscule_node` or `minuscule_node,,none`, `coxeter_plane_ring,1,"1.154701,12"`), the count above the cap as `complete_games,,not offered for a group of more than 60000 elements`, and five rows per real form (`real_form`, `real_form_cartan_label`, `real_form_black_nodes`, `real_form_tau`, `real_form_restricted_type`); a field with a comma or a quote is quoted with quotes doubled; integers in full digits; a final line break. LaTeX: `latexFile('dynkin', body, <page address>)` of P6-A5, the body being the line `exportLaTeX('dynkin', { type: T, black: [], tau: identity })` returns (for B3 `\dynkin B{ooo}`), then for each real form in catalogue order its `exportLaTeX('dynkin', { type: T, black, tau })` line followed by three spaces and `% <Cartan label>, <plain-text name>`, as in the examples of 6.7.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A4: the items as shown
Decision: one h2 per item in the order of the T14 entry (Cartan matrix, Roads, Weights, Roots, Highest roots, Exponents, Coxeter number h, Order of the Weyl group |W|, Determinant of the Cartan matrix, Minuscule nodes, Minus the longest element, Orbits of the fundamental weights, Complete games, Rings in the Coxeter plane, The affine board, Real forms), then Downloads; a list of in-page links opens the page. Matrices are MatrixView grids (caption, row and column headers labelled by node). Vectors are tuples in label order with a true minus sign. The positive roots are an ordered list, sorted by total and then lexicographically, with the sentence "All N positive roots are listed." (or, above the cap of 120, "The first 120 of the N positive roots are listed"; no type reaches it). The highest short root line is omitted on simply laced types (a sentence says every root has one length), the Coxeter plane item says "has rank 1, so it has no Coxeter plane" on A1, and the count above 60000 is replaced by "The number of complete games from all ones is not offered for a group of more than 60000 elements; this group has |W|." (stated limits, 4.0). Each statement beside a value is one of section 2 ([V] or definitions: F1, F4, F7, F8, F11, F12, F13, 2.4(c), 2.5, 2.12), never a [U] one.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A4: long numbers
Decision: a count of more than 12 digits (complete games on A7, D6, B6, C6, E6) is shown as T1 shows it, `shortValue` of `t01/longNumber.ts` ("1.2666... x 10^15 (16 digits)"), with the exact digits in `title`, in a `<details>` "The exact value" below it, in `data-exact`, and in all three downloads. Reason: SPEC 4.0 "Long numbers"; one format across the site.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A4: the picker of /tools/atlas and /embed/atlas, and two deviations from the plan
Decision: `AtlasPicker.svelte` (hydrated `client:idle` through the pre-approved line of `ToolIsland.astro`) renders the caption, the 32 boards grouped by letter (h2 "Type A" ... "Type G"), each a card with a native link to `/atlas/<T>/` and the drawing of the board beside the link (role img, "Diagram of <T>"; the card follows the link through a stretched `::after`, the focus ring is the card's), a Cite button (disabled until hydration; `citation(document.title, location.href)` of `lib/export.ts`, fetched on the click) with `data-out="citeText"`, a polite live region, and the noscript line `data-out="noscript"`. Hydration reads the URL with `decodeState` (prefix the instance id): a `g` naming one of the 32 boards puts "Open the Atlas page of <T>" (`data-out="chosen"`) first; an unreadable link shows the notice of 6.6. Two deviations from the plan's 5.10: (1) the picker draws the boards, and so calls engine functions (`boardFromName`, `adjacency` through `draw/roads.ts`, and those `decodeState` calls), where the plan says "It calls no engine function": `nojs.spec.ts` and `embed.spec.ts` require every tool route to show a default figure (an SVG or image with a text alternative) inside its `data-tool` root, and the honest figure of a board picker is the boards' drawings, made by the site's one drawing code; nothing is enumerated and nothing needs the worker. (2) The picker carries a Cite button although it is no ToolFrame: `embed.spec.ts` requires an enabled `[data-control="cite"]` on every hydrated tool route; `citeText` is therefore in the registry's outs (P6-A5's request). The registry's `component` is written `import('../../components/tools/../atlas/AtlasPicker.svelte')`, the same file as `@components/atlas/AtlasPicker.svelte`, because `registry-outs.spec.ts` finds the component of each entry with a pattern that requires `components/tools/` (request to MERGE below).

## 2026-10-25 P6-A4: plan readings of 4.0 and 7.5 for a static sheet
Decision: (1) Works without JavaScript: the whole page is HTML; the switch is CSS and the downloads are data URIs. (2) History, step, play to the end, undo, reset, Copy link, SVG and PNG export: there is no state to change and the page URL is the link; they do not apply. (3) Predict: the Atlas pages are not lesson figures and take no `prediction`; nor does the picker. (4) One state: the only state object is `defaultState('atlas', T)`, used for the JSON export; the picker's state is `{ schema: 1, tool: 'atlas', board }` read from `g`. (5) Configuration: board only; the registry has the one `default` preset that `collectRegistry` requires, with a caption and no state field (CONTRACTS 6: "T1 and T14 have no presets"). (6) Growth off the finite types: does not apply (every Atlas board is finite; the roots come from `positiveRoots`). (7) Keyboard and screen reader: the only controls are the radio group, the links and the `<details>` disclosures, all native (A-1); nothing but the switch changes the page, and the browser announces its state, so the pages need no live region. (8) Small screens: links and radios keep a target of at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels (radios are 24 px inside a 44 px label), the page reflows at 320 px and the matrices scroll inside their own boxes. (9) A-10: the sheet is tables and lists, and needs no separate table view; the drawing has a text alternative and the roads table beside it is its table form; the picker is a list of links, its own text form. (10) A-3, A-4, A-7 for nodes, A-8 and A-9 have no subject on a page with no node buttons, no moves and no motion.

## 2026-10-25 MERGE: P6-A3 reviewed; rulings
Decision: a fresh review of T13 at add4487 found no blocker. It confirmed the mathematics through the tool's own data path against the oracle and the golden file (the lights on all 3590 pairs of the 32 types with reason labels and fractions; the 174 admissible pairs on every field; the 167 records; the C2 adjustment applied exactly six times and never to a B2 record; all 142 drawings of the restricted board read by orbit; theta on 92722 runs; 35058 composite moves), the words (no 'not an involution', no E15 sentence, no E1 or E8 claim, true minus signs in every reason), the links and history writes, the hooks, E-9 on the default route, keyboard, axe, 320 px and no JavaScript, and /tools/satake/ at 85.0 kB. Two majors and nine minors go to P6-A3's repair with these rulings. Majors: (1) in the dark theme a black node (#000) and a white node (page colour) differ by a fill contrast of 1.12 to 1: black nodes are filled with the text colour so that black means filled and white means hollow in both themes, with a test of the fill contrast of a black node against a white node in both themes (at least 3 to 1). (2) An instance configured on E7 or E8 fetches the worker at hydration: the server render writes the computed data of the configured pair into the island (JSON beside it) and hydration reads it when the pair matches, so no default state needs the worker (E-9); a browser test with an E7 instance asserts no worker request before the first interaction. Minors: (3) data-moves: ToolFrame gains an optional prop `moves?: number` that overrides state.moves?.length (pre-approved for this repair, additive; P1-A2's file), T13 passes its step count, and the spec asserts data-moves equals moveCounter after a stage, a composite move and an undo; the session history stays out of the link. (4) A worker that fails ends the wait with a sentence that the data could not be computed, and the next change retries. (5) The restricted panel's caption pairs each drawn node's word length with its own reduced length, in Bourbaki order. (6) Captions, the figure's name and announcements use display spellings: U+2212 in names, subscripts or words as in the data panel, dim 𝔨, and '1 move' in the singular. (7) Above four nodes the announcements use announceTemplates.changedOnly and give the step number (A-4). (8) Tab order (A-1): undo, redo and reset come after the boards that play moves; the repair chooses the layout and records it. (9) An unknown preset id fails the build with the list of presets, as T8 does. (10) Tests: the two surviving mutants (the careful sentence when only condition 3 fails; computeNow without its admissible guard) must fail; count one tab stop per board group; the E7 island test of (2). (11) Golden values typed as duplicates of golden reads are dropped; only SPEC worked values stay typed, each marked. Also from the notes: the catalogue rows' empty-table-header (axe, minor) gets text for its row headers. Left as is: the Export LaTeX line for a decoration that is not admissible (harmless; the file states the decoration). For P6-A7: the failure note's general claim rests on Kolb's theorem ([Kol14], [S]); the lesson cites it where it says the same. Reason: the review (build-plan/reports/orchestrator/phase6/P6-A3-review.json).

## 2026-10-25 P6-size: the provide scan reads engine names with the TypeScript checker (repair after review)
Decision: site/tests/unit/worker-provide.test.ts reads the client code of site/src with the TypeScript compiler (typescript 6.0.3, already a root devDependency; nothing added): every .ts, .js and .mjs module, the <script> blocks and the markup of every .svelte file, and the <script> blocks of every .astro file. One program over the files that mention engineCall, with the options of site/tsconfig.json and Svelte's rune declarations, takes about 3 s. A reference to engineCall is found by its symbol, so `import { engineCall as run }` and a namespace member `w.engineCall` count. The names of a direct call are the string literal types of its first argument, so quotes of any kind and a call over several lines read the same, and a computed name gives every literal it can take: T01's `fn` reads as playFate, play and raisingPlay, so T01 must provide play and raisingPlay (playFate stays exempt with positionsOf and firstForbiddenMove). A name whose type is not a union of string literals, or that admits every engine name, is refused with a message; READ_BY_HAND in the test is the allow-list for such a name and is empty, since every name in site/src can be read. A re-export of engineCall, the string 'engineCall', and an engineCall in Svelte markup are refused. provide must take an object literal, whose keys are read (shorthand, identifier or quoted keys; an alias of provide counts). What the specification left open: how the scan reads names; the ruling of the review asked for any quotes, every literal of a computed name, aliases, .astro scripts and `export * as`. Reason: the type of the argument is exactly the set of names a call can take, so no pattern per call shape is needed and a later tool's computed name is read without an allow-list entry. Red before, green after: each of the review's five mutants applied to the real files fails the test (T10 with engineCall("wythoffEdges", ...) and only orbitGraph provided; T01 with only raisingPlay provided; a new module with `import { engineCall as run }` calling run('weylOrder', ...); a new .astro file whose <script> imports the engine namespace and calls engineCall, which fails both source tests; a new module with `export * as wholeEngine from '@two-games/engine'`), and so do the review's two controls (wythoffEdges dropped from T10's provide; the same call over two lines) and T13's load.ts without matchCatalogue. The same holes are fixtures of the test (files under a folder that does not exist on disk, read in the same program), each with the problem it must report, together with a clean fixture that must report none.

## 2026-10-25 P6-size: a reference to engineCall that is not a direct call counts as a call by its type (repair after review)
Decision: a reference to engineCall that is not the callee of a call counts as a call by every name the first parameter of the type it is given admits (the type of an `as` cast, else its contextual type: an annotated variable or parameter); it is refused when that type cannot be read, admits every engine name, or passes through `any`, `unknown` or `never`. What the specification left open: the ruling allowed either counting such a reference as a call or refusing it. Reason: t13/load.ts, merged during this repair, passes `engineCall as Caller` as the default of a parameter, where `Caller` takes `F extends 'satake' | 'restrictedBoard' | 'matchCatalogue'`; the scan reads those three names and finds them provided in load.ts. Refusing every such reference would have forced a change to T13's module and its unit test stub, which take engineCall's shape on purpose. The scan flagged no missing provide anywhere in site/src, so no module changed. Measured: 8 files call engineCall (T01, T04, t09/playOn, T10, T11, T12, T15, t13/load), and the names read match the review's list plus T13's three.

## 2026-10-25 P6-size: .astro scripts and `export * as` in the whole-engine rule (repair after review)
Decision: the rule that no client module imports the whole engine reads the <script> blocks of .astro files too (their frontmatter and template run at build time, in Node, and are not read), and its pattern also matches `export * as X from` the engine, `import d, * as X from`, and a dynamic import whose specifier is in backticks; `import type * as` and `export type *` stay allowed, since the compiler erases them. The test also checks that the pattern matches the two allowed files (engine.worker.ts and engineAll.ts), so that a pattern that matches nothing cannot pass. What the specification left open: nothing beyond the ruling. Reason: the review's mutants 4 and 5 passed the first rule.

Decision: worker.ts keeps the table's initial entries (positionsOf and firstForbiddenMove) in a constant, and `__testing.reset()` clears the table and puts them back, so that a provide made by one test, or a replay function replaced in one, never reaches the next. ## 2026-10-25 P6-A3: the data of an E7 or E8 instance written into the island (repair after review)
Decision: when the configured board's Satake data run in the worker (E7, E8; `dataOnMainThread` false), the server render computes the configured pair's data (`computeNow`) and writes them into the island as `<script type="application/json" data-t13-pair="<instance id>|<pair key>">` (`t13/load.ts` `islandScript`, `pairJson`: the fields the tool reads, with `<`, `>`, `&`, U+2028 and U+2029 escaped), through `{@html}` at the head of the figure. In the browser the component looks for that element with the same instance id and pair (`readIsland`), parses and checks it (`pairFromJson`), and uses it as the first data, so hydration asks no worker; the element is rendered again from the same text, so hydration adopts it. The data read are kept in a module map, so that a second run of the component (Svelte's recovery from a hydration mismatch, which empties the island first) finds them too. Main-thread boards write nothing (their data are computed at once in the browser, as before); a pair that is not admissible writes nothing. If the element is missing or does not parse, the worker is asked as before. The key is `pairKey` in `t13/model.ts` (board, black labels sorted, tau), which the component also uses for its own bookkeeping. Tests: `T13.test.ts` "an instance configured on E7 or E8 carries the data of its pair in the island, and only those" (server render of three E7 and E8 pairs contains exactly `islandScript(...)` once, the JSON reads back equal; none on A3, E6, D8 or the restricted preset; none for a pair that is not admissible; escaping); `T13.spec.ts` "an instance configured on E7 shows the data written into the island at build time and fetches no worker before the first interaction" (the embed page with its island's properties changed to `{ board: 'E7' }`, as the review's probe, and the element the server render writes; no worker request after hydration and network idle, the split form's name and real rank shown; the worker after picking E8; and, as a control, the same page without the element requests the worker at once). No page configures E7 or E8 today, so the browser test builds such a page from the embed route. Reason: MERGE ruling (2); SPEC 5.1 E-9, 7.6.

## 2026-10-25 P6-A3: a worker that fails (repair after review)
Decision: `refresh()` handles a rejected request: the pair's key and the error's message are kept, and while the current pair is that pair and has no data, the data, shadows and restricted panels show, in place of "computing the data in the background", `data-out="data-error"`: "The data could not be computed (<message>). The next change of the decoration or the board asks for them again." The caption reads "<where>, all three conditions hold, but the data could not be computed." Any change of decoration or board starts a new request (the failure is cleared and the new key asked for). No unhandled rejection remains. Test: `T13.spec.ts` "a worker that fails ends the wait ..." (the worker script answered 404, E8 picked: the sentence in three panels and the caption, no pending line, no data, no page error; then E7 picked with the worker allowed again: no failure sentence, a new wait or data). Request to P1-A2 (site/src/lib/worker.ts): after the worker's `error` event, `failAll` rejects the pending calls but the failed Worker object is kept, so a later call is posted to a worker that never answers; dropping it (`worker.terminate()`, `worker = null` in `onerror`) would let the next call start a new worker, so that T13's retry reaches the engine. Until then a retry after a worker that could not load waits ("computing the data in the background"). Reason: MERGE ruling (4); instruction 5.5, 5.12; SPEC 4.0 Stated limits.

## 2026-10-25 P6-terms: the shared spec glossary-later-uses.spec.ts
Decision: `site/tests/e2e/glossary-later-uses.spec.ts` applies the rule of `M8.spec.ts > later uses of a term link to the glossary` (SPEC 8.4: "Define every term on first use and link later uses to a glossary entry") to the lessons M0 to M9 and to history, confusions, open-problem, not-quiver-mutation and about: for every glossary term (each `dfn[id]` of the glossary, formula left out) used at least twice in the prose of a page, some use after the first is a link to the term's own anchor, and every glossary link of a term resolves. The prose scope is M8's: the article without tools, tables, the list of sources, the module links, challenges, h1 to h3, scripts and formulas. A use is the term as a whole word, any case, singular as the glossary writes it. Three refinements that M8's test does not need, each so that the rule asks only for links that can exist and mean what they say: (1) a hyphen joins a word on either side (M8's test stops a term only at a following hyphen, so there "anti-Martians" holds a use of "Martians" and "non-compact" one of "compact"); (2) a use inside the use of a longer term belongs to the longer term ("restricted board" is not a use of "board"); (3) the text of a link that is not a glossary link (a module title in the Developed line of M0, a statement of the about page linked to its module, a source) is not a use, because links do not nest. A link to the glossary page without a fragment is navigation, not a term link. Reason: SPEC 8.4 and MERGE's instruction (step 3).

## 2026-10-26 RT-FIX-P6-latex: T8 and T12 export their orbit graphs as a tikz-graph (P6-RT-10-01)
Decision: the Weyl Explorer (T8) and the Representation Builder (T12) pass ToolFrame's `latexForExport` a function, read at the click, that writes the orbit graph as drawn, in the `tikz-graph` form of decisions/P6-A5.md and the way P6-tikz writes T2's garden (decisions/P6-tikz.md): coordinates in centimetres at 96 CSS pixels to the inch, y negated (y up, layer 0 on top), the whole picture scaled down to 16 cm when wider; `directed: false`, since both drawings show each move as a line with no arrowhead and the layers show the direction. T8 (new pure module `site/src/components/tools/t08/latex.ts`, `weylLatex`): every dot of the scene of `t08/layout.ts` `buildScene`, in its order (`model.drawn`, the order of the `data-out="vertex"` hooks), at its centre, with no label because the dots carry none; then the edges of the scene in its order, that is every legal move up to 192 elements and above that the moves along the game and at the focused vertex, exactly as the SVG or the canvas draws them. T12 (new pure module `site/src/components/tools/t12/latex.ts`, `orbitLatex`): every vertex of the orbit, in the drawn order (`OrbitLayers.vertices`, the order of the `data-vertex` hooks), at the centre of its box, labelled with its position in label order, every digit, ASCII hyphen-minus and commas (the form of T2's labels; the drawing's text "(1, −1) #2" is written without the parentheses and without the basis index after `#`, which names a row of the matrices and is not part of the position); then every edge in the drawn order. The geometry of T12's boxes was moved, unchanged, out of `orbitSvgLayers` into a new exported `orbitGeometry` of `t12/OrbitLayers.svelte`, which both the drawing and the export read, so that the export cannot drift from the drawing. ## 2026-10-26 RT-FIX-P6-latex: the writers of T8 and T12 are fetched on the click (P6-RT-10-01)
Decision: ToolFrame's prop `latexForExport` (decisions/P6-A5.md: `LatexChoice | (() => LatexChoice | null)`) also accepts a function that answers with a promise of the same (`() => LatexChoice | null | Promise<LatexChoice | null>`), an additive widening: the click calls the function at once, awaits its answer together with the `import()` of export.ts, and hands the answer to `latexDownload` unchanged, so a value, a function answering a value and a function answering null behave as before. T8 and T12 answer `import('./t08/latex')` and `import('./t12/latex')`, so their writers, like export.ts, are fetched only on the first click and no route fetches more before an interaction. T2's and T10's writers stay as P6-tikz made them (imported with the tool, about 200 bytes each); moving them is not needed by this round's findings. Deviation: a recorded plan prop of P6-A5 is widened (not a CONTRACTS.md interface: CONTRACTS 5.1 lists no `latexForExport`); ToolFrame.svelte is touched only in the prop's type and in `onExportLatex`. Reason: the orchestrator's note for this cluster (the writers stay behind the dynamic import of the click; SPEC 7.6 budget). The components hand the writers their own model (T8: the scene and the model's edges; T12: the orbit, the geometry and the label order), so that the loops run in the fetched module and the code each route fetches first is only the closure. Measured with `npm run size -- --port 7301` (gzip bytes, before at 8de73de, after on this branch; the build of each): `/tools/rep/`, `/embed/rep/` and `/modules/m8-lie-algebras/` 85706 to 85875 (+169: the closure, the prop, and `orbitGeometry` now returning its functions); `/tools/weyl/` and `/embed/weyl/` 77359 to 77443 (+84); every other route that hydrates a ToolFrame +17 or +18 (ToolFrame's await of the answer); the writers (`t08/latex.ts` 330 bytes and `t12/latex.ts` 404 bytes before compression) are fetched by no route before the click (`latex-export.spec.ts` > "the writers of T8 and T12, like export.ts, are fetched on the click of Export LaTeX and not before (7.6)"); 90 routes, 0 over budget before and after.

## 2026-10-26 RT-FIX-P6-latex: T6, T15 and T16 keep their export (P6-RT-10-01)
Decision: T6 (Kaleidoscope) keeps the default export of P6-A5, the `\dynkin` line of its board; T15 (Affine Playground) and T16 (Sandbox) keep `nothing to export as LaTeX`. T6: its figure (SPEC 4 T6) is "the plane with the two mirrors, the simple roots drawn as the mirror normals, the chambers, and one point", with the parallelogram of the population and the two perpendiculars of the numbers; it is neither an orbit graph nor the projection of a point set (the orbit of the point is an optional overlay, off by default), and the two TikZ forms of P6-A5 cannot write it: `tikz-points` draws a dot at every point and segments only between such dots, so a mirror, an arrow, a chamber, a perpendicular or the parallelogram would come out with dots the figure does not have, and the chambers not at all. Writing only T6's points would export a picture different from the one drawn. A faithful TikZ export of T6 needs a form for lines and polygons without dots, that is a new kind or option of `exportLaTeX` (CONTRACTS 4), which is the owner's to add; until then the board's diagram is what the `dynkin-diagrams` half of SPEC 4.0's LaTeX export gives. T15 and T16: each figure is a board (the affine and twisted boards and the two cycles of T15; the editor's board of T16) with its numbers or populations, not an orbit graph or a projection, so 6.7's TikZ sentence does not reach them; their boards are not among the 32 finite types, which P6-A5 recorded as the only ones the package is written for ("Affine, twisted, preset and custom boards have no form in SPEC 6.7 and are refused"), so the notice stays. What the specification left open: which of these figures 6.7's last paragraph governs. Reason: SPEC 4 (each tool's figure), 6.7, decisions/P6-A5.md; the orchestrator's instruction to decide and record. Option for the owner: (a) keep this; (b) export T6's points only (root tips, the point, the orbit when shown) as `tikz-points`; (c) add a TikZ form for lines and polygons and export T6's plane in full. Recommendation (a) until (c) is wanted.

## 2026-10-31 RT-FIX-P6-pages: D10 default used, the projects kept separate (P6-RT-10-04)
Decision: this project and the research-software specification "MutationGraph" are kept separate. The site and the engine share no fixtures with it: `reference/golden_data.json` is this site's acceptance oracle and is not published as fixtures for another project, no source of the site or of the engine names MutationGraph or reads its files, and the site states no common rule for the two projects. The note that D10 asks for, on this project's side: on a simple graph, where A_ij = A_ji is 0 or 1 (SPEC 2.1), the mutation rule p_i <- p_i - sum_j C_ij p_j with C = 2I - A^T reads p_i <- -p_i + (the sum of the populations of the neighbours of i), and C = 2I - A^T is C=2I-A because A is symmetric; so on simple graphs the rule and C=2I-A agree. The site states it in M2 beat 3 (`site/src/content/modules/m2-form.mdx`: on a board with single roads the matrix of the form is B = 2I - A, which is the Cartan matrix C = 2I - A^T of module zero because A is symmetric, and the mutation subtracts (p, e_i) from city i, "the rule of module one"). So no reference page needed a new sentence, and none of them names the other project. The note on the side of MutationGraph lies outside this repository and is the owner's. What the specification left open: D10, the relation to MutationGraph (options: share `golden_data.json` as fixtures and state the common mutation rule; or keep the projects separate); SPEC does not say where in this project the note stands. Default used (SPEC section 10, D10): keep separate; note in both that on simple graphs the rule and C=2I-A agree. Whose default: every build agent's since phase 0, none of which shared a fixture or named the other project; no entry recorded it (RT-10 attack 18). Reason: no answer recorded; the default needs no code. Test: `site/tests/unit/repo-defaults-recorded.test.ts` (the record names M2 beat 3, and the test reads the note there).

Decision: in `site/src/components/board/ToolFrame.svelte` the "Show as table" view scrolls in a `<div class="bare" tabindex="0" role="group" aria-label="Table of <title>" data-scroll="table-view">` with the focus ring of A-2; inside it a `<fieldset>` (no longer the scroll box) still disables the table's buttons until hydration (7.4). The group carries the name the fieldset's visually hidden legend carried before ("Table of <title>"), and the legend is removed so that the name is not read twice. The box is a tab stop in every state, before hydration and without JavaScript included, since a disabled fieldset cannot take the focus; it is a stop whether or not the table overflows at the reader's width, as the display formulas are (the entry "RT-FIX-P3-layout: every display formula of <Tex> is a tab stop"). The hook `data-scroll="table-view"` is added, after T5's `data-scroll="tally"` for a scroll box; no hook or prop is renamed or removed (CONTRACTS 5.1). Role group, not region (the finding's proposal): a lesson with several tools of one title would hold several landmarks of one name (axe landmark-unique), and the site's other scroll boxes are named groups (decisions "P3-A3: tabs and scroll boxes", MatrixView). The table buttons of T13 and T9 stay disabled while a prediction freezes the tool, as the entries "P1-A5: prediction check" and "RT-FIX-P3-board-a11y: a frozen board stays one tab stop" record for History and the step controls; the box makes the table reachable without changing them. What the specification left open: how a scroll box with only disabled content is made keyboard operable (A-11 with A-1, WCAG 2.1.1). Default used: none. Reason: SPEC 7.5 A-1, A-10, A-11, 7.7 (axe scrollable-region-focusable).

## 2026-10-26 RT-FIX-P6-shared-a11y: a prediction's answer is written with U+2212 and spoken "minus" (P6-RT-05-04)

The answer is ...", and so on) the second. A choice is the author's text in both. `predictionAnswerText` is unchanged and still gives the `<details>` shown without JavaScript (`.answer-text`) and T10's own `<details>`: its ASCII hyphen is pinned by `site/tests/unit/tools/T01.test.ts` and `site/tests/e2e/M9.spec.ts` ("every prediction has a details fallback"), and the finding names the result line and the announcement only, so whether the no-JavaScript answer should also take U+2212 is left to the owner (see the report's open questions). ## 2026-10-26 RT-FIX-P6-shared-a11y: the run without JavaScript reads a figure's marks and T13's panel figures (P6-RT-06-01)
Decision: in `site/tests/e2e/nojs.spec.ts` (`toolReport`), a figure holds content by its marks: an SVG drawing a circle, ellipse, line, path, polyline, polygon or text outside defs, marker, title, desc, clipPath, mask, pattern and symbol (a rect alone, which is often a background, is no mark); an HTML drawing of role img (T2's chart of bars, a fraction) an element, as before. A board is a group (data-board-group) with a data-node and a drawing beside it with marks. Every board group and every named drawing (aria-label, aria-labelledby or a title) that is shown, not only the first, must hold its content, else it is reported as a blank part. The figure of the panel a T13 instance is configured to show is read: `data-out="shadow-picture"` must hold a `data-point` drawn by a mark, `data-out="restricted-board"` a board, and a tab panel that names its restricted board (`data-out="restricted-name"`) must draw it. The kind of a root's figure is chosen as before. This adds to the entries "RT-FIX-P3-test-integrity: the default figure of the run without JavaScript", "RT-FIX-P4-tool-t10" and "RT-FIX-P5-t12-a11y". M9.spec.ts checks without JavaScript that b3's picture holds a point per restricted root with its multiplicity and that the restricted boards of b7 and b12 hold a node per simple restricted root, drawn, showing the default shadow's coordinates; T14.spec.ts that every Atlas drawing holds a disc and a label per node. What the specification left open: SPEC 7.4 asks that "every default figure" be present without JavaScript and does not say how a test recognises one. Default used: none. Reason: SPEC 7.4, 4 T13 Shadows and Restricted board, 4 T14, 7.7; RED-TEAM-COMMON 2.
