## 2026-10-26 RT-FIX-P6-t12-t5: T12 reads a link in the task after hydration, frozen meanwhile (gate G6, T12.spec.ts:1242; P6-RT-07-04 evidence)
Decision: when the address holds a key of the instance's form (a one-letter name after the instance's prefix, the shape of every key of the codec), T12's hydration `$effect` no longer calls `readLink` and `load` itself: it marks the tool frozen (`linkPending`, read by `frozen`, so every control of T12 stays disabled and no pick, move, typed start or relation can arrive) and counts one run of drawing (`data-drawn="false"`), and reads the link in a `setTimeout` task of its own, which ends the freeze, then calls `readLink` and, when the link loads nothing new, `activate`, exactly as hydration did before. A state loaded in between by the back button (popstate, which calls `readLink` and so starts a new generation) is the one shown: the deferred read is dropped when the generation has changed. An address without such a key takes the old path unchanged. The test is over-inclusive on purpose: a key the codec does not know only moves `activate` one task later. What the specification left open: CONTRACTS 5.2 says a tool reads the URL "on hydration"; SPEC 7.6 bounds engine calls on the main thread; neither fixes the task. Default used: "on hydration" read as "in the hydration step, in the task after the island's hydration", as `site/src/lib/history.ts` already allows ("A link is applied by its tool after ToolFrame has registered the instance (a task after hydration for some tools)"): on a page opened from a link the state that arrives before the reader acts is recorded and not written. Reason: MERGE's ruling ("MERGE: the T12 repair after the first run of the G5 rerun") keeps T12's long-task tests as written and asks the product to change; the link's hydration task held the hydration of the server's markup and the re-render to the link's state with the engine facts of its node (14 to 20 ms of 35 to 65). The tool's controls stay disabled one task longer on a page opened from a link; Copy link and Download data (ToolFrame's) are not frozen and, in that one task, give the server's state. Measured on this container (true task lengths from a trace, 9 runs alternated between the base build and this one, load 21 to 25): the hydration task of a link to C8 node 7 has a median of 45.3 ms on the base and 23.0 ms here, of E7 node 7 44.5 and 21.9, of the page without a link 25.4 and 24.2. T12.spec.ts:1242 with --repeat-each 20: on the base 80 of 80 passed at load 6 to 1 and 73 of 80 at load 1 to 28 (long hydration tasks 52 of 240 for the cases, 59 of 240 for the control); here 80 of 80 at load 17 to 31 (9 of 240 and 17 of 240). The tasks still seen are the hydration of the server's markup under a load of five to eight times the four processors. /tools/rep/ measures 85.8 kB (85.7 on the base).

## 2026-10-26 RT-FIX-P6-t12-t5: the tooltip of a shortened list in T5 (P6-RT-03-01)
Decision: in T5's figure every value of more than 12 digits is written through `shortValue` (the tape, the start line, the tape tab's table, the sorted tapes, the ends of games A and B); a single shortened value carries its exact digits as its `title`, and a list (the tape, the start line, an end position) that holds one carries the exact list, comma-separated with the sign as `-`, as the board's tooltip writes a value. The table view keeps every value in full (`display`, `listText`, `tuple` are unchanged there), and the exports are unchanged. The dimension calculator's lambda, its start and its two tapes are not changed: lambda has at most six digits (decisions/P3-A3.md), so they never reach 13. What the specification left open: SPEC 4.0 "Long numbers" names "the tooltip" without saying whether a list has one per value or one for the whole. Default used: one per value where values are cells, one for the whole where the list is one text. Reason: the smallest change that gives every shortened value its digits in a tooltip without changing the markup of the lists.

## 2026-10-26 RT-FIX-P6-t13-followup: the typeset names of one board, fetched during hydration of a link state (P6-MERGE-T13-01)
Decision: `scripts/names.mjs` also writes the real forms one file per board, `site/src/generated/satake-names/<board>.json` (32 files, `{ katex, realForms }`, each entry the same as in `satake-names.json`; the boards are the `dynkin_type` of the golden key `satake`, read only, in first-appearance order), through a new export `writeSatakeNamesByBoard(dir)` that the command-line run calls after `writeGenerated`. `writeGenerated` still writes its two files (P6-A2's test of the generated directory is unchanged), and the entry of a real form is now built by one helper for both writers (the bytes of `satake-names.json` are unchanged). In the browser `t13/names.ts` imports those files lazily with `import.meta.glob`, one chunk per board, and `loadNames(board)` fetches only the board shown; the server render still reads every name in-process from `satake-names.json`, and the browser no longer imports `t13/satakeNames.ts`. `readLink` (hydration and the back button) now loads the names of the board after `setConfig` when the link changes the pair, and the reader's actions (paint, tau, picker, example, catalogue entry, panel, back button) load the names of the board they show. The default state fetches no names: its server markup is typeset and hydration keeps it. This replaces two sentences: in decisions/P6-A3.md "the names of real forms, typeset at build time and loaded lazily", "in the browser only after the reader's first change of decoration or of panel"; and decisions/RT-FIX-P6-t13.md "the typeset names load on the reader's own actions only": a link state now fetches the names of its own board while the island hydrates, so that P6-A3's "the first view is always the typeset one" holds for link states too (SPEC 7.5 A-12). Sizes, gzip level 9 as npm run size measures: each board's chunk weighs 487 B (A1, B2) to 833 B (D8); the per-board loaders add 628 B to T13's chunk (20306 to 20934 B), and the whole names chunk (5230 B) is no longer in the client build. `npm run size -- --port 7391`: `/tools/satake/`, `/embed/satake/` and `/modules/m9-real-forms/` 87.3 kB on the base d8102c0 and 87.9 kB on this branch (limits 90, 90, 120); 90 routes, 0 over budget. The RT-07 link sweep (redteam/redteam-RT-07-p6-link-sweep.mjs of the lens branch, a scratch copy) over the 167 links of the built site to the Studio: the default route 87943 B; every link 88430 B (A1) to 88776 B (D8 split), its one extra script being its board's chunk (the E7 and E8 links also fetch the uncounted worker, as at base); 0 over 90000 B. What the specification left open: how the typeset names reach the browser (SPEC 7.3 typesets them at build time; 7.6 counts every script before the first interaction). Reason: SPEC 7.5 A-12, 7.6, 7.3; decisions/P6-A3.md.

## 2026-10-26 RT-FIX-P6-t13-followup: the paint buttons of the decoration are controls (P6-MERGE-T13-02)
Decision: the paint buttons of the decoration carry `data-control="paint"`, the node's label in `data-paint`, the colour in `data-colour` ("black" or "white") and `data-can-act`, and no `data-node`, `data-board` or `data-value`. Their keyboard model (one group, one tab stop, roving tabindex, the arrows, Home and End of A-1, Enter and Space), their focus, their names ("Node 2, black") and the announcements ("Node 1 painted black. ...") are unchanged. The reading of SPEC 4.0 Test hooks [D] this rests on: its node buttons are those of a game's board, since `data-board` names the board of a game ("populations or numbers, which matters in the linked view") and `data-value` is "the value shown"; the decoration copy (6.3 last bullet) shows no value and plays neither game, and a paint changes the pair (X, τ), the tool's configuration, as the τ radio buttons do (A-3's templates name the state of a game, and the paint buttons' names already depart from them, P6-A3). The option of a third `data-board` value ("decoration") was not taken: it would change the two values 4.0 names. This replaces, for the paint buttons, the first entry of decisions/RT-FIX-P6-t13.md ("data-board="numbers" and data-value "1" on a black (filled) node and "0" on a white (hollow) one"); its `data-board="populations"` on the restricted board, its `data-colour` and its `data-table-population` stand. Tests: the new regression test (T13.spec.ts, regressions); the selectors of T13.spec.ts, T13-keyboard.spec.ts and M9.spec.ts read `data-paint` and `data-control="paint"` where they read the decoration's `data-node`, with the same asserted values; T13.spec.ts "every node button carries data-node, data-board, data-value and data-can-act" now counts 6 + 2 node buttons (the game board and the restricted board, was 6 + 6 + 2) and checks the six paint controls separately (their hooks, data-can-act, and the absence of the three node hooks), and its 320-pixel check of the hit areas still covers the paint buttons. nojs.spec.ts compares the server and hydrated `[data-node]` hooks: the decoration leaves that list, and its state stays compared through the outputs `black-nodes`, `tau` and `arrows`. What a Challenge would read (Challenge.svelte readTool over every `[data-node]` of the tool, challengeCheck.ts valuesOf by `data-board`, sorted by label): on every T13 instance the `numbers` group is now empty, so a `reach`, `distinct` or `mixed-signs` check on `numbers` is never met; `populations` holds the game board alone while the Restricted board panel is closed, and while it is open (M9 b7 and b12 open on it by preset) the game board and the restricted board together, interleaved by label (on e6(−26): cities 1 to 6 of E6 and nodes 1 and 2 of A2, eight values, the two with label 1 first, then the two with label 2). There a `reach` with the six populations of E6 fails on the length, `distinct` counts vectors of eight values, and `mixed-signs` can be met by a negative shadow coordinate. No such Challenge exists today (M9's three Challenges on T13, b10 to b12, are of kind `out`); a group hook that Challenge could read (the lens's proposal in P6-RT-10-05) would be a change under site/src/components/lesson/ and stays open. What the specification left open: whether the decoration's buttons are node buttons in the sense of 4.0 Test hooks. Reason: SPEC 4.0 Test hooks, 6.3 last bullet, 7.5 A-1 and A-3; the MERGE follow-up as raised by rtconfirm-p6-t13.

Decision: the paint buttons of the decoration carry `data-board="numbers"` and `data-value` "1" on a black (filled) node and "0" on a white (hollow) one; the colour stays readable in `data-colour` ("black" or "white"), which the tests already read. ## 2026-10-26 RT-FIX-P6-t13: the records for display come from satakeRecord (P6-RT-02-01)
Decision: `assembleData` (t13/model.ts) takes the restricted board's name and the orbits in Bourbaki order of each entry from the record for display of the reader's own pair, `displayRecord(d, r)`: `satakeRecord` on the board's name with the matched record's catalogue fields (real form, Cartan's label, `restricted_type_display`) and the reader's black nodes and tau. `matchCatalogue` returns `satakeRecord`'s own output for each catalogue pair, so a matched record whose pair is the reader's is that record already and is used as it is; `satakeRecord` runs only for a pair that is the image of a catalogue pair under a symmetry of the board. The site no longer applies the C2 adjustment of SPEC 6.4 itself. Every value shown is unchanged (the unit test compares with `satakeRecord` on every catalogue pair and every symmetry image of rank at most 6, and the existing tests compare every field of every record with the golden file). This replaces two sentences of decisions/P6-A3.md: in "the C2 drawing rule", "the C2 adjustment is applied record by record (where the record displays C2 and satake says B2, the restricted board is named C2 and satake's orbits in Bourbaki order are reversed)"; and in "where the Satake data are computed", "`satakeRecord` is not called (the records come from `matchCatalogue`)": it is now called by `assembleData` for a symmetry image, on the main thread. The rule of which record decides the drawing (MERGE ruling (1) on P6-A3) is unchanged. Where it runs: the data path of t13/load.ts is unchanged (satake, restrictedBoard and matchCatalogue through engineCall; the unit test "where the computation runs" still asserts that it calls no `satakeRecord`). Among the 32 boards only D4, D6 and D8 have catalogue pairs that a symmetry moves (8, 1 and 1 such images, counted over every catalogue entry and every symmetry; every Satake diagram of the other boards is fixed by their symmetries, and E7 and E8 have none but the identity), so on E7 and E8 nothing runs on the main thread (E-9 item 3; a unit test checks that `displayRecord` returns the matched record itself on every admissible pair of E7 and E8). Measured in Node on this shared machine (warm, three runs each): the worst `satakeRecord` on such an image took 4.1 ms on D8 and 2.3 ms on D4 at a moderate load, and 28.8 ms on D8, 8.4 ms on D6 and 17.2 ms on D4 while a build ran beside it; it runs once when the data of such a pair arrive. What the specification left open: where in the site's data path `satakeRecord` is called. Reason: SPEC 6.4 "Names in rank 2", Appendix H Rules, 5.1 E-9.

## 2026-10-26 RT-FIX-P6-worker-wire: a named board travels by its name only when it is the standard board of it (P6-RT-03-02 P6-RT-06-02)
Decision: `specOf` (site/src/lib/workerWire.ts) gives a board's name only when the board is the standard board of that name position by position (its matrix and its labels equal those of `boardFromName(name)`); every other board, named or not, travels as `{ cartan }` in its own position order. The check is cached per name in the module (a twisted name takes up to 18 ms in `boardFromName`; boards are immutable, so the cache changes no result). A name `boardFromName` refuses also travels by the matrix. What the specification left open: CONTRACTS 4 sends "Board as its BoardSpec (rebuilt with resolveBoard)" and P1-A2 recorded "its name, or `{ cartan }`", but neither says which BoardSpec belongs to a named board that is not the standard board of its name; SPEC 6.6 makes a name denote the standard board, so the name is not that board's BoardSpec. Reason: the matrix in position order is what the other fields of a RestrictedBoard are written against (orbits, cartan, simpleRestrictedRoots2, compositeWords, and restrictedCoordinates' rule that a composite move at orbit k acts as mutate(rb.board, c, k)); a board rebuilt from its name had its positions permuted against all of them. 7 of the 135 restricted boards of the catalogue travel by the matrix now: su(2,2), sp(4,R), sp(2,2), so*(8), e6(2), e6(-14), e8(-24). The same rule holds for arguments sent to the worker (a folded board of T11 named after its type, MERGE phase 4).
What is lost, because BoardSpec carries no labels: such a board comes back with labels 1..n in position order, no name, and Big arithmetic (resolveBoard gives every unnamed board Big, E-2). For e8(-24) the main thread has F4 with labels 4, 3, 2, 1 in SafeInt; the worker path now gives the same matrix [[2,-1,0,0],[-1,2,-2,0],[0,-1,2,-1],[0,0,-1,2]] with labels 1, 2, 3, 4, no name, entries as bigint. No reader reaches it: T13 never reads rb.board (t13/model.ts) and makes no call for a pair without a white node.
Needs a decision of the owner (the reproducers of RT-03 and RT-06 stay red on these three fields): (a) carry a board's labels and name on the wire with its matrix, for example `{ "$board": { cartan }, "labels": [...], "name": "F4" }`, rebuilt with resolveBoard and then given its labels and name, with SafeInt when the name is a finite type; this changes CONTRACTS 4 ("Board as its BoardSpec"), and it also repairs P1-A2's noted loss of a sub-board's labels; (b) the engine builds a named restricted board (and a folded board) in the Bourbaki order of its name, or names it only when its positions are already in that order; this changes the engine's output and the plan reading of E-7 that P4-A1 and P6-A1 recorded, and the order of RestrictedBoard.board against its other fields; (c) keep the rule above and record in CONTRACTS 4 that a board that is not the standard board of its name crosses the wire as its matrix, without its labels and name. Recommendation: (a), since E-7 makes the labels part of a board and the same loss already reaches sub-boards and folded boards.

## 2026-10-26 RT-FIX-P6-worker-wire: a reply the main side cannot rebuild rejects the call; the empty board (P6-RT-03-02)
Decision: worker.ts's message handler rejects the call with the error that `deserialize` or `wireToError` throws (its own class, for instance NotABoard from resolveBoard) instead of letting it escape the handler with the promise pending. The restricted board of a compact form is the empty board (n 0, MERGE ruling (4) on P6-A1); its BoardSpec `{ cartan: [] }` is refused by resolveBoard (fromAdjacency: "an adjacency matrix needs at least one node"), so restrictedBoard of e7(-133) or e8(-248) routed to the worker now rejects with NotABoard, while the main thread answers the empty board. What the specification left open: CONTRACTS 4 has no rule for a board that resolveBoard refuses inside a result. Reason: CONTRACTS 4 ("errors re-thrown on the main side as the same class") and worker.ts's header ("a worker failure rejects the promise"); no text permits a promise that never settles.
Needs a decision of the owner (the RT-03 reproducer expects the call to resolve with the empty board): (a) a wire rule for the empty board, `{ "$board": { "cartan": [] } }` rebuilt as an empty board without resolveBoard; this changes CONTRACTS 4, and the engine exports no constructor of an empty board (one would be a CONTRACTS 2 change; building the object in the site puts a board outside the engine); (b) keep the rejection and record in CONTRACTS 4 that a board of 0 nodes does not cross the wire; T13 makes no call for a pair without a white node (P6-A3, `noWhiteNode`); (c) let resolveBoard accept a matrix of 0 nodes: not recommended, since a link with an empty board would then pass the validation of SPEC 6.6. Recommendation: (b) now, or (a) together with option (a) of the entry above if the owner changes the wire format.

The confirmed findings were fixed in nine branches (worker wire, Atlas, glossary and M10, M9, reference pages, T13, shared accessibility, LaTeX export, T12 and T5), each confirmed by a separate agent that reran the original reproducers and reverted each fix to see its test fail; the failure of gate G6's first run (T12.spec.ts:1242) was repaired in the product inside the T12 cluster, its test unchanged, as MERGE ruled at the G5 rerun.
